<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks>

- [snippet] Verify the signature: sha256=<lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 digest> — `sha256=<lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 digest>` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#verify-the-signature
- [snippet] Python: import hashlib — `import hashlib` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#verify-the-signature
- [snippet] TypeScript: import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto"; — `import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#verify-the-signature
- [snippet] Event envelope: { — `{` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#event-envelope
- [snippet] Handle event versions: if (event.type === "context_hub.commit.created.v1") { — `if (event.type === "context_hub.commit.created.v1") {` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#handle-event-versions
- [parameter] Method: `POST` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] URL: Publicly reachable HTTPS endpoint — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Content type: `application/json` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Signature: `X-LangSmith-Signature` header, signed with the webhook's signing secret — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Timeout: 20 seconds per attempt — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Attempts: Up to 4 attempts: 1 initial attempt and up to 3 retries — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Retry conditions: Transport failures, HTTP `408`, `425`, `429`, and `5xx` responses — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Permanent responses: Other `4xx` responses are not retried — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Response handling: A status below `400` succeeds. Response bodies do not affect success. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] `id`: Type=UUID; Description=Unique event identifier that remains stable across retries. Use it to deduplicate events. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#event-envelope
- [parameter] `type`: Type=string; Description=Exact event type. Currently `context_hub.commit.created.v1`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#event-envelope
- [parameter] `created`: Type=integer; Description=Unix seconds in UTC when the event was enqueued. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#event-envelope
- [parameter] `data`: Type=object; Description=Versioned event data. Contains `data.commit`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#event-envelope
- [parameter] `repo_id`: Type=UUID; Description=Context Hub repository ID. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommit
- [parameter] `repo_handle`: Type=string; Description=Repository handle. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommit
- [parameter] `repo_type`: Type=string; Description=Repository type: `agent` or `skill`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommit
- [parameter] `commit_hash`: Type=string; Description=Hash of the new commit. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommit
- [parameter] `parent_commit_hash`: Type=string; Description=Hash of the parent commit. Omitted for an initial commit or when unavailable. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommit
- [parameter] `created_at`: Type=string; Description=RFC 3339 timestamp when the commit was created. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommit
- [parameter] `created_by`: Type=string; Description=LangSmith user ID that created the commit. Omitted when unavailable. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommit
- [parameter] `url`: Type=string; Description=Deep link to the commit in the LangSmith UI. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommit
- [parameter] `files_changed`: Type=array; Description=File changes included in the commit. Each entry contains `path` and `action`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommit
- [parameter] `path`: Type=string; Description=Path changed by the commit. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommitfiles-changed
- [parameter] `action`: Type=string; Description=Change type: `added`, `modified`, or `removed`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommitfiles-changed
- [definition] Configure Context Hub commit webhooks — [Context Hub](/langsmith/context-hub) commit webhooks notify external services whenever an agent or skill commit is created in your [workspace](/langsmith/administration-overview#workspaces). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#configure-context-hub-commit-webhooks
- [definition] Add a webhook — Each webhook applies to the entire workspace. Every configured endpoint receives every agent and skill commit, including commits created by Fleet. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#add-a-webhook
- [definition] Manage a webhook — The webhook list displays endpoint URLs and custom header names. Header values and signing secrets remain hidden until you click **Reveal secrets**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#manage-a-webhook
- [definition] Delivery — LangSmith sends a JSON `POST` request for each event. Custom headers cannot override `Content-Type` or `X-LangSmith-Signature`, which LangSmith sets after applying custom headers. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#delivery
- [definition] Verify the signature — Each request includes an `X-LangSmith-Signature` header in this format: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#verify-the-signature
- [definition] Event envelope — The outer `id`, `type`, `created`, and `data` envelope is frozen. The `.v1` suffix on the event type versions the `data.commit` schema. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#event-envelope
- [definition] `data.commit` — The `data.commit` object describes the Context Hub commit that triggered the event. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommit
- [definition] `data.commit.files_changed` — Each entry summarizes a changed path. It does not contain the file contents. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#datacommitfiles-changed
- [definition] Handle event versions — Branch on the complete event type before parsing `data.commit`: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/context-hub-webhooks#handle-event-versions

## LangSmith control plane
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/control-plane>

- [definition] LangSmith control plane — The _control plane_ is the part of LangSmith that manages deployments. It includes the control plane UI, where users create and update [Agent Servers](/langsmith/agent-server), and the control plane APIs, which support the UI and provide programmatic access. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/control-plane#langsmith-control-plane
- [definition] Control plane API — This section describes the data model of the control plane API. The API is used to create, update, and delete deployments. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/control-plane#control-plane-api
- [definition] Integrations — An integration is an abstraction for a `git` repository provider (e.g. GitHub). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/control-plane#integrations
- [definition] Deployments — A deployment is an instance of an Agent Server. A single deployment can have many revisions. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/control-plane#deployments
- [definition] Revisions — A revision is an iteration of a deployment. When a new deployment is created, an initial revision is automatically created. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/control-plane#revisions
- [definition] Listeners — A listener is an instance of a ["listener" application](/langsmith/data-plane#listener-application). A listener contains metadata about the application (e.g. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/control-plane#listeners
- [definition] Control plane features — This section describes various features of the control plane. For platform-specific behavior such as Cloud deployment types or self-hosted resource customization, see [Cloud platform features](/langsmith/cloud-platform-features) or [Deploy to self-hosted](/langsmith/deploy-to-self-hosted-overview). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/control-plane#control-plane-features
- [definition] Asynchronous deployment — Infrastructure for deployments and revisions are provisioned and deployed asynchronously. They are not deployed immediately after submission. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/control-plane#asynchronous-deployment
- [definition] Monitoring — After a deployment is ready, the control plane monitors the deployment and records various metrics, such as: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/control-plane#monitoring
- [definition] LangSmith integration — A [LangSmith](/langsmith/observability) tracing project is automatically created for each deployment. The tracing project has the same name as the deployment. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/control-plane#langsmith-integration

## Core capabilities overview
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/core-capabilities>

- [definition] Core capabilities overview — Building on the [Agent Server](/langsmith/agent-server) runtime, these capabilities cover how runs stream, pause, expose endpoints, and react to events: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/core-capabilities#core-capabilities-overview
- [definition] Durable execution — At its core, LangSmith Deployment is a durable execution engine. Your agents run on a managed task queue with automatic checkpointing, so any run can be retried, replayed, or resumed from the exact point of interruption, not from scratch. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/core-capabilities#durable-execution

- [parameter] `aput_writes`: Store pending writes — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-checkpointer#base-capabilities-required

- [parameter] `adelete_for_runs`: Description=Delete checkpoints for specific runs; Fallback if missing=Rollback multitask strategy unavailable — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-checkpointer#extended-capabilities-optional
- [parameter] `acopy_thread`: Description=Copy a thread; Fallback if missing=Slow fallback (re-inserts checkpoints one by one) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-checkpointer#extended-capabilities-optional
- [parameter] `aprune`: Description=Prune thread history; Fallback if missing=Thread history pruning unavailable — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-checkpointer#extended-capabilities-optional

- [definition] Define the checkpointer — Starting from an **existing** LangSmith application, create a file that defines an async context manager yielding your custom checkpointer. - [definition] Test against the conformance suite — Most open source checkpointer implementations do not yet implement all the operations required by Agent Server. - [definition] Configure `langgraph.json` — Add the `checkpointer` key to your [`langgraph.json` configuration file](/langsmith/application-structure#configuration-file-concepts). The `path` points to the async context manager you [defined earlier](#define-the-checkpointer). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-checkpointer#configure-langgraphjson
- [definition] Capabilities — The server checks your checkpointer for **base** (required) and **extended** (optional) capabilities at startup. If an extended capability is missing, the server either uses a fallback or disables the corresponding feature. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-checkpointer#capabilities
- [definition] Deploying — You can deploy this app as-is to LangSmith or to your self-hosted platform. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/custom-checkpointer#deploying

## Monitor projects with dashboards
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards>

- [parameter] Traces: Trace count, latency and error rates. A [trace](/langsmith/observability-concepts#traces) is a collection of [runs](/langsmith/observability-concepts#runs) related to a single operation. For example, if a user request triggers an agent, all runs for that agent invocation would be part of the same trace. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#dashboard-sections
- [parameter] LLM Calls: LLM call count and latency. Includes all runs where run type is "llm". — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#dashboard-sections
- [parameter] Cost & Tokens: Total and per-trace token counts and costs, broken down by token type. Costs are measured using [LangSmith's cost tracking](/langsmith/log-llm-trace#provide-token-and-cost-information). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#dashboard-sections
- [parameter] Tools: Run counts, error rates, and latency stats for tool runs broken down by tool name. Includes runs where run type is "tool". Limits to top 5 most frequently occurring tools. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#dashboard-sections
- [parameter] Run Types: Run counts, error rates, and latency stats for runs that are immediate children of the root run. This helps in understanding the high-level execution path of agents. Limits to top 5 most frequently occurring run names. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#dashboard-sections
- [parameter] Feedback Scores: Aggregate stats for the top 5 most frequently occurring types of feedback. Charts show average score for numerical feedback and category counts for categorical feedback. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#dashboard-sections
- [parameter] Count: Description=Number of runs.; Aggregations=— — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#pick-a-metric
- [parameter] Latency: Description=Aggregates over `latency_seconds`.; Aggregations=Average, Percentile (p50 or p99) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#pick-a-metric
- [parameter] Time to first token: Description=Aggregates over `first_token_seconds`.; Aggregations=Percentile (p50 or p99), Average — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#pick-a-metric
- [parameter] Tokens: Description=Choose Total, Input, or Output tokens.; Aggregations=Sum, Average, Percentile — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#pick-a-metric
- [parameter] Cost: Description=Choose Total, Input, or Output cost.; Aggregations=Sum, Average, Percentile — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#pick-a-metric
- [parameter] Feedback score: Description=Select a feedback key.; Aggregations=Average, Minimum, Maximum — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#pick-a-metric
- [parameter] Ratio: Description=Define a numerator and denominator, each a metric with its own filter. Useful for error rate, LLM run share, etc.; Aggregations=— — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#pick-a-metric
- [definition] Monitor projects with dashboards — Dashboards give you high-level insights into your [trace](/langsmith/observability-concepts#traces) data, helping you spot trends and monitor the health of your applications. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#monitor-projects-with-dashboards
- [definition] Prebuilt dashboards — Prebuilt dashboards are created automatically for each project and cover essential metrics, such as trace count, error rates, token usage, and more. By default, you can access the prebuilt dashboard for your tracing project using the **Dashboard** button on the top right of the tracing project page. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#prebuilt-dashboards
- [definition] Dashboard sections — Prebuilt dashboards are broken down into the following sections: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#dashboard-sections
- [definition] Group by — You can use group by [run tag or metadata](/langsmith/add-metadata-tags) to split data over attributes that are important to your application. The global group by setting appears on the top right-hand side of the dashboard. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#group-by
- [definition] Create a new dashboard — 1. Navigate to the **Monitoring** tab in the left sidebar. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#create-a-new-dashboard
- [definition] Add charts to your dashboard — 1. Within a dashboard, click the **+ New Chart** button to open the chart creation pane. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#add-charts-to-your-dashboard
- [definition] Create a new dashboard — 1. Navigate to the **Monitor** tab in the left sidebar. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/dashboards#create-a-new-dashboard

- [parameter] Access denied: The blob store credentials or bucket are not valid. - [parameter] Bucket is not valid: The specified blob store bucket is not valid. This error is thrown when the bucket doesn't exist or there is not enough access to perform writes on the bucket. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-destinations#common-errors

- [parameter] InvalidBucketName: The S3-compatible service rejected the request due to addressing style mismatch. Some services require virtual-hosted style addressing. - [definition] S3-compatible bucket with virtual-hosted style addressing — Some S3-compatible services (such as Volcengine TOS) require virtual-hosted style addressing, where the bucket name is part of the hostname rather than the URL path. Use `config_kwargs_s3` with `addressing_style: "virtual"` to enable this: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-destinations#s3-compatible-bucket-with-virtual-hosted-style-addressing
- [definition] S3-compatible bucket with virtual-hosted style endpoint — If your endpoint URL already includes the bucket name (virtual-hosted style), set `include_bucket_in_prefix` to `false` to avoid duplicating the bucket name in the path: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-destinations#s3-compatible-bucket-with-virtual-hosted-style-endpoint
- [definition] Rotate destination credentials — Use `PATCH /api/v1/bulk-exports/destinations/{destination_id}` to update the credentials on an existing destination. This lets you rotate or replace credentials without recreating the destination or its associated bulk exports. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-destinations#rotate-destination-credentials
- [definition] Response — Returns the updated destination object. Credential values are never returned—only the credential field names are included in the response under `credentials_keys`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-destinations#response
- [definition] Rotation checklist — 1. Provision new credentials in your cloud provider with write access to the destination bucket and prefix. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-destinations#rotation-checklist
- [definition] Authenticate with an AWS IAM role — AWS IAM role assumption lets GCP-hosted LangSmith SaaS export to S3 without storing static AWS credentials. Configure an AWS role that trusts the LangSmith service accounts for your production region, then provide its ARN when you create or update a destination. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-destinations#authenticate-with-an-aws-iam-role
- [definition] Create the AWS role — Create an AWS IAM role with a trust policy that permits web identity federation from the three subject IDs for your region. Grant the role access to your export bucket. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-destinations#create-the-aws-role
- [definition] Switch authentication mode — Switch an existing destination between static credentials and [AWS IAM role assumption](#authenticate-with-an-aws-iam-role) without recreating it. Use `PATCH /api/v1/bulk-exports/destinations/{destination_id}`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-destinations#switch-authentication-mode
- [definition] Switch from static credentials to AWS IAM role — Provide `aws_role_arn` in the PATCH body. This clears any previously stored credentials. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-destinations#switch-from-static-credentials-to-aws-iam-role

- [parameter] **Infrastructure interruption**: Cause=[Deployments](/langsmith/deployment), server restarts, worker crashes; Automatic retry?=Yes, automatically requeued with remaining retries.; Action required=None, jobs resume automatically. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-monitor#failure-scenarios
- [parameter] **Run timeout**: Cause=Single run exceeds 4-hour limit; Automatic retry?=Yes, retried up to 20 times (subject to change).; Action required=If persistent, narrow date range, add filters, or [limit the exported fields](/langsmith/data-export#limit-exported-fields). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-monitor#failure-scenarios
- [parameter] **Workflow timeout**: Cause=Entire export exceeds 72 hours; Automatic retry?=No; Action required=Reduce export scope (date range, filters) or break into smaller exports. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-monitor#failure-scenarios
- [parameter] **Storage/destination errors**: Cause=[Invalid credentials](/langsmith/data-export-destinations#credentials-configuration), [missing bucket](/langsmith/data-export-destinations#configuration-fields), [permission issues](/langsmith/data-export-destinations#permissions-required); Automatic retry?=No; Action required=Fix destination configuration and create new export. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-monitor#failure-scenarios
- [parameter] **Destination deleted**: Cause=Bucket removed during export; Automatic retry?=No; Action required=Recreate destination and restart export. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-monitor#failure-scenarios
- [parameter] **Terminal processing errors**: Cause=Data serialization issues, resource exhaustion; Automatic retry?=Yes, retried up to 20 times (subject to change).; Action required=Check run error details; may require investigation. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-monitor#failure-scenarios

- [parameter] `COMPLETED`: All runs successfully exported. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-monitor#export-status-lifecycle
- [parameter] `FAILED`: One or more runs failed after exhausting retries. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-monitor#export-status-lifecycle

- [definition] List runs for an export — An export is typically broken up into multiple runs which correspond to a specific date partition to export. - [definition] Progress tracking and resumability — The export system maintains detailed progress metadata for each run: - Latest cursor position in the data stream. - Number of rows exported. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export-monitor#progress-tracking-and-resumability

## LangSmith data plane
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane>

- [parameter] Required<br />Trace to LangSmith SaaS.: Hybrid=Optional<br />Disable tracing or trace to LangSmith SaaS.; Self-Hosted=Optional<br />Disable tracing, trace to LangSmith SaaS, or trace to Self-Hosted LangSmith. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#langsmith-tracing
- [parameter] Telemetry sent to LangSmith SaaS.: Hybrid=Telemetry sent to LangSmith SaaS.; Self-Hosted=Self-reported usage (audit) for air-gapped license key.<br />Telemetry sent to LangSmith SaaS for LangSmith License Key. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#telemetry
- [parameter] LangSmith API Key validated against LangSmith SaaS.: Hybrid=LangSmith API Key validated against LangSmith SaaS.; Self-Hosted=Air-gapped license key or Platform License Key validated against LangSmith SaaS. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#licensing
- [definition] LangSmith data plane — The _data plane_ consists of your [Agent Servers](/langsmith/agent-server) (deployments), their supporting infrastructure, and the "listener" application that continuously polls for updates from the [LangSmith control plane](/langsmith/control-plane). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#langsmith-data-plane
- [definition] Server infrastructure — In addition to the [Agent Server](/langsmith/agent-server) itself, the following infrastructure components for each server are also included in the broad definition of "data plane": — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#server-infrastructure
- [definition] "Listener" application — The data plane "listener" application periodically calls [control plane APIs](/langsmith/control-plane#control-plane-api) to: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#listener-application
- [definition] PostgreSQL — PostgreSQL stores server resources (threads, runs, assistants, crons) and items saved in the [long-term memory store](/oss/python/langgraph/persistence#memory-store). It is also the default backend for [checkpoints](/oss/python/langgraph/persistence) (graph execution state). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#postgresql
- [definition] Redis — Redis is used in each Agent Server as a way for server and queue workers to communicate, and to store ephemeral metadata. No user or run data is stored in Redis. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#redis
- [definition] Communication — All runs in an Agent Server are executed by a pool of background workers that are part of each deployment. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#communication
- [definition] Ephemeral metadata — Runs in an Agent Server may be retried for specific failures (currently only for transient PostgreSQL errors encountered during the run). In order to limit the number of retries (currently limited to 3 attempts per run) we record the attempt number in a Redis string when it is picked up. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#ephemeral-metadata
- [definition] Data plane features — This section describes various features of the data plane. For platform-specific behavior, see [Cloud platform features](/langsmith/cloud-platform-features) or [Deploy to self-hosted](/langsmith/deploy-to-self-hosted-overview). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#data-plane-features
- [definition] Autoscaling — [Dedicated type](/langsmith/cloud-platform-features#deployment-types) deployments automatically scale across containers. Scaling is based on 3 metrics: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#autoscaling
- [definition] MongoDB checkpointing — Available for [Cloud](/langsmith/cloud) (with an externally managed MongoDB instance) and [Standalone](/langsmith/deploy-standalone-server) deployments. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#mongodb-checkpointing
- [definition] LangSmith tracing — Agent Server is automatically configured to send traces to LangSmith. See the table below for details with respect to each deployment option. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#langsmith-tracing
- [definition] Telemetry — Agent Server is automatically configured to report telemetry metadata for billing purposes. See the table below for details with respect to each deployment option. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#telemetry
- [definition] Licensing — Agent Server is automatically configured to perform license key validation. See the table below for details with respect to each deployment option. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-plane#licensing

- [definition] Agent Server — The [Agent Server](/langsmith/agent-server) provides a durable execution runtime that relies on persisting checkpoints of your application state, long-term memories, thread metadata, assistants, and similar resources to the local file system or a database. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-storage-and-privacy#agent-server
- [definition] LangSmith tracing — When running the Agent server (either in-memory or in Docker), LangSmith tracing may be enabled to facilitate faster debugging and offer observability of graph state and LLM prompts in production. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-storage-and-privacy#langsmith-tracing
- [definition] In-memory development server — `langgraph dev` runs an [in-memory development server](/langsmith/local-dev-testing) as a single Python process, designed for quick development and testing. It saves all checkpointing and memory data to disk within a `.langgraph_api` directory in the current working directory. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-storage-and-privacy#in-memory-development-server
- [definition] Standalone Server — `langgraph up` builds your local package into a Docker image and runs the server as the [data plane](/langsmith/self-hosted) consisting of three containers: the API server, a PostgreSQL container, and a Redis container. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-storage-and-privacy#standalone-server
- [definition] Studio — [Studio](/langsmith/studio) is a graphical interface for interacting with your Agent Server. It does not persist any private data (the data you send to your server is not sent to LangSmith). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-storage-and-privacy#studio
- [definition] Quick reference — In summary, you can opt-out of server-side telemetry by turning off CLI analytics and disabling tracing. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-storage-and-privacy#quick-reference

Follow these steps systematically to identify and resolve common deployment issues. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#troubleshooting-for-self-hosted-deployments
- [definition] Prerequisites — Before beginning the diagnostic steps, ensure you have: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#prerequisites
- [definition] Step 1. Understand your deployment — Verify what was deployed and understand the baseline state of your system. This helps you recognize what normal operation looks like and identify deviations when issues occur. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#step-1-understand-your-deployment
- [definition] Key deployed components — Your deployment includes the following core components: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#key-deployed-components
- [definition] Step 2. Enable debug logging — When troubleshooting issues, the first step is typically to enable debug-level logging to gather more detailed information about what's happening in your system. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#step-2-enable-debug-logging
- [definition] For control plane or data plane deployments — If you are experiencing issues with a control plane deployment (for example, `langsmith-host-backend`) or a data plane deployment (for example, `langsmith-listener`), reinstall the Helm chart with the `LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` environment variable. Add the following to your `values.yaml` file: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#for-control-plane-or-data-plane-deployments
- [definition] For Agent Server deployments — If the issue is with an individual Agent Server deployment: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#for-agent-server-deployments
- [definition] For widespread issues — If you are unsure where the issue originates, enable `DEBUG` logging everywhere (control plane, data plane, and all Agent Server deployments). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#for-widespread-issues
- [definition] Review application logs — Tail the logs of each pod to understand baseline behavior: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#review-application-logs
- [definition] Interpret debug logs — Look for the following problem indicators: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#interpret-debug-logs
- [definition] Step 3. Describe deployments and pods — Describing Kubernetes resources reveals error events and statuses that may not appear in application logs. These errors are typically caused by configuration or infrastructure issues rather than application code bugs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#step-3-describe-deployments-and-pods
- [definition] Interpret results — Review the `Events:` section of the output and verify that everything is normal. Common issues that appear include: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#interpret-results
- [definition] Additional resources — For more troubleshooting information, refer to: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#additional-resources
- [definition] Support — If you have followed these diagnostic steps and still need assistance, gather the following information before contacting support: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/diagnostics-self-hosted#support

## Double texting
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/double-texting>

- [definition] Enqueue (default) — This option allows the current run to finish before processing any new input. Incoming requests are queued and executed sequentially once prior runs complete. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/double-texting#enqueue-default
- [definition] Reject — This option rejects any additional incoming runs while a current run is in progress and prevents concurrent execution or double texting. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/double-texting#reject
- [definition] Interrupt — This option halts the current execution and preserves the progress made up to the interruption point. The new user input is then inserted, and execution continues from that state. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/double-texting#interrupt
- [definition] Rollback — This option halts the current execution and reverts all progress—including the initial run input—before processing the new user input. The new input is treated as a fresh run, starting from the initial state. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/double-texting#rollback

- [definition] Basic encryption — For simple encryption with a single static key, set the `LANGGRAPH_AES_KEY` environment variable. LangGraph will automatically encrypt checkpoint blobs using AES. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/encryption#basic-encryption
- [definition] Encrypting JSON fields — To also encrypt specific JSON fields, set `LANGGRAPH_AES_JSON_KEYS` to a comma-separated list of keys to encrypt: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/encryption#encrypting-json-fields

- [definition] Configuration — Add your encryption module to `langgraph.json`: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/encryption#configuration
- [definition] Passing encryption context — Pass encryption context via the `X-Encryption-Context` header. The context is arbitrary data that you define—you control the schema and can include any fields your encryption logic needs (e.g., `tenant_id`, `key_version`). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/encryption#passing-encryption-context
- [definition] Envelope encryption with AWS Encryption SDK — For production deployments on AWS, use the [AWS Encryption SDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/python.html) with AWS KMS, or an equivalent within your cloud provider. ## API and SDK deprecation policy
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/endpoint-deprecation>

- [parameter] Cloud: 6 months from announcement to removal — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/endpoint-deprecation#deprecation-window-by-deployment
- [parameter] Self-hosted: At least one major release — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/endpoint-deprecation#deprecation-window-by-deployment
- [definition] API and SDK deprecation policy — LangSmith deprecates API endpoints and SDK methods before removing them, so you have time to migrate to a replacement. This page describes how deprecations are announced and how long they stay supported. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/endpoint-deprecation#api-and-sdk-deprecation-policy
- [definition] Deprecation lifecycle — Every deprecation follows the same stages: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/endpoint-deprecation#deprecation-lifecycle
- [definition] SDK method deprecation — Most SDK methods are thin wrappers around an API endpoint, so a method deprecates on the same timeline as the endpoint it calls, and is removed from the SDK when the endpoint is removed. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/endpoint-deprecation#sdk-method-deprecation
- [definition] Field-level deprecation — A deprecated field is removed at a version boundary, not on a date: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/endpoint-deprecation#field-level-deprecation

## LangSmith Engine issue categories
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories>

- [definition] LangSmith Engine issue categories — When [LangSmith Engine](/langsmith/engine) detects a recurring issue in your traces, it tags the issue with a category. This page lists every category Engine assigns, with a description and concrete example for each. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#langsmith-engine-issue-categories
- [definition] Agent looping — The agent repeats the same action multiple times within a single trace without making progress toward the user's goal. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#agent-looping
- [definition] Context explosion — The trace consumed an extremely large number of tokens due to unbounded context accumulation, not from looping. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#context-explosion
- [definition] Failed error recovery — A tool returned an explicit error, and the agent retried the same call with identical or near-identical arguments repeatedly instead of adapting its approach. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#failed-error-recovery
- [definition] Feature gap — The user asks for a legitimate in-scope capability that does not exist yet. This is an unmet product need, not an agent execution mistake. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#feature-gap
- [definition] Flawed plan — The agent's approach shows a fundamental misunderstanding of the task. The answer addresses a different question than asked, or the plan was wrong from the first tool call. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#flawed-plan
- [definition] Guardrail bypass — A user manipulated the agent into generating content outside its intended scope through multi-turn steering or prompt injection. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#guardrail-bypass
- [definition] Hallucination — The agent's response contains specific facts, numbers, or names that are not present in any tool output. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#hallucination
- [definition] Incorrect tool args — The agent picked the right tool but called it with arguments that do not match the user's intent or the tool's schema. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#incorrect-tool-args
- [definition] Missing capability awareness — The agent tried to use a tool it does not have, refused a task it was equipped to handle, or hit a case the prompt never prepared it for. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#missing-capability-awareness
- [definition] PII leak — The agent's response contains sensitive data such as Social Security numbers, dates of birth, home addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, or API keys. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#pii-leak
- [definition] Response truncation — The agent's response was cut off mid-sentence or mid-code-block. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#response-truncation
- [definition] Silent tool error — A tool returned an error message as its content instead of raising an exception, so the agent treated the error as a valid response. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#silent-tool-error
- [definition] System prompt drift — The agent answered an off-topic question outside the application's purpose instead of declining. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#system-prompt-drift
- [definition] Task evasion — The agent declared success before the work was complete, simplified the task to avoid a difficult part, or gave up after a single failure without trying alternative approaches. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#task-evasion
- [definition] Tracing quality — The project's traces are missing metadata, tags, or structural markers that unlock LangSmith features. This is not a behavioral issue with the agent but an instrumentation gap. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#tracing-quality
- [definition] Wrong tool — A better-fit tool existed but the agent chose the wrong one for the user's request. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories#wrong-tool

## LangSmith Engine
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-overview>

- [definition] LangSmith Engine — LangSmith Engine is the LangSmith Agent for agent engineering. It works from your production traces to surface recurring issues, diagnose their root cause, and drive the fix across every stage of the development lifecycle. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-overview#langsmith-engine
- [definition] Engine across the lifecycle — For each issue, Engine surfaces the contributing traces, proposes a fix, keeps the issue current by attaching new traces that match the same failure pattern, and creates ground truth dataset examples from the production trace inputs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-overview#engine-across-the-lifecycle
- [definition] How Engine runs — Engine scans each connected tracing project on a dynamic schedule tuned to balance cost and performance, clustering and prioritizing issues by severity. It uses LangChain-managed inference and charges in LangChain Compute Units (LCUs). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-overview#how-engine-runs

## LangSmith Engine security
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security>

- [parameter] LangSmith workspace content: **What Engine reads**=Trace data and other workspace content you have stored in LangSmith, such as prompts and evaluators.; **Storage and persistence**=Within your LangSmith tenant. [Trace retention](/langsmith/usage-and-billing#data-retention) is 14 days (base) or 400 days (extended), chosen per project. The durations are not configurable.; **Enables**=Issue… — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security#what-data-engine-uses
- [parameter] GitHub repository: **What Engine reads**=Source code and repository context from the repositories you connect (see [GitHub integration](#github-integration)).; **Storage and persistence**=Processed inside an isolated, LangChain-managed sandbox for the duration of each analysis run, then discarded.; **Enables**=Pull request authoring with proposed code fixes. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security#what-data-engine-uses
- [parameter] Model provider (inference): **What Engine reads**=Only the content required for each analysis task.; **Storage and persistence**=Zero data retention with every Engine model provider (see [Model subprocessors](#model-subprocessors)).; **Enables**=Engine reasoning and generation. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security#what-data-engine-uses
- [definition] LangSmith Engine security — LangSmith Engine is an AI agent built into LangSmith that improves the agents you build. Engine reviews the trace data already in LangSmith, surfaces and prioritizes issues, and opens pull requests with suggested fixes, proposed prompt changes, and evaluations. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security#langsmith-engine-security
- [definition] What data Engine uses — Engine operates on data you have already chosen to share with LangChain: the trace data you send to LangSmith and, separately, the GitHub repository content you grant through the LangChain-managed GitHub App (see [GitHub integration](#github-integration)). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security#what-data-engine-uses
- [definition] GitHub integration — Engine connects to your source code through a LangChain-managed GitHub App. Only GitHub.com is supported. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security#github-integration
- [definition] Model subprocessors — Engine's model subprocessors (currently OpenAI, Anthropic, Fireworks, and Baseten) all operate under zero data retention and are contractually prohibited from using customer data to train or fine-tune their models. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security#model-subprocessors
- [definition] Key security controls — Engine adds the following controls on top of LangSmith's baseline: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security#key-security-controls
- [definition] Compliance posture — Engine operates under LangSmith's control environment, which is audited annually under SOC 2 Type II and certified to ISO 27001. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security#compliance-posture
- [definition] Inherent AI risks and mitigations — The following risks are inherent to AI-assisted code generation. LangChain mitigates each in product, and your code-review workflow provides a second layer of defense. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security#inherent-ai-risks-and-mitigations
- [definition] Contact — For security questions, contact [trust@langchain.dev](mailto:trust@langchain.dev). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security#contact

## LangSmith Engine webhook events
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks>

- [snippet] Signing secret: sha256=<hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 digest> — `sha256=<hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 digest>` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#signing-secret
- [snippet] Python: import hashlib — `import hashlib` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#signing-secret
- [snippet] TypeScript: import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto"; — `import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#signing-secret
- [snippet] `issue.created`: { — `{` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issuecreated
- [snippet] `issue.trace.added`: { — `{` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issuetraceadded
- [snippet] `issue.agent_run.failed`: { — `{` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issueagent-runfailed
- [snippet] Test your endpoint: curl -X POST https://your-endpoint.example.com/webhook \ — `curl -X POST https://your-endpoint.example.com/webhook \` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#test-your-endpoint
- [parameter] Method: `POST` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Body: JSON, [common envelope](#event-envelope) below — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Scheme: `http://` and `https://` are accepted. `https://` is strongly recommended — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Signature: `X-LangSmith-Signature` header, signed with the subscription's signing secret — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Timeout: 20 seconds per attempt — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Attempts: Up to 4 attempts (1 initial plus 3 retries with exponential backoff) on transport errors, HTTP `408`, `425`, `429`, and any HTTP `5xx`. Other `4xx` responses are treated as permanent and are not retried — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] Response: Success is determined from the status code alone. Response bodies are ignored. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#delivery
- [parameter] `0`: Urgent — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#severity-filtering
- [parameter] `1`: High — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#severity-filtering
- [parameter] `2`: Medium — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#severity-filtering
- [parameter] `3`: Low — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#severity-filtering
- [parameter] `id`: Type=UUID; Description=Unique identifier for this delivery. Stable across retries. Use it to dedupe. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#event-envelope
- [parameter] `type`: Type=string; Description=Event type. One of [`issue.created`](#issue-created), [`issue.trace.added`](#issue-trace-added), or [`issue.agent_run.failed`](#issue-agent_run-failed). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#event-envelope
- [parameter] `created`: Type=integer; Description=Unix seconds (UTC) when the event was enqueued. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#event-envelope
- [parameter] `request_id`: Type=UUID; Description=Shared by every event fired from the same upstream action. See [Batch coalescing](#batch-coalescing). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#event-envelope
- [parameter] `data`: Type=object; Description=Event payload. Always contains `data.object`. Contains [`data.trace`](#data-trace) only on [`issue.trace.added`](#issue-trace-added) events. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#event-envelope
- [parameter] `id`: Type=UUID; Description=Issue ID. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issue-dataobject
- [parameter] `name`: Type=string; Description=Short title of the issue. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issue-dataobject
- [parameter] `description`: Type=string; Description=Human-readable description. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issue-dataobject
- [parameter] `severity`: Type=integer; Description=`0` (urgent) through `3` (low). See [Severity filtering](#severity-filtering). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issue-dataobject
- [parameter] `tenant_id`: Type=UUID; Description=Workspace the issue belongs to. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issue-dataobject
- [parameter] `tenant_name`: Type=string; Description=Workspace display name. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issue-dataobject
- [parameter] `session_id`: Type=UUID; Description=Tracing project the issue belongs to. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issue-dataobject
- [parameter] `session_name`: Type=string; Description=Tracing project name. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issue-dataobject
- [parameter] `url`: Type=string; Description=Deep link to the issue in the LangSmith UI. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issue-dataobject
- [parameter] `tenant_id`: Type=UUID; Description=Workspace the run belongs to. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#run-failure-dataobject
- [parameter] `tenant_name`: Type=string; Description=Workspace display name. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#run-failure-dataobject
- [parameter] `session_id`: Type=UUID; Description=Tracing project the run belongs to. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#run-failure-dataobject
- [parameter] `session_name`: Type=string; Description=Tracing project name. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#run-failure-dataobject
- [parameter] `url`: Type=string; Description=Deep link to the LangSmith project in the UI. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#run-failure-dataobject
- [parameter] `thread_id`: Type=string; Description=Engine thread ID. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#run-failure-dataobject
- [parameter] `run_id`: Type=string; Description=Engine run ID. Omitted when unavailable. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#run-failure-dataobject
- [parameter] `status`: Type=string; Description=Final run status. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#run-failure-dataobject
- [parameter] `error_message`: Type=string; Description=Error text from the failed run. Omitted when unavailable. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#run-failure-dataobject
- [parameter] `occurred_at`: Type=string; Description=RFC 3339 timestamp of when the failure occurred. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#run-failure-dataobject
- [parameter] `run_id`: Type=UUID; Description=ID of the run that was linked to the issue. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#datatrace
- [parameter] `trace_id`: Type=UUID; Description=ID of the trace that contains the run. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#datatrace
- [parameter] `start_time`: Type=string; Description=RFC 3339 timestamp of when the run started. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#datatrace
- [parameter] `comment`: Type=string \| null; Description=Optional note recorded when the trace was linked. Omitted when empty. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#datatrace
- [definition] LangSmith Engine webhook events — Forward LangSmith-detected agent issues into your incident-management, paging, or chat tools. [LangSmith Engine](/langsmith/engine) sends a webhook event to your endpoint when it opens a new issue, or when it links a new trace to an issue it has already opened. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#langsmith-engine-webhook-events
- [definition] Delivery — LangSmith sends a `POST` request with a JSON body to your webhook URL. The request uses `Content-Type: application/json` and includes any custom headers you attached to the subscription. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#delivery
- [definition] Custom headers — You can attach arbitrary headers to each subscription (for example, `Authorization: Bearer …`) to authenticate the caller at your endpoint. `Content-Type` is always set by LangSmith and cannot be overridden. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#custom-headers
- [definition] Signing secret — Each subscription has a signing secret. LangSmith uses this secret to sign the raw webhook request body and sends the result in the `X-LangSmith-Signature` header. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#signing-secret
- [definition] Roll a signing secret — Roll a signing secret when it may have been exposed, or when your organization's credential rotation policy requires a new secret. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#roll-a-signing-secret
- [definition] Severity filtering — Each subscription has a `severity_threshold` from `0` to `3`. For issue events, an event is delivered only when the issue's `severity` is less than or equal to the threshold. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#severity-filtering
- [definition] Event-type filtering — Each subscription specifies the [event types](#event-types) it wants to receive. Subscriptions created without an explicit list default to `["issue.created"]`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#event-type-filtering
- [definition] Event envelope — Every event delivered to your endpoint uses the same outer JSON shape. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#event-envelope
- [definition] Issue `data.object` — For [`issue.created`](#issue-created) and [`issue.trace.added`](#issue-trace-added), `data.object` is a snapshot of the issue. Treat it as the authoritative state of the issue at the time the event was generated. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issue-dataobject
- [definition] Run failure `data.object` — For [`issue.agent_run.failed`](#issue-agent_run-failed), `data.object` describes the Engine run that failed. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#run-failure-dataobject
- [definition] `data.trace` — `data.trace` is included only on [`issue.trace.added`](#issue-trace-added) events. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#datatrace
- [definition] Batch coalescing — A single upstream action can produce multiple webhook events. When Engine opens a new issue and attaches five traces to it, you receive one [`issue.created`](#issue-created) event and five [`issue.trace.added`](#issue-trace-added) events, all sharing the same `request_id`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#batch-coalescing
- [definition] Event types — The event types below are the complete set LangSmith Engine sends today. New types may be added in the future, so handlers should ignore unknown `type` values rather than failing. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#event-types
- [definition] `issue.created` — Sent when LangSmith Engine creates a new issue. `data.trace` is omitted. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issuecreated
- [definition] `issue.trace.added` — Sent when a new trace is linked to an existing issue. `data.trace` describes the linked trace. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issuetraceadded
- [definition] `issue.agent_run.failed` — Sent when LangSmith Engine fails to complete a run. This event is session-scoped, so it does not include `data.trace` and does not use severity filtering. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#issueagent-runfailed
- [definition] Test your endpoint — Before pointing a real subscription at your endpoint, send a sample payload to verify it accepts and acknowledges within the 20-second timeout: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks#test-your-endpoint

## Cloud Agent Server environment variables
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud>

- [snippet] `LS_APM_OTEL_ENABLED`: LS_APM_OTEL_ENABLED=true — `# If you set LS_APM_OTEL_ENABLED AND (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPO` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#ls-apm-otel-enabled
- [snippet] `LS_APM_OTEL_ENABLED`: LS_APM_OTEL_ENABLED=true — `LS_APM_OTEL_ENABLED=true` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#ls-apm-otel-enabled
- [definition] Cloud Agent Server environment variables — The Agent Server supports the following environment variables when deployed on [Cloud](/langsmith/deploy-to-cloud-overview). For variables specific to self-hosted deployments, see [Self-hosted Agent Server environment variables](/langsmith/env-var-self-hosted). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#cloud-agent-server-environment-variables
- [definition] `BG_JOB_ISOLATED_LOOPS` — Set `BG_JOB_ISOLATED_LOOPS` to `True` to execute background runs in an isolated event loop separate from the serving API event loop. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#bg-job-isolated-loops
- [definition] `BG_JOB_MAX_RETRIES` — Maximum number of times a background run will be retried after a retriable failure (e.g. transient database errors, server shutdown cancellations). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#bg-job-max-retries
- [definition] `BG_JOB_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_SECS` — Specifies, in seconds, how long the server will wait for background jobs to finish after the queue receives a shutdown signal. After this period, the server will force termination. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#bg-job-shutdown-grace-period-secs
- [definition] `BG_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECS` — The timeout of a background run can be increased. However, the infrastructure for a Cloud deployment enforces a 1 hour timeout limit for API requests. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#bg-job-timeout-secs
- [definition] `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` — Set `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` to specify allowed origins. - Example for allowing a single origin: `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS=https://example.com` - Example for allowing multiple origins: `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS=https://example.com,https://app.example.com` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#cors-allow-origins
- [definition] Supported Datadog environment variables {#dd_api_key} — Set these environment variables or secrets on the deployment to send Agent Server traces and logs to Datadog. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#supported-datadog-environment-variables-dd-api-key
- [definition] `LANGGRAPH_POSTGRES_POOL_MAX_SIZE` — Beginning with langgraph-api version `0.2.12`, the maximum size of the Postgres connection pool (per replica) can be controlled using the `LANGGRAPH_POSTGRES_POOL_MAX_SIZE` environment variable. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#langgraph-postgres-pool-max-size
- [definition] `LS_CHECKPOINT_DELETE` — JSON-valued configuration for deferred checkpoint deletion. When enabled, thread delete and prune operations enqueue checkpoints for background deletion instead of deleting synchronously, moving the I/O off the request hot path. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#ls-checkpoint-delete
- [definition] `LS_DEFAULT_CHECKPOINTER_BACKEND` — Sets the default [checkpointer backend](/langsmith/configure-checkpointer) for agent servers that don't specify one in `langgraph.json`. Accepted values: `"default"` (PostgreSQL), `"mongo"`, `"custom"`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#ls-default-checkpointer-backend
- [definition] `LANGSMITH_TRACING` — Set `LANGSMITH_TRACING` to `false` to disable tracing to LangSmith. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#langsmith-tracing
- [definition] `LOG_COLOR` — This is mainly relevant in the context of using the dev server via the `langgraph dev` command. Set `LOG_COLOR` to `true` to enable ANSI-colored console output when using the default console renderer. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#log-color
- [definition] `LOG_LEVEL` — Configure [log level](https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logging-levels). Defaults to `INFO`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#log-level
- [definition] `LOG_JSON` — Set `LOG_JSON` to `true` to render all log messages as JSON objects using the configured `JSONRenderer`. This produces structured logs that can be easily parsed or ingested by log management systems. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#log-json
- [definition] `N_JOBS_PER_WORKER` — Maximum number of runs a single queue worker executes concurrently from the Agent Server task queue. Defaults to `10`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#n-jobs-per-worker
- [definition] `LS_APM_OTEL_ENABLED` — To configure OpenTelemetry APM tracing for your deployment, set `LS_APM_OTEL_ENABLED` to `true` and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` to the target trace ingestion endpoint. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#ls-apm-otel-enabled
- [definition] `LS_MONGODB_URI` — MongoDB connection URI for the MongoDB checkpointer backend. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#ls-mongodb-uri
- [definition] `REDIS_MAX_CONNECTIONS` — The maximum size of the Redis connection pool (per replica) can be controlled using the `REDIS_MAX_CONNECTIONS` environment variable. By setting this variable, you can determine the upper bound on the number of simultaneous connections the server will establish with the Redis instance. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#redis-max-connections
- [definition] `RESUMABLE_STREAM_TTL_SECONDS` — Time-to-live in seconds for resumable stream data in Redis. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud#resumable-stream-ttl-seconds

## How to run a pairwise evaluation
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise>

- [snippet] Python: from langchain_classic import hub — `from langchain_classic import hub` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#run-a-pairwise-evaluation
- [snippet] TypeScript: import { evaluate} from "langsmith/evaluation"; — `import { evaluate} from "langsmith/evaluation";` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#run-a-pairwise-evaluation
- [parameter] `target`: A list of the two **existing experiments** you would like to evaluate against each other. These can be uuids or experiment names. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#evaluate-comparative-args
- [parameter] `evaluators`: A list of the pairwise evaluators that you would like to attach to this evaluation. See the section below for how to define these. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#evaluate-comparative-args
- [parameter] `randomize_order` / `randomizeOrder`: An optional boolean indicating whether the order of the outputs should be randomized for each evaluation. This is a strategy for minimizing positional bias in your prompt: often, the LLM will be biased towards one of the responses based on the order. This should mainly be addressed via prompt engineering, but this is another optional mitigation. Defaults to… — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#evaluate-comparative-args
- [parameter] `experiment_prefix` / `experimentPrefix`: A prefix to be attached to the beginning of the pairwise experiment name. Defaults to None. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#evaluate-comparative-args
- [parameter] `description`: A description of the pairwise experiment. Defaults to None. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#evaluate-comparative-args
- [parameter] `max_concurrency` / `maxConcurrency`: The maximum number of concurrent evaluations to run. Defaults to 5. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#evaluate-comparative-args
- [parameter] `client`: The LangSmith client to use. Defaults to None. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#evaluate-comparative-args
- [parameter] `metadata`: Metadata to attach to your pairwise experiment. Defaults to None. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#evaluate-comparative-args
- [parameter] `load_nested` / `loadNested`: Whether to load all child runs for the experiment. When False, only the root trace will be passed to your evaluator. Defaults to False. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#evaluate-comparative-args
- [definition] How to run a pairwise evaluation — Concept: [Pairwise evaluations](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#pairwise) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#how-to-run-a-pairwise-evaluation
- [definition] `evaluate()` comparative args — At its simplest, `evaluate` / `aevaluate` function takes the following arguments: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#evaluate-comparative-args
- [definition] Define a pairwise evaluator — Pairwise evaluators are just functions with an expected signature. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#define-a-pairwise-evaluator
- [definition] Evaluator args — Custom evaluator functions must have specific argument names. They can take any subset of the following arguments: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#evaluator-args
- [definition] Evaluator output — Custom evaluators are expected to return one of the following types: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-pairwise#evaluator-output

- [definition] Overview — A typical RAG evaluation workflow has three steps: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-rag-tutorial#overview
- [definition] Build the application — This tutorial uses LangChain, but the evaluation patterns work with any framework. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-rag-tutorial#build-the-application
- [definition] Create a dataset — Now that you have your application, create a small dataset of example questions and reference answers to evaluate it. This example uses an example set of inputs and outputs: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-rag-tutorial#create-a-dataset
- [definition] Define evaluators — RAG evaluators compare one artifact to another (response, input, retrieved docs, or reference answer): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-rag-tutorial#define-evaluators
- [definition] Correctness: Response vs reference answer — Use an LLM-as-judge to compare the generated answer to the reference answer in the dataset: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-rag-tutorial#correctness-response-vs-reference-answer
- [definition] Relevance: Response vs input — Compare `inputs` and `outputs` without `reference_outputs`. You cannot score accuracy without a reference answer, but you can still score whether the model addressed the question: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-rag-tutorial#relevance-response-vs-input
- [definition] Groundedness: Response vs retrieved docs — Another useful way to evaluate responses is to check whether the response is justified by (grounded in) the retrieved documents, without a reference answer: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-rag-tutorial#groundedness-response-vs-retrieved-docs
- [definition] Retrieval relevance: Retrieved docs vs input — Use an LLM-as-judge to score whether the retrieved documents are relevant to the user question: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-rag-tutorial#retrieval-relevance-retrieved-docs-vs-input
- [definition] Run the evaluation — Run the evaluation with all of the evaluators: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-rag-tutorial#run-the-evaluation

## Application-specific evaluation approaches

- [parameter] Document relevance: Detail=Are documents relevant to the question?; Needs reference output=No; LLM-as-judge?=Yes - [prompt](https://smith.langchain.com/hub/langchain-ai/rag-document-relevance); Pairwise relevant=No — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#rag-evaluation-summary
- [parameter] Answer faithfulness: Detail=Is the answer grounded in the documents?; Needs reference output=No; LLM-as-judge?=Yes - [prompt](https://smith.langchain.com/hub/langchain-ai/rag-answer-hallucination); Pairwise relevant=No — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#rag-evaluation-summary
- [parameter] Answer helpfulness: Detail=Does the answer help address the question?; Needs reference output=No; LLM-as-judge?=Yes - [prompt](https://smith.langchain.com/hub/langchain-ai/rag-answer-helpfulness); Pairwise relevant=No — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#rag-evaluation-summary
- [parameter] Answer correctness: Detail=Is the answer consistent with a reference answer?; Needs reference output=Yes; LLM-as-judge?=Yes - [prompt](https://smith.langchain.com/hub/langchain-ai/rag-answer-vs-reference); Pairwise relevant=No — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#rag-evaluation-summary
- [parameter] Pairwise comparison: Detail=How do multiple answer versions compare?; Needs reference output=No; LLM-as-judge?=Yes - [prompt](https://smith.langchain.com/hub/langchain-ai/pairwise-evaluation-rag); Pairwise relevant=Yes — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#rag-evaluation-summary
- [parameter] Factual accuracy: Detail=Is the summary accurate relative to the source documents?; Needs reference output=No; LLM-as-judge?=Yes - [prompt](https://smith.langchain.com/hub/langchain-ai/summary-accurancy-evaluator); Pairwise relevant=Yes — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#summarization
- [parameter] Faithfulness: Detail=Is the summary grounded in the source documents (e.g., no hallucinations)?; Needs reference output=No; LLM-as-judge?=Yes - [prompt](https://smith.langchain.com/hub/langchain-ai/summary-hallucination-evaluator); Pairwise relevant=Yes — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#summarization
- [parameter] Helpfulness: Detail=Is summary helpful relative to user need?; Needs reference output=No; LLM-as-judge?=Yes - [prompt](https://smith.langchain.com/hub/langchain-ai/summary-helpfulness-evaluator); Pairwise relevant=Yes — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#summarization
- [parameter] Accuracy: Detail=Standard definition; Needs reference output=Yes; LLM-as-judge?=No; Pairwise relevant=No — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#classification-and-tagging
- [parameter] Precision: Detail=Standard definition; Needs reference output=Yes; LLM-as-judge?=No; Pairwise relevant=No — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#classification-and-tagging
- [parameter] Recall: Detail=Standard definition; Needs reference output=Yes; LLM-as-judge?=No; Pairwise relevant=No — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#classification-and-tagging
- [definition] Application-specific evaluation approaches — Below, we will discuss evaluation of a few popular types of LLM applications. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#application-specific-evaluation-approaches
- [definition] Agents — [LLM-powered autonomous agents](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2023-06-23-agent/) combine three components (1) Tool calling, (2) Memory, and (3) Planning. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#agents
- [definition] Evaluating an agent's final response — One way to evaluate an agent is to assess its overall performance on a task. This basically involves treating the agent as a black box and simply evaluating whether or not it gets the job done. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#evaluating-an-agents-final-response
- [definition] Evaluating a single step of an agent — Agents generally perform multiple actions. While it is useful to evaluate them end-to-end, it can also be useful to evaluate these individual actions. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#evaluating-a-single-step-of-an-agent
- [definition] Evaluating an agent's trajectory — Evaluating an agent's trajectory involves evaluating all the steps an agent took. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#evaluating-an-agents-trajectory
- [definition] Evaluate RAG applications — [Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)](https://github.com/langchain-ai/rag-from-scratch) retrieves documents for a user input and passes them to a model so the response can use external knowledge. For a step-by-step walkthrough, see [Evaluate a RAG application](/langsmith/evaluate-rag-tutorial). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#evaluate-rag-applications
- [definition] Choose a dataset — When you evaluate RAG applications, start by deciding whether you have a reference answer for each example: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#choose-a-dataset
- [definition] Choose evaluators — LLM-as-judge evaluators work well for RAG because they can score factual accuracy and consistency between texts. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#choose-evaluators
- [definition] Summarization — Summarization is one specific type of free-form writing. The evaluation aim is typically to examine the writing (summary) relative to a set of criteria. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#summarization
- [definition] Classification and tagging — Classification and tagging apply a label to a given input (e.g., for toxicity detection, sentiment analysis, etc). Classification/tagging evaluation typically employs the following components, which we will review in detail below: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-approaches#classification-and-tagging
