- [parameter] **Data access**: **Offline Evaluation**=Inputs, Outputs, Reference Outputs; **Online Evaluation**=Inputs, Outputs only — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#quick-reference-offline-vs-online-evaluation
- [parameter] **When to use**: **Offline Evaluation**=Pre-deployment, during development; **Online Evaluation**=Production, post-deployment — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#quick-reference-offline-vs-online-evaluation
- [parameter] **Primary use cases**: **Offline Evaluation**=Benchmarking, unit testing, regression testing, backtesting; **Online Evaluation**=Real-time monitoring, production feedback, anomaly detection — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#quick-reference-offline-vs-online-evaluation
- [parameter] **Evaluation timing**: **Offline Evaluation**=Batch processing on curated test sets; **Online Evaluation**=Real-time or near real-time on live traffic — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#quick-reference-offline-vs-online-evaluation
- [parameter] **Setup location**: **Offline Evaluation**=Evaluation tab (SDK, UI, Playground); **Online Evaluation**=[Observability tab](/langsmith/online-evaluations-llm-as-judge) (automated rules) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#quick-reference-offline-vs-online-evaluation
- [parameter] **Data requirements**: **Offline Evaluation**=Requires dataset curation; **Online Evaluation**=No dataset needed, evaluates live traces — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#quick-reference-offline-vs-online-evaluation
- [definition] Evaluation concepts — LLM outputs are non-deterministic, which makes response quality hard to assess. Evaluations (evals) are a way to breakdown what "good" looks like and measure it. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#evaluation-concepts
- [definition] What to evaluate — Before building evaluations, identify what matters for your application. Break down your system into its critical components—LLM calls, retrieval steps, tool invocations, output formatting—and determine quality criteria for each. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#what-to-evaluate
- [definition] Offline and online evaluations — LangSmith supports two types of evaluations that serve different purposes in your development workflow: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#offline-and-online-evaluations
- [definition] Offline evaluations — <Icon icon="flask" iconType="solid" /> Use offline evaluations for **pre-deployment testing**: - **Benchmarking**: Compare multiple versions to find the best performer. - **Regression testing**: Ensure new versions don't degrade quality. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#offline-evaluations
- [definition] Online evaluations — <Icon icon="radar" iconType="solid" /> Use online evaluations for **production monitoring**: - **Real-time monitoring**: Track quality continuously on live traffic. - **Anomaly detection**: Flag unusual patterns or edge cases. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#online-evaluations
- [definition] Evaluation lifecycle — As you develop and [deploy your application](/langsmith/deployment), your evaluation strategy evolves from pre-deployment testing to production monitoring. During development and testing, offline evaluations validate functionality against curated datasets. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#evaluation-lifecycle
- [definition] 1. Development with offline evaluation — Before production deployment, use offline evaluations to validate functionality, benchmark different approaches, and build confidence. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#1-development-with-offline-evaluation
- [definition] 2. Initial deployment with online evaluation — After deployment, use online evaluations to monitor production quality, detect unexpected issues, and collect real-world data. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#2-initial-deployment-with-online-evaluation
- [definition] 3. Continuous improvement — Use both evaluation types together in an iterative feedback loop. Online evaluations surface issues that become offline test cases, offline evaluations validate fixes, and online evaluations confirm production improvements. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#3-continuous-improvement
- [definition] Core evaluation targets — Evaluations run on different targets depending on whether they are offline or online. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#core-evaluation-targets
- [definition] Targets for offline evaluation — Offline evaluations run on datasets and examples. The presence of reference outputs enables comparison between expected and actual results. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#targets-for-offline-evaluation
- [definition] Targets for online evaluation — Online evaluations run on runs and threads from production traffic. Without reference outputs, evaluators focus on detecting issues, anomalies, and quality degradation in real-time. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#targets-for-online-evaluation
- [definition] Evaluators — _Evaluators_ are workspace-level resources that score application performance. They provide the measurement layer for both offline and online evaluation, adapting their inputs based on what data is available. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#evaluators
- [definition] Attaching an evaluator to a tracing project or dataset — A single evaluator can be attached to many tracing projects and datasets. Configuration like sampling rate, filters, and [spend limits](/langsmith/evaluator-spend) is set per attached project or dataset, not per evaluator. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#attaching-an-evaluator-to-a-tracing-project-or-dataset
- [definition] Evaluator inputs — Evaluator inputs differ based on evaluation type: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#evaluator-inputs
- [definition] Evaluator outputs — Evaluators return **feedback**, which is the scores from evaluation. Feedback is a dictionary or list of dictionaries. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#evaluator-outputs
- [definition] Evaluation techniques — LangSmith supports several evaluation approaches: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#evaluation-techniques
- [definition] Reference-free vs reference-based evaluators — Understanding whether an evaluator requires reference outputs is essential for determining when it can be used. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#reference-free-vs-reference-based-evaluators
- [definition] Evaluation types — LangSmith supports various evaluation approaches for different stages of development and deployment. Understanding when to use each type helps build a comprehensive evaluation strategy. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#evaluation-types
- [definition] Building datasets — There are various strategies for building datasets: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#building-datasets
- [definition] Human feedback collection — Human feedback often provides the most valuable assessment, particularly for subjective quality dimensions. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#human-feedback-collection
- [definition] Evaluations vs testing — Testing and evaluation are similar but distinct concepts. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#evaluations-vs-testing
- [definition] Quick reference: Offline vs online evaluation — The following table summarizes the key differences between offline and online evaluations: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#quick-reference-offline-vs-online-evaluation

## Evaluation types
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types>

- [definition] Evaluation types — This page covers two aspects of evaluation in LangSmith: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#evaluation-types
- [definition] Offline evaluation types — Offline evaluation tests applications on curated datasets before deployment. By running evaluations on examples with reference outputs, teams can compare versions, validate functionality, and build confidence before exposing changes to users. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#offline-evaluation-types
- [definition] Benchmarking — _Benchmarking_ compares multiple application versions on a curated dataset to identify the best performer. This process involves creating a dataset of representative inputs, defining performance metrics, and testing each version. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#benchmarking
- [definition] Unit tests — _Unit tests_ verify the correctness of individual system components. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#unit-tests
- [definition] Regression tests — _Regression tests_ measure performance consistency across application versions over time. They ensure new versions do not degrade performance on cases the current version handles correctly, and ideally demonstrate improvements over the baseline. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#regression-tests
- [definition] Backtesting — _Backtesting_ evaluates new application versions against historical production data. Production logs are converted into a dataset, then newer versions process these examples to assess performance on past, realistic user inputs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#backtesting
- [definition] Pairwise evaluation — _Pairwise evaluation_ compares outputs from two versions by determining relative quality rather than assigning absolute scores. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#pairwise-evaluation
- [definition] Online evaluation types — Online evaluation assesses production application outputs in near real-time. Without reference outputs, these evaluations focus on detecting issues, monitoring quality trends, and identifying edge cases that inform future offline testing. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#online-evaluation-types
- [definition] Real-time monitoring — Monitor application quality continuously as users interact with the system. Online evaluations run automatically on production traffic, providing immediate feedback on each interaction. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#real-time-monitoring
- [definition] Anomaly detection — Identify outliers and edge cases that deviate from expected patterns. Online evaluators can flag runs with unusual characteristics—extremely long or short responses, unexpected error rates, or outputs that fail safety checks—for human review and potential addition to offline datasets. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#anomaly-detection
- [definition] Production feedback loop — Use insights from production to improve offline evaluation. Online evaluations surface real-world issues and usage patterns that may not appear in curated datasets. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#production-feedback-loop
- [definition] Implement evaluators — The evaluation types above describe _when_ to evaluate. LangSmith provides several approaches for _how_ to implement evaluators that work across these evaluation types. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#implement-evaluators
- [definition] LLM-as-a-judge — Use an LLM to score outputs based on criteria defined in a prompt. This approach works well for subjective qualities like tone, clarity, or semantic correctness that are difficult to capture with deterministic rules. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#llm-as-a-judge
- [definition] Code evaluators — Write deterministic, rule-based functions that check specific conditions. These evaluators execute custom logic to validate structure, check for patterns, or apply business rules. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#code-evaluators
- [definition] Composite evaluators — Combine multiple evaluator scores into a single metric using weighted averages or sums. This creates aggregate quality scores that reflect multiple evaluation criteria simultaneously. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#composite-evaluators
- [definition] Summary evaluators — Compute metrics across an entire experiment rather than individual examples. These evaluators receive all outputs from a dataset and calculate aggregate statistics like precision, recall, F1 scores, or distribution analysis. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#summary-evaluators
- [definition] Pairwise evaluators — Compare outputs from two versions to determine relative quality. This approach, covered earlier under [pairwise evaluation](#pairwise-evaluation), helps when absolute scoring is difficult but determining "which is better" is straightforward. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-types#pairwise-evaluators

## LangSmith Evaluation
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation>

- [definition] LangSmith Evaluation — LangSmith's testing tools help you measure agent quality, iterate on prompts, and debug live in an interactive environment. Evaluation is the core of testing: it scores your agent's outputs against datasets and criteria so you can benchmark versions, catch regressions, and track quality over time. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation#langsmith-evaluation
- [definition] Create an account — Sign up at [smith.langchain.com](https://smith.langchain.com?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=snippets-langsmith-account-api-key-quickstart) (no credit card required). You can log in with **Google**, **GitHub**, or **email**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation#set-up-your-account
- [definition] Create an API key — Go to your [Settings page](https://smith.langchain.com/settings) → **API Keys** → **Create API Key**. Copy the key and save it securely. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation#set-up-your-account
- [definition] Create a dataset — Create a [dataset](/langsmith/manage-datasets) with <Tooltip tip="Individual test cases with inputs and reference outputs">[examples](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#examples)</Tooltip> from manually curated test cases, historical production traces, or synthetic data generation. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation#evaluation-workflow
- [definition] Define evaluators — Create <Tooltip tip="Functions that score how well your application performs">[evaluators](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#evaluators)</Tooltip> to score performance: - [Human](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#human) review - [Code](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#code) rules… — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation#evaluation-workflow
- [definition] Run an experiment — Execute your application on the dataset to create an <Tooltip tip="Results of evaluating a specific application version on a dataset">[experiment](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#experiment)</Tooltip>. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation#evaluation-workflow
- [definition] Analyze results — Compare experiments for [benchmarking](/langsmith/evaluation-types#benchmarking), [unit tests](/langsmith/evaluation-types#unit-tests), [regression tests](/langsmith/evaluation-types#regression-tests), or [backtesting](/langsmith/evaluation-types#backtesting). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation#evaluation-workflow
- [definition] Deploy your application — Each interaction creates a <Tooltip tip="A single execution trace including inputs, outputs, and intermediate steps">[run](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#runs)</Tooltip> without reference outputs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation#evaluation-workflow
- [definition] Configure online evaluators — Set up [evaluators](/langsmith/online-evaluations-llm-as-judge) to run automatically on production traces: safety checks, format validation, quality heuristics, and reference-free LLM-as-judge. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation#evaluation-workflow
- [definition] Monitor in real-time — Evaluators run automatically on [runs](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#runs) or <Tooltip tip="Collections of related runs forming multi-turn conversations">[threads](/langsmith/online-evaluations-multi-turn)</Tooltip>, providing real-time monitoring, anomaly detection, and alerting. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation#evaluation-workflow
- [definition] Establish a feedback loop — Add failing production traces to your [dataset](/langsmith/manage-datasets), create targeted evaluators, validate fixes with offline experiments, and redeploy. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation#evaluation-workflow
- [definition] Get started — <Card title="Evaluation quickstart" icon="rocket" href="/langsmith/evaluation-quickstart" arrow="true" > Get started with offline evaluation. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation#get-started

## Track and limit evaluator spend
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend>

- [parameter] [Evaluators page dashboard](#evaluators-page-dashboard): Where to find it=**Evaluators** in the left sidebar; Who can see or change it=All workspace members — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#spend-views-and-controls
- [parameter] [Evaluators table](#evaluators-table) (Spend, Spend Status): Where to find it=**Evaluators** in the left sidebar; Who can see or change it=All workspace members — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#spend-views-and-controls
- [parameter] [Projects & Datasets tab](#projects-%26-datasets-tab-on-an-evaluator): Where to find it=Open an evaluator, **Projects & Datasets**; Who can see or change it=All workspace members — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#spend-views-and-controls
- [parameter] [Organization default spend limit](#set-an-organization-default-spend-limit): Where to find it=Organization **Settings** > **Usage Configuration**; Who can see or change it=`organization:manage` required to view and edit — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#spend-views-and-controls
- [parameter] [Per-evaluator override](#override-the-default-for-an-attached-project-or-dataset): Where to find it=Edit evaluator > **Advanced** > **Spend limit**; Who can see or change it=All members can view, `organization:manage` required to edit — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#spend-views-and-controls
- [definition] Track and limit evaluator spend — Cap weekly LLM spend per evaluator to prevent a single evaluator from exceeding your budget. LangSmith tracks week-to-date evaluator spend, resetting at Monday 12AM UTC. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#track-and-limit-evaluator-spend
- [definition] How enforcement works — LangSmith records spend after each evaluator run completes, then sums spend from Monday 12AM UTC to the current moment. When the total reaches the effective limit, LangSmith pauses the evaluator on that attached project or dataset. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#how-enforcement-works
- [definition] View evaluator spend — You can find spend in the following UI locations: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#view-evaluator-spend
- [definition] Evaluators page dashboard — Navigate to the **Evaluators** page from the left sidebar. The top of the page shows a weekly view across the workspace: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#evaluators-page-dashboard
- [definition] Evaluators table — The Evaluators table on the same page includes: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#evaluators-table
- [definition] Projects & Datasets tab on an evaluator — Open an evaluator and select the **Projects & Datasets** tab to see per-project or dataset spend and limits: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#projects-datasets-tab-on-an-evaluator
- [definition] Set an organization default spend limit — Organization admins set a single weekly cap that applies to every evaluator's attached projects and datasets across every workspace in the organization. There is one default per organization, not one per workspace. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#set-an-organization-default-spend-limit
- [definition] Override the default for an attached project or dataset — Organization admins can override the default for a specific project or dataset attached to an evaluator. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#override-the-default-for-an-attached-project-or-dataset
- [definition] When a limit is reached — When weekly spend on an attached project or dataset reaches its effective limit: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#when-a-limit-is-reached
- [definition] Configure model pricing — When a spend limit is set, evaluators can only be run on supported models (OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini), and the models need to have pricing configured. Models without pricing configured cannot be used in evaluators. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend#configure-model-pricing

## Manage evaluators
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluators>

- [snippet] Python: import asyncio — `import asyncio` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluators#create-an-evaluator-with-the-sdk
- [snippet] TypeScript: import { Client } from "langsmith"; — `import { Client } from "langsmith";` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluators#create-an-evaluator-with-the-sdk
- [parameter] Name: The evaluator name — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluators#view-evaluators
- [parameter] Type: **LLM as a judge** or **Code**. Composite score evaluators are scoped to individual tracing projects and datasets and do not appear here. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluators#view-evaluators
- [parameter] Feedback Key: The feedback key the evaluator produces — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluators#view-evaluators
- [parameter] Projects & Datasets: Tracing projects and datasets this evaluator is attached to — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluators#view-evaluators
- [parameter] Evaluator Trace Count (this week): Number of traces this evaluator ran on in the past week. Only shown when spend tracking is enabled; **–** for Code evaluators or evaluators with no attached rules. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluators#view-evaluators
- [parameter] Spend (this week): Estimated USD spend for this evaluator in the past week. Only shown when spend tracking is enabled; **–** for Code evaluators or evaluators with no attached rules. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluators#view-evaluators
- [parameter] Spend Status: Whether the evaluator is **Under limits**, **Unlimited**, or has hit one or more configured spend limits. Only shown when spend tracking is enabled; **–** for Code evaluators. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluators#view-evaluators

- [definition] Chain evaluators — Extended stats can be used to chain evaluators, where a code evaluator reads a score that another evaluator already produced. - [definition] Delete an evaluator — You cannot delete an evaluator while it is attached to a tracing project or dataset. To delete an evaluator: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluators#delete-an-evaluator

- [parameter] `thread.events`: Iterate every raw protocol event (Python). In JavaScript, open `thread.subscribe(...)`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#what-event-streaming-provides
- [parameter] `thread.messages`: Stream chat model messages, token deltas, reasoning, and tool-call argument chunks. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#what-event-streaming-provides
- [parameter] `thread.values`: Iterate state snapshots and await the final value. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#what-event-streaming-provides
- [parameter] `thread.output`: Await the final output. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#what-event-streaming-provides
- [parameter] `thread.tool_calls` (`thread.toolCalls` in JavaScript): Observe tool invocations with assembled input, streamed output, and result. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#what-event-streaming-provides
- [parameter] `thread.subgraphs`: Discover and observe nested graph executions. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#what-event-streaming-provides
- [parameter] `thread.subagents`: Subagent-oriented view of `thread.subgraphs`. Use this name when working with Deep Agents subagent invocations. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#what-event-streaming-provides
- [parameter] `thread.interrupts`: Inspect human-in-the-loop interrupt payloads. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#what-event-streaming-provides
- [parameter] `thread.interrupted`: Check whether the run paused for human input. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#what-event-streaming-provides
- [parameter] `thread.extensions`: Consume custom stream transformer projections published on `custom:<name>` channels. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#what-event-streaming-provides
- [parameter] `values`: Full graph state snapshots. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#channels-and-event-lifecycle
- [parameter] `updates`: Per-node state deltas. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#channels-and-event-lifecycle
- [parameter] `messages`: Content-block-centric chat model output. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#channels-and-event-lifecycle
- [parameter] `tools`: Tool call start, streamed output, finish, and error events. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#channels-and-event-lifecycle
- [parameter] `lifecycle`: Run, subgraph, and subagent status changes. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#channels-and-event-lifecycle
- [parameter] `checkpoints`: Lightweight checkpoint envelopes for branching and time travel. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#channels-and-event-lifecycle
- [parameter] `input`: Human-in-the-loop input requests and responses. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#channels-and-event-lifecycle
- [parameter] `tasks`: Pregel task creation and result events. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#channels-and-event-lifecycle
- [parameter] `custom`: User-defined payloads from graph code. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#channels-and-event-lifecycle
- [parameter] `custom:<name>`: Application-defined stream transformer output. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#channels-and-event-lifecycle
- [definition] Event streaming API — Event streaming is the typed-projection streaming model for LangSmith deployments. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#event-streaming-api
- [definition] What event streaming provides — The stream returned by `client.threads.stream(...)` exposes typed projections over one underlying event flow: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#what-event-streaming-provides
- [definition] Stream messages — Use `thread.messages` for chat model output: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#stream-messages
- [definition] Stream state — Use `thread.values` to stream full state snapshots after each step: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#stream-state
- [definition] Stream tool calls — `thread.tool_calls` (`thread.toolCalls` in JavaScript) exposes assembled tool invocations. Each handle carries the tool name (`call.name`) and the assembled input (`call.input`, a plain value—not awaited). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#stream-tool-calls
- [definition] Stream subgraphs — Use `thread.subgraphs` to observe nested graph work without parsing namespace strings: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#stream-subgraphs
- [definition] Stream output — Await `thread.output` for the final state once the run completes: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#stream-output
- [definition] Stream multiple projections — Run concurrent consumers when application code needs more than one projection at a time: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#stream-multiple-projections
- [definition] Resume after an interrupt — When a graph pauses for human input, inspect `thread.interrupted` and `thread.interrupts`, then resume by responding to the interrupt: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#resume-after-an-interrupt
- [definition] Join an active run — To attach to a run already in flight on a thread—after a page reload, in a separate worker, or from another client—open the thread stream with the existing `thread_id` and skip `thread.run.start()`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#join-an-active-run
- [definition] Stream all protocol events — Read the raw protocol event flow when application code needs every event. In Python, iterate `thread.events`; in JavaScript, open a `subscribe` (the JavaScript stream object is not itself iterable): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#stream-all-protocol-events
- [definition] Channels and event lifecycle — Raw events flow on channels. The channel name appears as the event's `method`; each channel emits a specific event shape. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#channels-and-event-lifecycle
- [definition] Messages — The `messages` channel models output as content blocks. The `data.event` field is one of `message-start`, `content-block-start`, `content-block-delta`, `content-block-finish`, `message-finish`, or `error`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#messages
- [definition] Tools — The `tools` channel exposes tool execution. The `data.event` field is one of `tool-started`, `tool-output-delta`, `tool-finished`, `tool-error`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#tools
- [definition] Lifecycle — The `lifecycle` channel tracks root run, subgraph, and subagent status. The `data.event` field is one of `started`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `interrupted`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#lifecycle
- [definition] Resume from last event — Event streams are resumable. The Agent Server buffers events per run in a bounded buffer, assigns each a `seq` (per-session ordering) and a durable `event_id` (stable across replays and replicas), and replays from a cursor on reconnect. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/event-streaming#resume-from-last-event

## Example data format
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/example-data-format>

- [parameter] **id**: Type=UUID; Description=Unique identifier for the example. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/example-data-format#example-data-format
- [parameter] **name**: Type=string; Description=The name of the example. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/example-data-format#example-data-format
- [parameter] **created\_at**: Type=datetime; Description=The time this example was created — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/example-data-format#example-data-format
- [parameter] **modified\_at**: Type=datetime; Description=The last time this example was modified — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/example-data-format#example-data-format
- [parameter] **inputs**: Type=object; Description=A map of inputs for the example. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/example-data-format#example-data-format
- [parameter] **outputs**: Type=object; Description=A map or set of outputs generated by the run. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/example-data-format#example-data-format
- [parameter] **dataset\_id**: Type=UUID; Description=The dataset the example belongs to — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/example-data-format#example-data-format
- [parameter] **source\_run\_id**: Type=UUID; Description=For examples created from a LangSmith [`Run`](/langsmith/run-data-format), the ID of that run — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/example-data-format#example-data-format
- [parameter] **source\_thread\_id**: Type=string; Description=For examples created from a [thread](/langsmith/observability-concepts#threads) or from a run in a thread, the ID of that thread — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/example-data-format#example-data-format
- [parameter] **metadata**: Type=object; Description=A map of additional, user or SDK defined information that can be stored on an example. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/example-data-format#example-data-format

## Experiment configuration
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/experiment-configuration>

- [definition] Experiment configuration — LangSmith supports several configuration options for experiments: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/experiment-configuration#experiment-configuration
- [definition] Repetitions — _Repetitions_ run an experiment multiple times to account for LLM output variability. Since LLM outputs are non-deterministic, multiple repetitions provide a more accurate performance estimate. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/experiment-configuration#repetitions
- [definition] Concurrency — _Concurrency_ controls how many examples run simultaneously during an experiment. Configure it by passing the `max_concurrency` argument to `evaluate` / `aevaluate`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/experiment-configuration#concurrency
- [definition] Caching — _Caching_ stores API call results to disk to speed up future experiments. Set the `LANGSMITH_TEST_CACHE` environment variable to a valid folder path with write access. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/experiment-configuration#caching

- [definition] Query traces using the SDK — The recommended way to query [runs](/langsmith/observability-concepts#runs) (the span data in LangSmith traces) is to use the `list_runs` method in the [SDK](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langsmith/) or `/runs/query` endpoint in the [API](/langsmith/smith-api-ref). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#query-traces-using-the-sdk
- [definition] Use filter arguments — For simple queries, you don't have to rely on our query syntax. You can use the filter arguments specified in the [filter arguments reference](/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#use-filter-arguments
- [definition] List root runs in a project — Root runs are runs that have no parents. These are assigned a value of `True` for `is_root`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#list-root-runs-in-a-project
- [definition] Fetch a single run by ID — To fetch a single run (trace) by its ID, use the `read_run` method. This is useful when you have a specific trace ID (for example, from a LangSmith share link like `https://smith.langchain.com/public/<trace-id>/r`) and want to retrieve its full data. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#fetch-a-single-run-by-id
- [definition] Use filter query language — For more complex queries, you can use the filter query language. The following examples cover the most common patterns. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#use-filter-query-language
- [definition] List all root runs in a conversational thread — This is the way to fetch runs in a conversational thread. For more information on setting up threads, refer to our [how-to guide on setting up threads](/langsmith/threads). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#list-all-root-runs-in-a-conversational-thread
- [definition] Search trace trees by full text — You can use the `search()` function without any specific field to do a full text search across all string fields in a run. This allows you to quickly find traces that match a search term. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#search-trace-trees-by-full-text
- [definition] Check for presence of metadata — If you want to check for the presence of metadata, you can use the `eq` operator, optionally with an `and` statement to match by value. This is useful if you want to log more structured information about your runs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#check-for-presence-of-metadata
- [definition] Check for environment details in metadata — A common pattern is to add environment information to your traces via metadata. If you want to filter for runs containing environment metadata, you can use the same pattern as above: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#check-for-environment-details-in-metadata
- [definition] Check for thread ID in metadata — A common way to associate traces in the same conversation is by using a shared thread ID. If you want to filter runs based on a thread ID in this way, you can search for that ID in the metadata. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#check-for-thread-id-in-metadata
- [definition] Negative filtering on key-value pairs — You can use negative filtering on metadata, input, and output key-value pairs to exclude specific runs from your results. Here are some examples for metadata key-value pairs but the same logic applies to input and output key-value pairs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#negative-filtering-on-key-value-pairs
- [definition] Combine multiple filters — If you want to combine multiple conditions to refine your search, you can use the `and` operator along with other filtering functions. - [definition] Tree filter — List all runs named "RetrieveDocs" whose root run has a "user_score" feedback of 1 and any run in the full trace is named "ExpandQuery". — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#tree-filter
- [definition] Query trace trees with child-run predicates — Use `trace_filter` to match fields on the root run and `tree_filter` to match supported searchable fields on any run in the trace tree. For predicates over arbitrary returned child-run fields, such as nested `inputs`, `outputs`, or `extra` payloads, use the steps below: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/export-traces#query-trace-trees-with-child-run-predicates
- [definition] Advanced: export flattened trace view with child tool usage — The following Python example demonstrates how to export a flattened view of traces, including information on the tools (from nested runs) used by the agent within each trace. - [parameter] Streaming: LangGraph (open source)=Basic; LangSmith=Dedicated mode for token-by-token messages — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#how-are-langgraph-and-langsmith-different

- [parameter] Deployment: LangGraph (open source)=Self-managed; LangSmith=• Cloud <br /> • Free self-hosted <br /> • Enterprise (paid self-hosted) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#how-are-langgraph-and-langsmith-different
- [parameter] Scalability: LangGraph (open source)=Self-managed; LangSmith=Auto-scaling of task queues and servers — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#how-are-langgraph-and-langsmith-different
- [parameter] Fault-tolerance: LangGraph (open source)=Self-managed; LangSmith=Automated retries — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#how-are-langgraph-and-langsmith-different
- [parameter] Concurrency Control: LangGraph (open source)=Simple threading; LangSmith=Supports double-texting — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#how-are-langgraph-and-langsmith-different

- [definition] *Does my application need egress to function properly?* — Our deployment only needs egress for a few things (most of which can reside within your VPC): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#does-my-application-need-egress-to-function-properly
- [definition] *Are downgrades supported?* — Downgrades are not officially supported. LangSmith upgrades may include database migrations and other changes that are not backward-compatible. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#are-downgrades-supported
- [definition] Do I need to use LangChain to use LangGraph? what's the difference? — No. LangGraph is an orchestration framework for complex agentic systems and is more low-level and controllable than LangChain agents. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#do-i-need-to-use-langchain-to-use-langgraph-whats-the-difference
- [definition] How is LangGraph different from other agent frameworks? — Other agentic frameworks can work for simple, generic tasks but fall short for complex tasks bespoke to a company’s needs. LangGraph provides a more expressive framework to handle companies’ unique tasks without restricting users to a single black-box cognitive architecture. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#how-is-langgraph-different-from-other-agent-frameworks
- [definition] Does LangGraph impact the performance of my app? — LangGraph will not add any overhead to your code and is specifically designed with streaming workflows in mind. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#does-langgraph-impact-the-performance-of-my-app
- [definition] Is LangGraph open source? is it free? — Yes. LangGraph is an MIT-licensed open-source library and is free to use. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#is-langgraph-open-source-is-it-free
- [definition] How are LangGraph and LangSmith different? — LangGraph is a stateful, orchestration framework that brings added control to agent workflows. LangSmith is a service for deploying and scaling agentic applications, with an opinionated API for building agent UXs, plus an integrated developer UI. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#how-are-langgraph-and-langsmith-different
- [definition] Does LangGraph work with LLMs that don't support tool calling? — Yes! You can use LangGraph with any LLMs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#does-langgraph-work-with-llms-that-dont-support-tool-calling
- [definition] Does LangGraph work with OSS LLMs? — Yes! LangGraph is totally ambivalent to what LLMs are used under the hood. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#does-langgraph-work-with-oss-llms
- [definition] Can I use Studio without logging in to LangSmith? — Yes! You can use the [development version of Agent Server](/langsmith/local-dev-testing) to run the backend locally. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#can-i-use-studio-without-logging-in-to-langsmith
- [definition] What is a Deployment Run? — A Deployment Run is one end-to-end invocation of a LangGraph agent deployed via LangSmith Deployment. Nodes and subgraphs are not charged separately. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/faq#what-is-a-deployment-run

- [parameter] `created_at`: Type=datetime; Description=Timestamp when the record was created — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/feedback-data-format#feedback-data-format
- [parameter] `modified_at`: Type=datetime; Description=Timestamp when the record was last modified — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/feedback-data-format#feedback-data-format
- [parameter] `session_id`: Type=UUID; Description=Unique identifier for the experiment or tracing project the run was a part of. Required when creating feedback for a run. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/feedback-data-format#feedback-data-format

- [parameter] `score`: Type=number; Description=Numerical score associated with the feedback key — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/feedback-data-format#feedback-data-format
- [parameter] `value`: Type=string; Description=Reserved for storing a value associated with the score. Useful for categorical feedback. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/feedback-data-format#feedback-data-format
- [parameter] `comment`: Type=string; Description=Any comment or annotation associated with the record. This can be a justification for the score given. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/feedback-data-format#feedback-data-format
- [parameter] `correction`: Type=object; Description=Reserved for storing correction details, if any — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/feedback-data-format#feedback-data-format
- [parameter] `feedback_source`: Type=object; Description=Object containing information about the feedback source — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/feedback-data-format#feedback-data-format
- [parameter] `feedback_source.type`: Type=string; Description=The type of source where the feedback originated, e.g. `'api'`, `'app'`, `'evaluator'` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/feedback-data-format#feedback-data-format
- [parameter] `feedback_source.metadata`: Type=object; Description=Reserved for additional metadata, currently — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/feedback-data-format#feedback-data-format

- [definition] Filter traces — Tracing projects can accumulate large amounts of data across [threads](/langsmith/observability-concepts#threads), [traces](/langsmith/observability-concepts#traces), and [runs](/langsmith/observability-concepts#runs). LangSmith's filtering tools let you navigate and analyze that data precisely. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/filter-traces-in-application#filter-traces

- [definition] Negative filtering on key-value pairs — Different types of negative filtering can be applied to **\{x} Metadata**, **<Icon icon="arrow-down-right"/> Input**, and **<Icon icon="arrow-up-left"/> Output** fields to exclude specific runs from your results. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/filter-traces-in-application#negative-filtering-on-key-value-pairs

- [definition] Update a saved filter — With the filter selected in the dropdown, you can make any changes to filter parameters. Then, click **Save** to update the filter. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/filter-traces-in-application#update-a-saved-filter
- [definition] Delete a saved filter — Click the <Icon icon="dots-vertical"/> icon next to the saved filter in the dropdown, and delete the filter using the trash <Icon icon="trash"/> icon. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/filter-traces-in-application#delete-a-saved-filter
- [definition] Copy a filter — You can copy a constructed filter to share it with colleagues, reuse it later, or query runs programmatically in the [API](/langsmith/smith-api/run/query-runs) or [SDK](https://docs.smith.langchain.com/reference/python/client/langsmith.client.Client#langsmith.client.Client.list_runs). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/filter-traces-in-application#copy-a-filter

- [definition] Manually specify a raw query in LangSmith query language — If you have [copied a previously constructed filter](#copy-a-filter), you may want to manually apply this raw query in a future session. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/filter-traces-in-application#manually-specify-a-raw-query-in-langsmith-query-language
- [definition] Filter for runs (spans) on properties of the root — A common concept is to filter for runs which are part of a trace whose root run has some attribute. - [definition] Filter for runs (spans) whose child runs have some attribute — You may want to search for runs who have specific types of sub runs. - [definition] Example: Filtering on all runs whose tree contains the tool call filter — Extending the [tool call filtering example](#example-filtering-for-tool-calls), if you would like to filter for all runs _whose tree contains_ the tool filter call, you can use the tree filter in the **Advanced** filters setting. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/filter-traces-in-application#example-filtering-on-all-runs-whose-tree-contains-the-tool-call-filter

## Access & oversight
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight>

- [snippet] Policy evaluation order: ABAC deny → RBAC → ABAC allow — `ABAC deny → RBAC → ABAC allow` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#policy-evaluation-order
- [snippet] Policy evaluation order: Workspace policy gate → ABAC deny → RBAC → ABAC allow — `Workspace policy gate → ABAC deny → RBAC → ABAC allow` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#policy-evaluation-order
- [parameter] `mcp-servers:read`: Discover and list MCP servers and integrations — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#role-based-permissions
- [parameter] `mcp-servers:invoke`: Execute tools from MCP servers and integrations, including OAuth connect/disconnect — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#role-based-permissions
- [parameter] `mcp-servers:create`: Create new MCP server configurations — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#role-based-permissions
- [parameter] `mcp-servers:update`: Modify MCP server configurations — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#role-based-permissions
- [parameter] `mcp-servers:delete`: Remove MCP server configurations — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#role-based-permissions
- [parameter] `mcp_server`: Custom MCP servers added to the workspace — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#attribute-based-access-control
- [parameter] `fleet_integration`: Built-in integrations (Gmail, Slack, GitHub, etc.) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#attribute-based-access-control
- [definition] Access & oversight — Fleet gives you the control layer for scaling agents across your organization: tiered permissions, credential management, human-in-the-loop oversight, and an audit trail for agent actions. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#access-oversight
- [definition] Permissions and sharing — Fleet provides granular control over every agent in two dimensions: **who gets access** and **what they can do**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#permissions-and-sharing
- [definition] Agent identity and credentials — Fleet offers two credential models that control how agents authenticate with external tools: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#agent-identity-and-credentials
- [definition] Tool access control — Fleet provides layered access control for tools, covering both **custom MCP servers** (user-added, workspace-scoped) and **built-in integrations** (platform-provided, such as Gmail, Slack, and GitHub): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#tool-access-control
- [definition] Role-based permissions — Role-based access control (RBAC) grants or denies access to all MCP servers and integrations in a workspace based on a user's role. Configure roles in **Settings > Roles**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#role-based-permissions
- [definition] Open role settings — Navigate to **Settings > Roles** and click **Create role**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#create-a-role-with-tool-permissions
- [definition] Configure MCP Servers permissions — Expand the **MCP Servers** section and select the permissions to include. For example, grant `Read` and `Invoke` for users who need to use tools but not manage server configurations. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#create-a-role-with-tool-permissions
- [definition] Assign the role — Assign the role to users in the workspace in **Settings > Members**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#create-a-role-with-tool-permissions
- [definition] Attribute-based access control — Attribute-based access control (ABAC) adds resource-level granularity on top of RBAC. Admins can tag individual MCP servers or integrations and create policies that grant or restrict access based on those tags. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#attribute-based-access-control
- [definition] Workspace integration policy — Built-in integrations have an additional control layer: a workspace-level enable/disable toggle managed from **Settings > Integrations > Access control**. This acts as an admin-controlled baseline that runs before per-user RBAC and ABAC. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#workspace-integration-policy
- [definition] Policy evaluation order — The three layers evaluate in sequence. The evaluation order differs slightly between custom MCP servers and built-in integrations: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#policy-evaluation-order
- [definition] Observability and audit trail — Agent actions in Fleet are captured in a structured [LangSmith trace](/langsmith/observability), including tool calls, decisions, and outputs. You can inspect, search, and export traces. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#observability-and-audit-trail
- [definition] Human-in-the-loop oversight — Fleet provides a [central inbox](https://smith.langchain.com/agents/inbox) for reviewing agent actions across all your agents. You can configure agents to pause and request approval before taking specific actions, then review, approve, edit, or reject from one place. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/access-and-oversight#human-in-the-loop-oversight

## Agent identity
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/agent-identity>

- [definition] Agent identity — Agent identity controls whose [credentials](/langsmith/fleet/workspace-admin) the agent uses when it interacts with apps and services. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/agent-identity#agent-identity
- [definition] Fixed credentials ("Claws") — The agent always authenticates with the same API keys and OAuth tokens, regardless of who is interacting with it. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/agent-identity#fixed-credentials-claws
- [definition] User credentials ("Assistants") — The agent authenticates with the API keys and OAuth tokens of the user interacting with it, acting on the user's behalf. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/agent-identity#user-credentials-assistants

## Computer use
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use>

- [parameter] **Shared computer**: All threads share a single computer. The filesystem, installed packages, and running processes persist across threads. Choose this mode when you want files, dependencies, or environment setup to accumulate across conversations. Shared computers are not deleted automatically. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#computer-modes
- [parameter] **Computer per thread**: Each thread gets its own isolated computer that starts fresh and is archived when it goes idle. Choose this mode for software-engineering agents and other workloads that run many parallel, write-heavy tasks, or for any case where threads should not see each other's state. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#computer-modes
- [definition] Computer use — Computer use gives your Fleet agent access to an isolated virtual computer. The agent can write and execute code, manage files, install packages, and call authenticated external APIs without exposing credentials to the language model. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#computer-use
- [definition] Computer modes — Choose how the virtual computer is shared across an agent's conversation threads: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#computer-modes
- [definition] Configure computer use — The computer mode is set when the agent is created and cannot be changed afterward. To switch modes, create a new agent. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#configure-computer-use
- [definition] Open the Create agent dialog — In the [Fleet](https://smith.langchain.com/agents?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-fleet-computer-use) left navigation, under **My Agents**, click <Icon icon="plus" /> and select either **Create with AI** or **Blank agent**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#configure-computer-use
- [definition] Enable computer use — Under **Should your agent use a computer?**, select **Yes**, then choose **Shared computer** or **Computer per thread**. If you select **No** (the default), the agent is created with no computer access. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#configure-computer-use
- [definition] Set the base snapshot (optional) — Expand **Advanced** to choose a **Snapshot** for new computers. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#configure-computer-use
- [definition] Access profiles — Use access profiles to let your agent call authenticated external APIs without putting credentials in the prompt or exposing them to the language model. Outbound HTTP requests to matching hosts are routed through a proxy that injects the configured headers before forwarding. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#access-profiles
- [definition] Create the access profile — Go to the [Fleet Integrations tab](https://smith.langchain.com/agents/tools) and navigate to the **Computer** section. Click **+ Create profile** and follow the prompts to configure the host patterns and credentials. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#add-an-access-profile
- [definition] Attach the profile to an agent — In the agent editor, click the **Computer** node. Click **+ Add** next to **Access profiles** and select the profile you created. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#add-an-access-profile
- [definition] Computer lifecycle — Each agent has two lifecycle settings that control how long a computer stays active and how long it is kept after it stops. [Configure both in the settings popover](#configure-lifecycle-and-snapshot). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#computer-lifecycle
- [definition] Base snapshot — A snapshot is the disk image used to boot the computer. By default, all Fleet agents use the workspace default snapshot. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#base-snapshot
- [definition] Configure lifecycle and snapshot — The snapshot, idle timeout, and stopped computer cleanup for an agent are all set in the **Computer lifecycle** section of the settings popover. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#configure-lifecycle-and-snapshot
- [definition] Open the settings popover — In [Fleet](https://smith.langchain.com/agents?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-fleet-computer-use), open the agent and click the <Icon icon="settings" /> settings icon in the agent editor. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#configure-lifecycle-and-snapshot
- [definition] Set the lifecycle fields — Scroll to the **Computer lifecycle** section. Set the **Snapshot**, **Idle timeout**, and, for **Computer per thread** mode, **Stopped computer cleanup**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/computer-use#configure-lifecycle-and-snapshot

## Essentials
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials>

- [parameter] **Fast**: Best for=Everyday tasks such as research, summaries, and drafting; <Tooltip tip="Higher tiers typically cost more and take longer.">Relative cost</Tooltip>=Low — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#models
- [parameter] **Pro**: Best for=More complex tasks that benefit from stronger reasoning; <Tooltip tip="Higher tiers typically cost more and take longer.">Relative cost</Tooltip>=Medium — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#models
- [parameter] **Max**: Best for=The most demanding tasks, where maximum capability matters most; <Tooltip tip="Higher tiers typically cost more and take longer.">Relative cost</Tooltip>=High — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#models
- [definition] Essentials — LangSmith Fleet essentials are the core features that make up the foundation of your agents. They include tools, channels, memory, sub-agents, and approvals. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#essentials
- [definition] Agent identity — Agent identity controls whose [credentials](/langsmith/fleet/workspace-admin) the agent uses when it interacts with apps and services. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#agent-identity
- [definition] Agent sidebar — Configure your agent from the sidebar built into the agent chat page. The sidebar organizes agent configuration into drawers: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#agent-sidebar
- [definition] Channels — Channels define when your agent should start running. You can connect your agent to external tools or time-based schedules, letting it respond automatically to messages, emails, or recurring events. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#channels
- [definition] Human-in-the-loop — Stay in control of important decisions. You can set up your agent to pause and ask for your approval before taking certain actions. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#human-in-the-loop
- [definition] Set an approval mode — Each tool has an approval mode you can set in the **Connections** drawer of the [agent sidebar](#agent-sidebar): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#set-an-approval-mode
- [definition] What you can do when your agent pauses — When your agent stops to ask for approval, you have two options: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#what-you-can-do-when-your-agent-pauses
- [definition] Instructions — Instructions are the system prompt that defines your agent's behavior, personality, and capabilities. They guide how the agent interprets requests, uses its tools, and responds to users. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#instructions
- [definition] LangChain Compute Units (LCUs) — Fleet usage is measured in LangChain Compute Units (LCUs). LCU usage is based on the [model](#models) work your agent performs, including the selected tier and the amount of content it processes and generates. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#langchain-compute-units-lcus
- [definition] Memory — Agents remember important information from previous conversations and can update themselves to work better. Fleet agents use two sources of memory: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#memory
- [definition] Models — Fleet manages models for you. It selects and maintains a strong model for each task, so you get good results without having to choose a provider, configure a model, or supply an API key. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#models
- [definition] Custom models — Custom models are not available alongside Fast, Pro, and Max in the managed Fleet model picker. LangChain manages model-provider access for the managed tiers, so you do not need your own model-provider API key. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#custom-models
- [definition] Self-updates — Agents can update themselves: they can add new tools, remove ones they don't need, or adjust their instructions. However, agents can't change their name, description, or the channels that start them. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#self-updates
- [definition] Skills — Skills are a way to bundle capabilities and provide more specific information in situations where the context is not universally relevant. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#skills
- [definition] Sub-agents — Build complex agents by breaking big tasks into smaller, specialized helpers. Think of sub-agents as a team of specialists, each one handling a specific part of the job while working with your main agent. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#sub-agents
- [definition] Threads — Threads are conversations between you and your agent. Each thread contains messages, agent responses, and any actions the agent takes. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#threads
- [definition] Read and unread status — How threads are marked depends on whether the agent uses channels: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#read-and-unread-status
- [definition] Tools — Tools let your agents interact with your apps and services. Your agents can send emails, create calendar events, post messages, search the web, and more. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#tools
- [definition] Traces — Traces are a series of steps that your agent takes to go from input to output. You can use [LangSmith](/langsmith/observability) to visualize these execution steps. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials#traces

## Quickstart
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart>

- [definition] Quickstart — By the end of this quickstart, you will have an Executive Assistant that labels the Gmail messages needing your attention and pauses for approval before acting, all set up without code or a model API key and controlled through chat. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#quickstart
- [definition] Before you start — You need: - A LangSmith account ([sign up here](https://smith.langchain.com/agents?skipOnboarding=true&utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-fleet-quickstart)). - A Gmail account. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#before-you-start
- [definition] Navigate to Fleet — 1. In the [LangSmith UI](https://smith.langchain.com?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-fleet-quickstart), click <Icon icon="pointer"/> **Switch to Fleet** at the top of the left-hand navigation. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#1-create-your-agent
- [definition] Choose a template — 1. Select **Templates** in the left-hand navigation, or click **+** in **My Agents** and select **From template**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#1-create-your-agent
- [definition] Skip channel setup for now — When the agent prompts you to connect a channel, click **Skip for now**. You connect channels in a [later step](#3-configure-your-agent). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#1-create-your-agent
- [definition] Answer onboarding questions — Provide information so your agent knows how to work the way you prefer. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#1-create-your-agent
- [definition] 2. Connect tools — Your agent asks you to connect to your Gmail and Google Calendar accounts. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#2-connect-tools
- [definition] Connect Gmail — 1. In the **Gmail** row, click **Connect** on the right. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#2-connect-tools
- [definition] Connect Google Calendar — 1. Connecting Gmail authorized your Google account for Gmail only, not Google Calendar. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#2-connect-tools
- [definition] 3. Configure your agent — There are two ways to configure your agent: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#3-configure-your-agent
- [definition] Open the agent sidebar — Click **<Icon icon="settings"/> Configure** at the top right to open the agent sidebar. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#3-configure-your-agent
- [definition] View connections — Expand the **Connections** drawer. **Gmail** and **Google Calendar** appear as **Connected**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#3-configure-your-agent
- [definition] Configure a tool to ask for approval — In the **Connections** drawer, click **Gmail** to view the available tools. By default, the tools are enabled and set to **Auto**, so they run without your approval. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#3-configure-your-agent
- [definition] Connect channels — Expand the **Channels** drawer. Click **Gmail**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#3-configure-your-agent
- [definition] Save your changes — Click **Save** at the top of the sidebar to save your changes, then click **X** to close the panel. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#3-configure-your-agent
- [definition] Send your agent a task — In the agent chat, try out the Executive Assistant, for example: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#4-test-your-agent
- [definition] Accept or reject the agent's action — Click **Accept** to approve the agent's proposed action or tell the agent what it did wrong and click **Reject**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#4-test-your-agent
- [definition] Check your inbox in Gmail — If you clicked **Accept**, emails that need review now have the **Review** label in your inbox. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#4-test-your-agent
- [definition] Edit your agent — You may want to update your agent's instructions or include more tools. You can chat with your agent directly to ask for updates, or configure it from the [agent sidebar](/langsmith/fleet/essentials#agent-sidebar): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/quickstart#edit-your-agent

## Salesforce integration
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce>

- [definition] Salesforce integration — The Salesforce integration gives your agents read-only access to data in your Salesforce org. Once connected, an agent can: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#salesforce-integration
- [definition] Register the connector — The first connection attempt registers the **LangChain Fleet Connector** in your Salesforce org so that an administrator can install it. This initial attempt is expected to fail with an authentication error. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#register-the-connector
- [definition] Open the Integrations page — In the [LangSmith UI](https://smith.langchain.com?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-fleet-salesforce), navigate to the [**Fleet** > **Integrations**](https://smith.langchain.com/agents/tools) tab. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#register-the-connector
- [definition] Start the Salesforce connection — Find the **Salesforce** tool and click **Connect**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#register-the-connector
- [definition] Sign in to Salesforce — Sign in with your Salesforce credentials. If your org requires a custom domain or SSO, click **Use Custom Domain** and enter your org's My Domain before signing in. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#register-the-connector
- [definition] Install the connector — This step must be completed by a Salesforce System Administrator. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#install-the-connector
- [definition] Open Salesforce Setup — In Salesforce, click the <Icon icon="settings"/> gear icon and select **Setup**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#install-the-connector
- [definition] Open Connected Apps OAuth Usage — In the **Quick Find** box, type `Connected Apps OAuth Usage` and open the page. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#install-the-connector
- [definition] Install the connector — 1. Find **LangChain Fleet Connector** in the list. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#install-the-connector
- [definition] Grant user access — Granting access through a permission set is the recommended way to control which users can authenticate with Fleet. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#grant-user-access
- [definition] Open the app policies — From **Connected Apps OAuth Usage**, click **Manage App Policies** next to **LangChain Fleet Connector**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#grant-user-access
- [definition] Pre-authorize admin-approved users — Under **OAuth Policies** > **Permitted Users**, select **Admin approved users are pre-authorized**, then click **Save**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#grant-user-access
- [definition] Assign a permission set — Use **Manage Permission Sets** to grant access to the users who need to connect the Salesforce tool in Fleet. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#grant-user-access
- [definition] Connect from Fleet — Once your administrator has installed the connector and granted access, return to Fleet to complete the connection. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#connect-from-fleet
- [definition] Use Salesforce with an agent — After connecting, add Salesforce tools to a specific agent: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#use-salesforce-with-an-agent
- [definition] Connection fails with an authentication error — The first connection attempt is expected to fail. It registers the **LangChain Fleet Connector** in your Salesforce org so an administrator can install it. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#connection-fails-with-an-authentication-error
- [definition] Agent cannot see an object or field — Salesforce tools run with the permissions of the connected user. If an agent cannot read an object or custom field, verify that the user's Salesforce profile and permission sets grant read access to that object. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/salesforce#agent-cannot-see-an-object-or-field

## Skills
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills>

- [snippet] Use Fleet skills in local development: langsmith fleet skills pull [skill-name] [flags] — `langsmith fleet skills pull [skill-name] [flags]` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#use-fleet-skills-in-local-development
- [snippet] Use Fleet skills in local development: $ langsmith fleet skills pull web-research --format pretty — `$ langsmith fleet skills pull web-research --format pretty` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#use-fleet-skills-in-local-development
- [parameter] `--global=false`: Install to project-level directories (`.agents/` and `.claude/`) instead of the home directory. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#use-fleet-skills-in-local-development
- [parameter] `--agent`: Target a specific agent (`claude`, `cursor`, `codex`). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#use-fleet-skills-in-local-development
- [parameter] `--copy`: Copy files instead of symlinking. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#use-fleet-skills-in-local-development
- [parameter] `--format pretty`: Display the installed skill's file tree. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#use-fleet-skills-in-local-development
- [definition] Skills — Skills are reusable capabilities that provide specialized workflows and domain knowledge to your agent. Each skill is stored in the agent's long-term memory at `memories/skills/<skill-name>`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#skills
- [definition] Private vs. shared skills — Skills can be **private** to a single agent or **shared** across a workspace: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#private-vs-shared-skills
- [definition] Write effective skill descriptions — Write the description as instructions for when to use the skill, not as a label for what it does. The agent routes tasks based on the description alone. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#write-effective-skill-descriptions
- [definition] Fix recurring mistakes — The default response to an agent mistake is to correct it in the moment. A skill changes this: it gives the agent explicit rules to follow every time it encounters that class of task, so the same mistake cannot happen again. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#fix-recurring-mistakes
- [definition] Edit a private skill — 1. Select an agent in [Fleet](https://smith.langchain.com/agents?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-fleet-skills). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#edit-a-private-skill
- [definition] Edit a shared skill — Only the user who created the shared skill can edit it. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#edit-a-shared-skill
- [definition] Share a skill — 1. Select an agent in [Fleet](https://smith.langchain.com/agents?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-fleet-skills). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#share-a-skill
- [definition] Delete a private skill — Deleting a private skill removes it permanently, since it is stored in that agent's memory. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#delete-a-private-skill
- [definition] Delete a shared skill — Only the user who created the shared skill can delete it. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#delete-a-shared-skill
- [definition] Use Fleet skills in local development — Download skills from your Fleet workspace with the LangSmith CLI and install them locally for use in coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/skills#use-fleet-skills-in-local-development

- [definition] Step 1. Connect the Fleet Slack manager — The Fleet Slack app acts as a manager for your workspace. A single connection grants two things: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/slack-app#step-1-connect-the-fleet-slack-manager
- [definition] Add Slack to the agent — In [Fleet](https://smith.langchain.com/agents?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-fleet-slack-app), select your agent and open its configuration sidebar. - [definition] Set up Slack on Self-hosted — Self-hosted deployments do not use the Fleet Slack manager. - [definition] Step 1. Set up the Slack OAuth provider — Every self-hosted instance needs this one-time setup before agents can use Slack. - [definition] Configure Helm — Choose a provider ID, for example `slack-oauth-provider`. - [definition] Register the provider in LangSmith — Copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret** from **Basic Information** in your Slack app. In LangSmith, go to **Settings > OAuth Providers** and add a provider: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/slack-app#step-1-set-up-the-slack-oauth-provider
- [definition] Add the redirect URI to Slack — In the Slack app, go to **OAuth & Permissions > Redirect URLs** and add the following, replacing `<hostname>` with your LangSmith hostname and `<provider-id>` with your provider ID: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/slack-app#step-1-set-up-the-slack-oauth-provider
- [definition] Step 2. Create a custom Slack app — Start this flow from the agent you want the bot to run, so Fleet links the app for you when you finish. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/slack-app#step-2-create-a-custom-slack-app
- [definition] Open the Slack setup dialog — Select your agent and open its configuration sidebar. Expand the **Channels** drawer and select **Slack**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/slack-app#step-2-create-a-custom-slack-app

- [definition] Enter your app credentials — Back in Fleet, click **Continue To Credentials** and copy the following values from your new Slack app: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/slack-app#step-2-create-a-custom-slack-app

- [definition] Finish a draft Slack app — Clicking **Save & Request Approval** saves the app as a draft, so you keep your progress while a Slack admin reviews the install request.
