- [definition] Use your agent in Slack — Once the app is installed, invite the agent to a channel, tag it to start a run, and respond to approval requests without leaving Slack. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/slack-app#use-your-agent-in-slack
- [definition] Invite the agent to a channel — 1. In Slack, go to the channel where you want to use the agent. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/slack-app#invite-the-agent-to-a-channel
- [definition] Approve or deny actions in Slack — When an agent pauses on a tool that requires approval, it raises the request directly in Slack. - [definition] Error messages in Slack — If an agent encounters an error during a run, it replies in the Slack thread instead of going silent. - [definition] Add Slack tools — Slack tools let your agent send messages, reply in threads, read history, and send direct messages. - [definition] Agent does not respond — If your agent is not responding, try the following: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/slack-app#agent-does-not-respond
- [definition] Not allowed to tag the bot — If you receive a private message saying you are not allowed to tag the bot, your Slack ID is not authorized for that agent. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/slack-app#not-allowed-to-tag-the-bot
- [definition] Slack app stays pending approval — A Slack row that stays in the pending state is waiting on a Slack admin. Ask an admin to approve the app in Slack, then click **Finish setup** again. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/slack-app#slack-app-stays-pending-approval
- [definition] Add Slack App is disabled — On Self-hosted, the **Add Slack App** button in the **Slack Apps** section is disabled until `fleet.oauth.slackOAuthProvider` is set. ## Templates
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/templates>

- [definition] Templates — LangSmith Fleet includes [starter templates](https://www.langchain.com/templates) to help you create agents quickly. Templates include predefined instructions, [tools](/langsmith/fleet/tools), and [channels](/langsmith/fleet/essentials#channels) (if applicable) for common use cases. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/templates#templates
- [definition] Features — Templates are pre-configured agents designed for specific use cases. Each template includes the following components: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/templates#features
- [definition] Pre-configured tools — Templates come with a curated set of [tools](/langsmith/fleet/essentials#tools) that enable the agent to perform specific actions. For example, an email assistant template includes tools for reading, sending, and organizing emails. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/templates#pre-configured-tools
- [definition] System instructions — Each template includes a _system prompt_ (also called _instructions_) that defines the agent's behavior, personality, and capabilities. The system prompt guides how the agent interprets user requests and uses its available tools. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/templates#system-instructions
- [definition] Channels (optional) — Some templates include [channels](/langsmith/fleet/essentials#channels) that allow agents to respond to external events automatically. For example, a Slack bot template might include a channel that activates when someone mentions the agent in a Slack conversation. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/templates#channels-optional
- [definition] Cloning and customization — Templates serve as starting points that you clone to create your own agent. When you clone a template, you create an independent copy that you can customize without affecting the original. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/templates#cloning-and-customization

- [parameter] `json`: JSON editor. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/webhooks#custom-input-fields
- [parameter] `select`: Dropdown with predefined options. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/webhooks#custom-input-fields
- [definition] Fleet webhooks — When triggered, a webhook sends a complete package of your agent's configuration and files to the specified endpoint. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/webhooks#fleet-webhooks
- [definition] Add a webhook — 1. Navigate to [Settings > Fleet webhooks](https://smith.langchain.com/settings/workspaces/agent-builder-webhooks). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/webhooks#add-a-webhook

- [parameter] Up to 31 days: Aggregation=Daily; Stride=`days: 1` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#stride
- [parameter] 32–93 days (~3 months): Aggregation=Weekly; Stride=`days: 7` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#stride
- [parameter] 94–366 days (~1 year): Aggregation=Monthly; Stride=`days: 30` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#stride
- [parameter] More than 366 days: Aggregation=Yearly; Stride=`days: 365` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#stride
- [parameter] `nodes_executed`: Total LangGraph nodes executed in the time bucket. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#response
- [parameter] `agent_runs`: Total agent runs (graph invocations) in the time bucket. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#response
- [parameter] `agent_uptime_seconds`: Total replica uptime, in seconds, summed across deployment replicas. The deduplicated standby minutes used for invoicing is computed separately by the billing pipeline; this field is the raw sum surfaced for breakdown and analysis. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#response
- [parameter] Time Bucket Start: Always — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#csv-export
- [parameter] Time Bucket End: Always — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#csv-export
- [parameter] Workspace ID / Name: Always (populated when `group_by=workspace`) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#csv-export
- [parameter] Project ID / Name: Always (populated when `group_by=project`) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#csv-export
- [parameter] User ID / Email: Always (populated when `group_by=user`) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#csv-export
- [parameter] API Key Short Key: Always (populated when `group_by=api_key`) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#csv-export
- [parameter] Traces: `kind=traces` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#csv-export

- [definition] Day-granular contract — Usage data is aggregated at day granularity. The endpoint normalizes the window to whole days at the API layer: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#day-granular-contract
- [definition] Stride — The `stride` field in each response indicates the time bucket size used for aggregation, calculated from the requested time range. Daily is the minimum. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#stride
- [definition] Compatibility — `kind=langsmith_deployments` combined with `group_by=trace_tier` returns `400 Bad Request`. Retention tiers only apply to traces. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/granular-usage#compatibility

- [parameter] `access_context`: Type=`str`; Description=Why the factory was called: `"threads.create_run"`, `"threads.update"`, `"threads.read"`, or `"assistants.read"`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#serverruntime-reference
- [parameter] `user`: Type=`BaseUser \| None`; Description=The authenticated user, or `None` if no [custom auth](/langsmith/custom-auth) is configured. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#serverruntime-reference
- [parameter] `store`: Type=`BaseStore`; Description=The store instance for persistence and memory. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#serverruntime-reference
- [parameter] `ensure_user()`: Returns the authenticated user. Raises `PermissionError` if no user is provided. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#serverruntime-reference
- [parameter] `execution_runtime`: Returns the execution runtime when `access_context` is `"threads.create_run"`, or `None` otherwise. Use this to conditionally set up expensive resources only during execution. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#serverruntime-reference
- [parameter] `threads.create_run`: Full graph execution. `execution_runtime` is available. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#access-contexts
- [parameter] `threads.update`: State update via `aupdate_state`. Does not execute node functions, but it can change the pending tasks. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#access-contexts
- [parameter] `threads.read`: State reads via `aget_state` / `aget_state_history`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#access-contexts
- [parameter] `assistants.read`: Schema and graph introspection for visualization, MCP, A2A, etc. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#access-contexts
- [definition] Rebuild graph at runtime — You might need to rebuild your graph with a different configuration for a new run. For example, you might want to load different tools depending on the user's credentials. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#rebuild-graph-at-runtime
- [definition] Define graphs — Let's say you have an app with a simple graph that calls an LLM and returns the response to the user. The app file directory looks like the following: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#define-graphs
- [definition] No rebuild — The most common way to deploy your Agent Server is to reference a compiled graph instance that's defined at the top level of your file. An example is below: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#no-rebuild
- [definition] Rebuild — To rebuild your graph on each new run, provide a **factory function** that returns (or yields) a graph. The factory can optionally accept a `ServerRuntime` parameter or a `RunnableConfig`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#rebuild
- [definition] ServerRuntime reference — Your factory function receives a `ServerRuntime` instance with the following attributes: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#serverruntime-reference
- [definition] Access contexts — The server calls your factory in several contexts beyond just executing runs. In all contexts, the returned graph should have the **same topology** (nodes, edges, state schema). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#access-contexts
- [definition] Customize tracing per graph — You can use the factory function to customize or disable tracing for a specific graph. See [Conditional tracing: Customize tracing in deployed agents](/langsmith/conditional-tracing#customize-tracing-in-deployed-agents) for examples. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/graph-rebuild#customize-tracing-per-graph

## How to handle model rate limits
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/handle-model-rate-limiting>

- [snippet] Using `langchain` RateLimiters (Python only): from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model — `from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/handle-model-rate-limiting#using-langchain-ratelimiters-python-only
- [snippet] Python: from langchain import init_chat_model — `from langchain import init_chat_model` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/handle-model-rate-limiting#with-langchain
- [snippet] TypeScript: import { initChatModel } from "langchain"; — `import { initChatModel } from "langchain";` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/handle-model-rate-limiting#with-langchain
- [snippet] Python: from langsmith import aevaluate — `from langsmith import aevaluate` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/handle-model-rate-limiting#limiting-max-concurrency
- [snippet] TypeScript: import { evaluate } from "langsmith/evaluation"; — `import { evaluate } from "langsmith/evaluation";` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/handle-model-rate-limiting#limiting-max-concurrency
- [definition] How to handle model rate limits — A common issue when running large evaluation jobs is running into third-party API rate limits, usually from model providers. There are a few ways to deal with rate limits. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/handle-model-rate-limiting#how-to-handle-model-rate-limits
- [definition] Using `langchain` RateLimiters (Python only) — If you're using `langchain` Python chat models in your application or evaluators, you can add rate limiters to your model(s) that will add client-side control of the frequency with which requests are sent to the model provider API to avoid rate limit errors. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/handle-model-rate-limiting#using-langchain-ratelimiters-python-only
- [definition] Retrying with exponential backoff — A very common way to deal with rate limit errors is retrying with exponential backoff. Retrying with exponential backoff means repeatedly retrying failed requests with an (exponentially) increasing wait time between each retry. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/handle-model-rate-limiting#retrying-with-exponential-backoff
- [definition] Limiting `max_concurrency` — Limiting the number of concurrent calls you're making to your application and evaluators is another way to decrease the frequency of model calls you're making, and in that way avoid rate limit errors. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/handle-model-rate-limiting#limiting-max-concurrency

- [definition] Name — `name` is required. Pass a static string that starts with a letter and contains only letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens, such as `"research-assistant"`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-agent-definition#name

- [definition] Tools — Pass tools in the `tools` array to let the agent call application logic or external services. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-agent-definition#tools
- [definition] Middleware — Pass middleware in the `middleware` array to add behavior around model calls, tool calls, and the agent lifecycle. Middleware runs in array order. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-agent-definition#middleware
- [definition] Subagents — Pass subagent definitions in `subagents` when the agent should delegate specialized or context-heavy work. Each subagent can have its own prompt, model, and tools. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-agent-definition#subagents
- [definition] Permissions — Pass filesystem permission rules in `permissions` to control which paths the agent's built-in filesystem tools can read or write. See [Permissions](/oss/javascript/deepagents/permissions). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-agent-definition#permissions
- [definition] Human-in-the-loop — Set `interruptOn` to pause before selected tool calls. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-agent-definition#human-in-the-loop
- [definition] Structured output — Set `responseFormat` when the agent must return data that matches a schema instead of an unconstrained text response. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-agent-definition#structured-output

- [definition] Deploy your agent — Run the deployment command from the project root: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-channels-slack#deploy-the-agent
- [definition] Authorize Slack if prompted — If you haven't authorized LangSmith before, the CLI displays an HTTPS authorization link. - [definition] Use the agent in Slack — After the first deployment, your agent sends you a direct message in Slack. Reply to the message to start an agent run. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-channels-slack#deploy-the-agent

## Connect Managed Deep Agents to channels
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-channels>

- [definition] Connect Managed Deep Agents to channels — A channel makes a managed deep agent available in an external messaging service. - [definition] Understand channels — A channel combines three parts of an external messaging integration: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-channels#understand-channels
- [definition] Declare channels in a project — Put each channel in a separate module under `channels/`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-channels#declare-channels-in-a-project
- [definition] Distinguish channels from connectors — A channel receives messages that start agent runs and delivers responses. An [MCP connector](/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-mcp-connectors) gives the agent tools from a remote MCP server. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-channels#distinguish-channels-from-connectors

- [parameter] `--identity`: Add managed authentication with user-owned threads. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-cli#initialize-projects
- [parameter] `--memory agent\|none`: Optionally write a root memory declaration. If omitted, no memory file is created and durable memory is off. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-cli#initialize-projects
- [parameter] `--model SPEC`: Model the agent runs on, as `provider:model`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-cli#initialize-projects
- [parameter] `--no-sandbox`: Leave out the managed sandbox declaration. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-cli#initialize-projects

- [parameter] Both or neither: Interactive language prompt. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-cli#initialize-projects
- [parameter] `agent.ts`: Named `agent` export from `defineDeepAgent(...)`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-cli#initialize-projects
- [parameter] `instructions.md`: Managed system prompt. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-cli#initialize-projects

- [parameter] `--hostname HOSTNAME`: Forward a host to the LangGraph dev server. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-cli#develop-locally
- [parameter] `--no-browser`: Prevent the dev server from opening Studio in a browser when it starts. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-cli#develop-locally
- [parameter] `--no-reload`: Disable the dev server's hot reload. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-cli#develop-locally

- [parameter] `path`: Project directory. Defaults to the current directory. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-cli#deploy-projects

- [parameter] `prefix_tool_name_with_server_name` / `prefixToolNameWithServerName`: Default=`true`; Description=Prefix each tool with `{server}__`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-mcp-connectors#configure-connections
- [parameter] `throw_on_load_error` / `throwOnLoadError`: Default=`true`; Description=Fail loading instead of starting with a partial tool set. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-mcp-connectors#configure-connections

- [parameter] `defaultTimeout`: Default=`600`; Description=Seconds allowed for each command. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-sandboxes#configure-a-sandbox

- [definition] Add a sandbox to Managed Deep Agents — Agents often want to write or execute code when doing their job. A sandbox gives a managed deep agent an isolated filesystem and shell for working with files, running code, and executing commands. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-sandboxes#add-a-sandbox-to-managed-deep-agents
- [definition] Project structure — Keep the agent entry point at the project root and the sandbox declaration under `sandbox/`. Add `sandbox/setup.sh` only if you want to provision a snapshot: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-sandboxes#project-structure
- [definition] Configure a sandbox — `mda init` scaffolds a sandbox declaration. Managed Deep Agents enables the sandbox only while the `sandbox/` directory is present. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-sandboxes#configure-a-sandbox
- [definition] Provision a snapshot — If `sandbox/setup.sh` exists, `mda deploy` and `mda dev` run the script once and save the resulting environment as a snapshot. Modifications from that run, such as cloned repositories and installed packages, persist in the snapshot. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-sandboxes#provision-a-snapshot
- [definition] Choose a bake base — With no bake base, LangSmith's default sandbox template is the starting point. To start from something else, set exactly one of these: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-sandboxes#choose-a-bake-base
- [definition] How the agent uses the sandbox — The agent uses filesystem tools such as `ls`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `delete`, `glob`, and `grep`, and runs shell commands with `execute`. Use `instructions.md` to specify where the agent should work and what it must not modify. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-sandboxes#how-the-agent-uses-the-sandbox
- [definition] Sandbox lifecycle — Managed Deep Agents owns sandbox naming, recipe bake, reuse, recovery, and cleanup. Each durable thread gets its own sandbox, cloned from the current recipe snapshot. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-sandboxes#sandbox-lifecycle

- [definition] How skills compare to other concepts — Skills is context that is loaded dynamically, when the agent chooses to. The agent cannot modify them. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/javascript/managed-deep-agents-skills#how-skills-compare-to-other-concepts

- [definition] LangSmith CLI — The LangSmith CLI is a command-line tool for querying and managing your LangSmith data. It's designed for both developers and AI coding agents and outputs human-readable tables by default, with a `--format json` option for scripting. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#langsmith-cli
- [definition] Authenticate — `langsmith auth login` requires LangSmith CLI `v0.2.30` or later. `langsmith profile` commands require LangSmith CLI `v0.2.26` or later. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#authenticate
- [definition] Self-hosted instances — Point the CLI at your instance with `--api-url`, or with `LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT`. Both the browser-based login and API keys are supported. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#self-hosted-instances
- [definition] Quickstart — The following commands cover the core resource types: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#quickstart
- [definition] Commands — Each command group targets a specific LangSmith resource. Most commands support `--limit`, `--offset`, and a shared set of [filter flags](#filter-flags). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#commands
- [definition] List projects — Returns up to 20 projects by default, sorted by most recent activity. Lists tracing projects only. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#list-projects
- [definition] Query traces — Defaults to the last 7 days, newest first. Use `--since` or `--last-n-minutes` to change the time window. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#query-traces
- [definition] Query runs — Defaults to 50 results (most other commands default to 20). The same 7-day time window applies. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#query-runs
- [definition] Query threads — `--project` is required for all thread commands. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#query-threads
- [definition] Manage datasets — `dataset export` exports the examples (rows) within a dataset, not the dataset metadata itself. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#manage-datasets
- [definition] Manage examples — Use `--split` to assign examples to named splits (such as `test` or `train`) when creating or listing. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#manage-examples
- [definition] Manage evaluators — Evaluators can be offline (run against a dataset during experiments) or online (run against a live project). Use `--sampling-rate` to evaluate only a fraction of production runs, and `--replace` to overwrite an existing evaluator by name. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#manage-evaluators
- [definition] View experiments — `experiment list` shows evaluation experiments, not tracing projects. (Use [`project list`](#list-projects) to list tracing projects.) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#view-experiments
- [definition] Manage sandboxes — Sandbox commands let you build snapshots, create sandboxes, execute commands, open interactive consoles, and tunnel TCP ports to services running inside sandboxes. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#manage-sandboxes
- [definition] Call the LangSmith API directly — The `api` command is an authenticated, scriptable wrapper around the raw LangSmith REST API — useful for endpoints the typed commands above don't cover, or for piping JSON into and out of shell scripts. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#call-the-langsmith-api-directly
- [definition] Filter flags — Most `trace` and `run` commands share these filters: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-cli#filter-flags

- [definition] Configure your collector for LangSmith telemetry — The various services in a LangSmith deployment emit telemetry data in the form of logs, metrics, and traces. You may already have telemetry collectors set up in your Kubernetes cluster, or would like to deploy one to monitor your application. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-collector#configure-your-collector-for-langsmith-telemetry
- [definition] Logs — This is an example for a ***Sidecar*** collector to read logs from its own pod, excluding logs from non domain-specific containers. A Sidecar configuration is useful here because we require access to every container's filesystem. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-collector#logs
- [definition] Metrics — Metrics can be scraped using the Prometheus endpoints. A single instance ***Gateway*** collector can be used to avoid duplication of queries when fetching metrics. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-collector#metrics
- [definition] Traces — For traces, you need to enable the OTLP receiver. The following configuration can be used to listen to HTTP traces on port 4318, and GRPC on port 4317: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-collector#traces
- [definition] Recommended OTEL processors — The following processors are recommended when using the OTel collector: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-collector#recommended-otel-processors
- [definition] Exporters — Exporters just need to point to an external endpoint of your liking. The following configuration allows you to configure a separate endpoint for logs, metrics and traces: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-collector#exporters

- [snippet] Cursor: { — `{` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#cursor

- [snippet] AI SDK: import { createMCPClient } from "@ai-sdk/mcp"; — `import { createMCPClient } from "@ai-sdk/mcp";` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#ai-sdk
- [snippet] Enabling Remote MCP: step crypto jwk create /dev/null /tmp/jwk.json --kty OKP --crv Ed25519 --no-password --insecure -f — `step crypto jwk create /dev/null /tmp/jwk.json --kty OKP --crv Ed25519 --no-password --insecure -f` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#enabling-remote-mcp
- [snippet] Enabling Remote MCP: config: — `config:` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#enabling-remote-mcp
- [snippet] Enabling Remote MCP: curl https://<your-langsmith-host>/api/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp — `curl https://<your-langsmith-host>/api/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#enabling-remote-mcp
- [definition] LangSmith Remote MCP — The LangSmith Remote MCP is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) (MCP) server hosted by LangSmith. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#langsmith-remote-mcp
- [definition] Authentication — The Remote MCP supports two authentication methods. Use **OAuth** for interactive MCP clients (Claude Code, Cursor, and similar), and an **API key** for programmatic or headless clients that can't complete a browser-based login. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#authentication
- [definition] OAuth — OAuth 2.1 with [Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591) is the default for interactive clients. Compatible MCP clients register themselves automatically on first use—there is no client ID to provision and no API key to manage. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#oauth
- [definition] API key — Send a [LangSmith API key](/langsmith/create-account-api-key) in the `X-Api-Key` header on every request. This suits backend services, scripts, and SDKs, for example, the [AI SDK](#ai-sdk), where the interactive OAuth flow is not practical. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#api-key
- [definition] Claude Code — Add the server to your project's `.mcp.json` (or run `claude mcp add --transport http -s user langsmith https://api.smith.langchain.com/mcp` to install it user-wide): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#claude-code
- [definition] Deep Agents Code (`dcode`) — Add the server to your user-level `~/.deepagents/.mcp.json` file to make it available in every Deep Agents Code project, or add it to a project-level `.mcp.json` file for only that project. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#deep-agents-code-dcode
- [definition] LangSmith CLI — The [LangSmith CLI](/langsmith/langsmith-cli) authenticates against this same OAuth server, so `langsmith auth login` logs you in via the OAuth device flow—no API key required: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#langsmith-cli
- [definition] AI SDK — For programmatic use from the [AI SDK](https://ai-sdk.dev/), authenticate with an API key via the `X-Api-Key` header and the built-in `http` (Streamable HTTP) transport: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#ai-sdk
- [definition] Other clients — Any MCP client supporting the [Streamable HTTP transport](https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/transports/#streamable-http) can connect with just the URL above—using OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, or a LangSmith API key in the `X-Api-Key` header. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#other-clients
- [definition] Available tools — The Remote MCP exposes the same tool surface as the [standalone server](/langsmith/langsmith-mcp-server#available-tools): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#available-tools
- [definition] Re-authenticating — If a client loses its session (for example, after revoking access in your LangSmith account, or if the refresh token is invalidated), trigger re-auth from the client: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#re-authenticating
- [definition] Self-hosted LangSmith — [Self-hosted LangSmith](/langsmith/self-hosted) deployments on v0.16 or later expose the Remote MCP at `https://<your-langsmith-host>/api/mcp`. Once enabled, authentication and the tool surface are identical to LangSmith Cloud. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#self-hosted-langsmith
- [definition] Enabling Remote MCP — The Remote MCP and its OAuth Authorization Server are wired automatically when `config.hostname` is set, but they stay **inert (404)** until you provide a signing JWKS. This is the one piece of configuration LangSmith Cloud handles for you. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/langsmith-remote-mcp#enabling-remote-mcp

## How to define an LLM-as-a-judge evaluator

- [parameter] `ls_user_id`: LangSmith user ID (present only when `actor_type` is `user`) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#jwt-claims-reference
- [definition] Set up the LLM auth proxy — The LLM auth proxy lets your organization enforce its own authentication flows for all model invocations from LangSmith so that provider credentials are never exposed to end users and every request is traceable back to a specific actor. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#set-up-the-llm-auth-proxy
- [definition] How it works — Each request from LangSmith passes through the following steps in the proxy: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#how-it-works
- [definition] 1. Configure JWT signing (self-hosted LangSmith only) — Skip this step for LangSmith SaaS. JWT signing is already configured. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#1-configure-jwt-signing-self-hosted-langsmith-only
- [definition] 3. Configure organization settings in LangSmith — In the LangSmith UI, navigate to **Settings** > **General**, configure the following: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#3-configure-organization-settings-in-langsmith
- [definition] Write an `ext_authz` service — Use `ext_authz` when you need to add, remove, or edit authorization headers, for example, to inject a provider API key based on the identity in the JWT. Your service receives the validated JWT and optionally the request body, and returns the headers to inject upstream. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#write-an-ext-authz-service
- [definition] How it works — Before forwarding each request, Envoy calls your service at `<serviceUrl>/check<original_path>` using the same HTTP method as the original request. Your service receives the validated JWT in the `x-langsmith-llm-auth` header. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#how-it-works
- [definition] Deployment options — Your `ext_authz` service can run in two ways: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#deployment-options
- [definition] Sample deployment — The example below is a minimal Python `ext_authz` service that performs an OAuth2 client credentials token exchange. On each request, it returns a cached `Authorization` header with a fresh access token, refreshing it from the configured token endpoint before it expires. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#sample-deployment
- [definition] Write an `ext_proc` transformer — Use `ext_proc` when you need to rewrite request or response bodies, for example, to convert between OpenAI format and a custom gateway format, or to inject additional fields into the request payload. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#write-an-ext-proc-transformer
- [definition] Processing modes — Control which phases are sent to your transformer via `processingMode`. Only enable the phases you need, as disabling unused phases reduces latency. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#processing-modes
- [definition] Request flow — Example with `ext_proc` enabled for header injection and body rewriting: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#request-flow
- [definition] Sample deployment — The example below deploys a minimal Go transformer as a Kubernetes Deployment. It reads the JWT from request headers, injects an `Authorization` header, and rewrites the request body from OpenAI format to a custom format. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#sample-deployment
- [definition] HTTP proxy — Envoy does not respect `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, or `NO_PROXY` environment variables. Configure an HTTP proxy explicitly: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#http-proxy
- [definition] Deploy without a public ingress — When the auth proxy does not have a public ingress and is only reachable through internal Kubernetes networking, LangSmith services must be configured to allow outbound requests to private IP addresses. Without these settings, the built-in SSRF protection blocks requests to private IPs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#deploy-without-a-public-ingress
- [definition] Other options — For ingress, autoscaling, resource limits, and other configuration options, see the [Helm chart README](https://github.com/langchain-ai/helm/tree/main/charts/langsmith-auth-proxy#readme). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#other-options
- [definition] JWT claims reference — LangSmith signs JWTs using **Ed25519 (EdDSA)**. Public keys are served at `/.well-known/jwks.json` and fetched automatically by the proxy. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#jwt-claims-reference
- [definition] Helm chart reference — For the full list of configurable values, see the [Helm chart README](https://github.com/langchain-ai/helm/tree/main/charts/langsmith-auth-proxy). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-auth-proxy-self-hosted#helm-chart-reference

## Traces and access control
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access>

- [parameter] **Administrative changes**: Policy creation, modification, and deletion. Role and permission changes related to gateway access. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#audit-logging
- [parameter] **Gateway invocations**: Each proxied call, including the caller identity and matched policy IDs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#audit-logging
- [parameter] Make calls through the gateway: Permission needed=`gateway:invoke` + `workspaces:read`; Who has it by default=`WORKSPACE_ADMIN` only — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#required-permissions
- [parameter] Create, edit, or delete policies: Permission needed=`organization:manage`; Who has it by default=Org admins — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#required-permissions
- [parameter] View gateway traces: Permission needed=`projects:read` + `runs:read`; Who has it by default=`WORKSPACE_ADMIN`, `WORKSPACE_USER`, `WORKSPACE_VIEWER` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#required-permissions
- [parameter] View audit logs: Permission needed=`organization:manage`; Who has it by default=Org admins — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#required-permissions
- [definition] Where gateway traces appear — By default, tracing of content is turned off for all organizations. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#where-gateway-traces-appear
- [definition] Trace metadata — Gateway-proxied calls are distinguishable from direct LLM calls by the project they land in and the metadata attached to their spans: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#trace-metadata
- [definition] Trace content and billing — Using a data retention policy, you can disable trace content (request and response bodies) from being written to a trace. This will apply to any traces emitted through the gateway that match the scope of the policy. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#trace-content-and-billing
- [definition] LangSmith Engine integration — When a governance policy fires (such as when a spend limit is hit, PII is detected and redacted, or a secret is caught), the event is recorded as metadata on the trace. These policy violations surface as issues in LangSmith Engine. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#langsmith-engine-integration
- [definition] Audit logging — The gateway logs two categories of events: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#audit-logging
- [definition] API key scoping — Always use workspace-scoped API keys for the gateway. Organization-scoped keys are not supported for invoking the gateway. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#api-key-scoping
- [definition] Centralizing provider credentials — The gateway centralizes provider API keys in LangSmith workspace secrets. Individual developers and agents authenticate with their [LangSmith API key](/langsmith/create-account-api-key) and never need direct access to provider keys. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#centralizing-provider-credentials
- [definition] Restricting trace visibility — Gateway traces are written as runs into a workspace project and follow LangSmith's standard workspace membership model. Anyone with `runs:read` (and `projects:read` to see the project itself) on the workspace can view traces in that workspace's gateway project. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-access#restricting-trace-visibility

- [definition] Prerequisites — You need [`organization:manage` permission](/langsmith/organization-workspace-operations) in LangSmith. [Step 2 Option A](/langsmith/llm-gateway-admin-setup#option-a-create-a-custom-workspace-role-recommended) also requires a plan that includes [RBAC](/langsmith/rbac) (custom roles). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-admin-setup#prerequisites
- [definition] 1. Add Provider Secrets — The gateway resolves provider API keys from your workspace's Provider Secrets—this is how it proxies calls to upstream providers without individual users needing local copies of provider keys. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-admin-setup#1-add-provider-secrets
- [definition] 2. Configure gateway access for users — The built-in roles `WORKSPACE_USER` and `WORKSPACE_VIEWER` do not include the `gateway:invoke` permission and cannot be edited. You have two options for granting gateway access: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-admin-setup#2-configure-gateway-access-for-users
- [definition] 3. Configure policies (optional) — Gateway policy management requires `organization:manage` permission. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-admin-setup#3-configure-policies-optional
- [definition] 4. Distribute API keys to users — Create workspace-scoped [Service Keys](/langsmith/administration-overview#service-keys) for users who need gateway access. Each key should be attached to a role that includes `gateway:invoke` and `workspaces:read`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-admin-setup#4-distribute-api-keys-to-users
- [definition] Verification — Ask a user to run the [verification cURL from the quickstart](/langsmith/llm-gateway-quickstart#2-make-a-call). A `200` response confirms the gateway, the API key, provider secrets, and role permissions are all configured correctly. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-admin-setup#verification

- [parameter] `400 Bad Request`: The request is malformed, the model ID is unavailable or incorrectly formatted, or the request cannot be translated. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#handle-errors
- [parameter] `401 Unauthorized`: The LangSmith API key is missing or invalid. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#handle-errors
- [parameter] `403 Forbidden`: The key does not have the required gateway permissions. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#handle-errors
- [parameter] `429 Too Many Requests`: A gateway rate limit or an upstream provider rate limit was reached. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#handle-errors
- [parameter] No models with a provider prefix appear in `GET /v1/models`: The provider may not be configured or may not have returned a model catalog. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#handle-errors
- [definition] API formats — The standard LLM Gateway API supports three request and response formats. Choose the format your application already uses, then call bring-your-own-key or Gateway Credits models through the same endpoint. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#api-formats
- [definition] Use Chat Completions — Point an OpenAI-compatible client at `https://gateway.smith.langchain.com/v1`. For the full request and response schema, see the [OpenAI Chat Completions API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#use-chat-completions
- [definition] Use Messages — Point an Anthropic client at `https://gateway.smith.langchain.com`. For the full request and response schema, see the [Anthropic Messages API](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/messages). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#use-messages
- [definition] Use Responses — Point an OpenAI-compatible client at `https://gateway.smith.langchain.com/v1`. For the full request and response schema, see the [OpenAI Responses API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#use-responses
- [definition] Enable prompt caching — OpenAI models (Chat Completions and Responses) support implicit prompt caching automatically, no extra parameters are required. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#enable-prompt-caching
- [definition] Anthropic models — Include `prompt_cache_options` with a `ttl` value: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#anthropic-models
- [definition] Older OpenAI models — Some older OpenAI models support explicit cache control via `prompt_cache_retention`. Set it to `"in_memory"` for most models. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#older-openai-models
- [definition] Understand translation behavior — The endpoint determines the format your application sends and receives. The model ID determines the upstream provider. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#understand-translation-behavior
- [definition] List models — Call `GET /v1/models` to list models available from providers configured for the workspace and from [Gateway Credits](/langsmith/llm-gateway-credits). The gateway returns a single OpenAI-compatible list: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#list-models
- [definition] Use a regional gateway — Replace `gateway.smith.langchain.com` with the hostname for your LangSmith region: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#use-a-regional-gateway
- [definition] Use a BYOC data plane — The LLM Gateway is also available on [BYOC](/langsmith/byoc), where it runs inside your data plane so model requests and their traces stay in your VPC. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-api-formats#use-a-byoc-data-plane

- [definition] 2. Make a call — Call the saved configuration by name (`my-custom-openai-endpoint` and `my-anthropic-endpoint` in the following examples). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-custom-providers#2-make-a-call
- [definition] Any model: `/providers/{configName}` — Use this route when the upstream serves multiple models and you want callers to pick which one: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-custom-providers#any-model-providersconfigname
- [definition] One model: `/models/{configName}` — Use this route to pin every call through this configuration to a single model, regardless of what the client requests—useful for enforcing model behavior for a team or application: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-custom-providers#one-model-modelsconfigname

- [definition] Matchable headers — The gateway matches on request headers prefixed with `X-Gateway-`, and on keys inside the `X-Gateway-Metadata` JSON header. No other request header is matchable. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-header-policies#matchable-headers
- [definition] Separate a default spend limit by header — A default spend limit applies the same cap to every member of a subject dimension. Separating it by a header applies that cap independently to every subject and header-value pair, without requiring a policy for each value. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-header-policies#separate-a-default-spend-limit-by-header
- [definition] Add an explicit header condition — An explicit spend or rate limit policy can match one exact header value. Use an explicit policy to assign different limits to different header values. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-header-policies#add-an-explicit-header-condition
- [definition] Cap spend per end customer — A reseller or multi-tenant application usually calls the gateway from its own backend, using one workspace-scoped API key on behalf of many end customers. Use an explicit header condition when each customer needs a different cap. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-header-policies#cap-spend-per-end-customer
- [definition] Step 1. Send a customer header on every call — Attach the header to each request your backend makes on behalf of an end customer: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-header-policies#step-1-send-a-customer-header-on-every-call
- [definition] Step 2. Create a cap for one customer — Create one spend policy per end customer through the [LangSmith REST API](/langsmith/smith-api-ref): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-header-policies#step-2-create-a-cap-for-one-customer
- [definition] Step 3. Sync policies with your customer list — Because each end customer needs its own policy, keep the policy set in step with your customer list. The following script creates or updates a cap for every current customer, then deletes the caps of customers that are gone: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-header-policies#step-3-sync-policies-with-your-customer-list
- [definition] Step 4. Read spend per customer — Each spend policy returned by the API reports `current_spend_usd`, the spend accumulated in the policy's active window. Use it to show each end customer their usage, or to warn them before they reach the cap. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-header-policies#step-4-read-spend-per-customer
- [definition] Limit throughput per end customer — Rate limits use the same subject matchers. Swap `policy_type` and `config` to give an end customer its own request and token allowance: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-header-policies#limit-throughput-per-end-customer

## Rate limit policies
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-rate-limit-policies>

- [snippet] Rate limit policies: API Error: 429 request blocked by gateway policies: Dev Team Rate Limit — `API Error: 429 request blocked by gateway policies: Dev Team Rate Limit` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-rate-limit-policies#rate-limit-policies
- [parameter] **User**: What it limits=Requests or tokens from a single user or group of users (resolved from the API key's identity); Example="No individual developer can send more than 100 requests per minute" — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-rate-limit-policies#policy-dimensions
- [parameter] **Workspace**: What it limits=Requests or tokens within a single workspace or group of workspaces; Example="The R&D workspace cannot exceed 1,000,000 tokens per hour" — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-rate-limit-policies#policy-dimensions
- [parameter] **API key**: What it limits=Requests or tokens from a single API key or group of API keys; Example="The customer support agent keys share a limit of 200 requests per minute" — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-rate-limit-policies#policy-dimensions
- [parameter] **Metric**: `requests` or `tokens` (total tokens as reported by the provider) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-rate-limit-policies#limits
- [parameter] **Window**: `minute` or `hour` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-rate-limit-policies#limits
- [parameter] **Value**: A positive integer (the cap) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-rate-limit-policies#limits
- [definition] Policy dimensions — Rate limit policies are evaluated for every incoming request. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-rate-limit-policies#policy-dimensions
- [definition] Independent enforcement — Each subject is tracked and enforced separately. One user hitting their limit does not affect other users. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-rate-limit-policies#independent-enforcement
- [definition] Limits — A single rate limit policy can enforce **multiple limits at once**. For example, one policy can enforce both *100 requests per minute* and *1,000,000 tokens per hour* simultaneously. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-rate-limit-policies#limits
- [definition] Create a rate limit policy — Creating and managing policies requires `organization:manage` permission. For the full permissions breakdown, refer to [Traces, Engine, and access control](/langsmith/llm-gateway-access). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-rate-limit-policies#create-a-rate-limit-policy

## Spend policies
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies>

- [snippet] Spend policies: API Error: 402 request blocked by gateway policies: R&D Spend Cap — `API Error: 402 request blocked by gateway policies: R&D Spend Cap` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#spend-policies
- [parameter] **Organization**: What it caps=Total spend across all workspaces in the org; Example="The entire org cannot spend more than $10,000/month on LLM calls" — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#policy-dimensions
- [parameter] **Workspace**: What it caps=Total spend within a single workspace or group of workspaces; Example="The workspaces related to R&D cannot spend more than $2,000/month" — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#policy-dimensions
- [parameter] **API key**: What it caps=Spend by a single API key or group of API keys (maps to a service or agent); Example="The customer support agent keys cannot spend more than $500/month cumulatively" — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#policy-dimensions
- [parameter] **User**: What it caps=Spend by a single user or group of users (resolved from the API key's identity); Example="No individual developer can spend more than $50/day" — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#policy-dimensions
- [parameter] **Monthly**: Resets=First of each month; Use case=Budget alignment, overall cost control — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#time-windows
- [parameter] **Weekly**: Resets=Midnight UTC on the Monday of each week; Use case=weekly budgeting — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#time-windows
- [parameter] **Daily**: Resets=Midnight UTC; Use case=Prevent single-day cost spikes (for example, a coding agent in a retry loop overnight) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#time-windows
- [parameter] **Hourly**: Resets=Top of each hour; Use case=Catch runaway agents quickly — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#time-windows
- [definition] Policy dimensions — Spend policies are evaluated from broadest to most specific. All matching policies are checked, and if any one returns a block, the request is rejected. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#policy-dimensions
- [definition] Conflict resolution — By default, LLM Gateway assesses the broadest scope first. If a granular policy applies, the most restrictive policy wins. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#conflict-resolution
- [definition] Create a spend policy — Creating and managing policies requires `organization:manage` permission. For the full permissions breakdown, refer to [Traces, Engine, and access control](/langsmith/llm-gateway-access). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#create-a-spend-policy
- [definition] View spend — The spend visibility dashboard shows real-time cost rollups so you can understand where your LLM budget is going before you reach the limit. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#view-spend
- [definition] Integration with LangSmith Engine — When a spend policy blocks a request, the violation is recorded as metadata on the trace. These violations surface as issues in [LangSmith Engine](/langsmith/engine), where you can click through from the issue to the trace to understand what the agent was doing when it hit the limit. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway-spend-policies#integration-with-langsmith-engine

- [snippet] TypeScript expandable wrap: import { Client } from "langsmith"; — `import { Client } from "langsmith";` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#route-between-langsmith-and-opentelemetry-destinations
- [definition] Log traces to a specific project — This page covers how to control where LangSmith sends your traces: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#log-traces-to-a-specific-project
- [definition] Set the destination project statically — LangSmith uses the concept of a [_project_](/langsmith/observability-concepts#projects) to group traces. If left unspecified, the project is set to `default`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#set-the-destination-project-statically
- [definition] Set the destination project dynamically — You can also set the project name at program runtime in various ways, depending on how you are [annotating your code for tracing](/langsmith/annotate-code). This is useful when you want to log traces to different projects within the same application: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#set-the-destination-project-dynamically
- [definition] Set the destination workspace dynamically — If you need to route traces dynamically to different LangSmith [workspaces](/langsmith/administration-overview#workspaces) based on runtime configuration (e.g., routing different users or tenants to separate workspaces), the approach differs by language: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#set-the-destination-workspace-dynamically
- [definition] Generic cross-workspace tracing — Use this approach for general applications where you want to dynamically route traces to different workspaces based on runtime logic (e.g., customer ID, tenant, or environment). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#generic-cross-workspace-tracing
- [definition] Override default workspace for LangSmith deployments — When [deploying agents](/langsmith/deployment) to LangSmith, you can override the default workspace that traces are sent to by using a graph lifespan context manager. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#override-default-workspace-for-langsmith-deployments
- [definition] Write traces to multiple destinations with replicas — Replicas let you send every trace to multiple projects or workspaces **at the same time**. Unlike the dynamic routing patterns where each trace goes to one destination, replicas duplicate the trace to all configured destinations in parallel. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#write-traces-to-multiple-destinations-with-replicas
- [definition] Configure replicas via environment variable — Set the `LANGSMITH_RUNS_ENDPOINTS` environment variable to a JSON value. Two formats are supported: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#configure-replicas-via-environment-variable
- [definition] Configure replicas at runtime — You can also pass replicas directly in code, which is useful when destinations vary per request or tenant. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#configure-replicas-at-runtime
- [definition] Replicate within the same server (project-only replicas) — If all your replicas use the same LangSmith server, you can omit `api_url` and `auth` and specify only a `project_name`. The SDK reuses the default client credentials: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#replicate-within-the-same-server-project-only-replicas
- [definition] Leave feedback on all replica instances — When you use replicas, each replica receives a copy of every run. To submit feedback for a run on a specific replica, you need that replica's run ID. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#leave-feedback-on-all-replica-instances
- [definition] Route between LangSmith and OpenTelemetry destinations — You can decide at runtime whether a given invocation sends traces to LangSmith, to an OpenTelemetry (OTel) backend, or to both, without redeploying or modifying application logic. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/log-traces-to-project#route-between-langsmith-and-opentelemetry-destinations

- [definition] Delete an agent or skill — This operation is permanent and cannot be undone. Deleting a repo also removes its owned child file repos. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-contexts-sdk#delete-an-agent-or-skill

## Create and manage datasets in the UI
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets-in-application>

- [definition] Create and manage datasets in the UI — [_Datasets_](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#datasets) enable you to perform repeatable evaluations over time using consistent data. Datasets are made up of [_examples_](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#examples), which store inputs, outputs, and optionally, reference outputs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets-in-application#create-and-manage-datasets-in-the-ui
- [definition] Create a dataset and add examples — The following sections explain the different ways you can create a dataset in LangSmith and add examples to it. Depending on your workflow, you can manually curate examples, automatically capture them from tracing, import files, or even generate synthetic data: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets-in-application#create-a-dataset-and-add-examples
- [definition] Manually from a tracing project — A common pattern for constructing datasets is to convert notable traces from your application into dataset examples. This approach requires that you have [configured tracing to LangSmith](/langsmith/observability-concepts). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets-in-application#manually-from-a-tracing-project
- [definition] Automatically from a tracing project — Use [automation rules](/langsmith/rules) to add traces to a dataset automatically when they meet specified conditions. For example, add traces that are [tagged](/langsmith/observability-concepts#tags) for a specific use case or have a [low feedback score](/langsmith/observability-concepts#feedback). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets-in-application#automatically-from-a-tracing-project
- [definition] From the Playground — On the [**Playground**](/langsmith/prompt-engineering-concepts#playground) page: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets-in-application#from-the-playground
- [definition] Import a dataset from a CSV or JSONL file — On the **Datasets & Experiments** page, click **+New Dataset**, then **Import** an existing dataset from CSV or JSONL file. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets-in-application#import-a-dataset-from-a-csv-or-jsonl-file
- [definition] Create a new dataset from the datasets & experiments page — 1. Navigate to the **Datasets & Experiments** page from the left-hand menu. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets-in-application#create-a-new-dataset-from-the-datasets-experiments-page
- [definition] Add synthetic examples created by an LLM — If you have existing examples and a [schema](#create-a-dataset-schema) defined on your dataset, when you click **+ Example** there is an option to <Icon icon="sparkles"/> **Add AI-Generated Examples**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets-in-application#add-synthetic-examples-created-by-an-llm
- [definition] Create a dataset schema — LangSmith datasets store arbitrary JSON objects. We recommend (but do not require) that you define a schema for your dataset to ensure that they conform to a specific JSON schema. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets-in-application#create-a-dataset-schema
- [definition] Create and manage dataset splits — For an overview of when and why to use splits, refer to [Dataset organization](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#dataset-organization). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets-in-application#create-and-manage-dataset-splits
- [definition] Filter examples — You can filter examples by split, metadata key/value or perform full-text search over examples. These filtering options are available to the top left of the examples table: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets-in-application#filter-examples

- [definition] Manage datasets — LangSmith provides tools for managing and working with your [_datasets_](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#datasets). This page describes dataset operations including: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets#manage-datasets
- [definition] Version a dataset — In LangSmith, datasets are versioned. This means that every time you add, update, or delete examples in your dataset, a new version of the dataset is created. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets#version-a-dataset
- [definition] Create a new version of a dataset — Any time you add, update, or delete examples in your dataset, a new [version](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#dataset-organization) of your dataset is created. This allows you to track changes to your dataset over time and understand how your dataset has evolved. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets#create-a-new-version-of-a-dataset
- [definition] Tag a version — You can also tag versions of your dataset to give them a more human-readable name, which can be useful for marking important milestones in your dataset's history. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets#tag-a-version
- [definition] Use `list_examples` — You can use `evaluate` / `aevaluate` to pass in an iterable of examples to evaluate on a particular version of a dataset. Use `list_examples` / `listExamples` to fetch examples from a particular version tag using `as_of` / `asOf` and pass that into the `data` argument. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets#use-list-examples
- [definition] Evaluate on a filtered view of a dataset — You can use the `list_examples` / `listExamples` method to [fetch](/langsmith/manage-datasets-programmatically#fetch-examples) a subset of examples from a dataset to evaluate on. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets#evaluate-on-a-filtered-view-of-a-dataset
- [definition] Evaluate on a dataset split — You can use the `list_examples` / `listExamples` method to evaluate on one or multiple [splits](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#dataset-organization) of your dataset. The `splits` parameter takes a list of the splits you would like to evaluate. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets#evaluate-on-a-dataset-split
- [definition] Share a dataset publicly — Sharing a dataset publicly will make the **dataset examples, experiments and associated runs, and feedback on this dataset accessible to anyone with the link**, even if they don't have a LangSmith account. Make sure you're not sharing sensitive information. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets#share-a-dataset-publicly
- [definition] Unshare a dataset — 1. Click on **Unshare** by clicking on **Public** in the upper right hand corner of any publicly shared dataset, then **Unshare** in the dialog. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets#unshare-a-dataset
- [definition] Export a dataset — You can export your LangSmith dataset to a CSV, JSONL, or [OpenAI's fine tuning format](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/fine-tuning#example-format) from the LangSmith UI. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets#export-a-dataset
- [definition] Export filtered traces from experiment to dataset — After running an [offline evaluation](/langsmith/evaluation-concepts#offline-evaluations) in LangSmith, you may want to export [traces](/langsmith/observability-concepts#traces) that met some evaluation criteria to a dataset. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets#export-filtered-traces-from-experiment-to-dataset
- [definition] View experiment traces — To do so, first click on the arrow next to your experiment name. This will direct you to a project that contains the traces generated from your experiment. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets#view-experiment-traces

- [definition] Manage prompts programmatically — You can use the LangSmith Python, TypeScript, and Java SDKs to manage prompts programmatically. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#manage-prompts-programmatically
- [definition] Install packages — In Python, you can directly use the LangSmith SDK (*recommended, full functionality*) or you can use through the LangChain package (limited to pushing and pulling prompts). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#install-packages
- [definition] Configure environment variables — If you already have `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` set to your current workspace's api key from LangSmith, you can skip this step. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#configure-environment-variables
- [definition] Push a prompt — To create a new prompt or update an existing prompt, you can use the `push prompt` method. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#push-a-prompt
- [definition] Push a StructuredPrompt — A `StructuredPrompt` combines a prompt template with an output schema, ensuring the model returns data in a defined structure. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#push-a-structuredprompt
- [definition] Without a model — Push the structured prompt on its own when you want to store the template and schema independently of any model configuration. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#without-a-model
- [definition] With a model — Push the structured prompt as a RunnableSequence with a model to store the full pipeline, including model configuration, in the hub. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#with-a-model
- [definition] Pull a prompt — To pull a prompt, you can use the `pull prompt` method, which returns the prompt as a langchain `PromptTemplate`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#pull-a-prompt
- [definition] Use with the LangSmith gateway — If your workspace uses the [LangSmith LLM Gateway](/langsmith/llm-gateway), you can route prompt model calls through it by setting an environment variable before pulling and invoking your prompt. No other code changes are required. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#use-with-the-langsmith-gateway
- [definition] Prompt caching — The LangSmith SDK includes built-in in-memory caching for prompts. When enabled, LangSmith will cache pulled prompts in memory, reducing latency and API calls for frequently used prompts. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#prompt-caching
- [definition] Default behavior — Caching is **enabled by default**. When enabled, the default settings are: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#default-behavior
- [definition] Using the cache — By default, all clients use the global prompt cache. No configuration is needed: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#using-the-cache
- [definition] Configuring the global cache — You can configure the global prompt cache that all clients use by default. This is useful when you want to customize caching behavior across your entire application: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#configuring-the-global-cache
- [definition] Disabling the cache — To disable caching for a specific client, pass `disable_prompt_cache=True`. You can also configure a max size of zero globally: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#disabling-the-cache
- [definition] Skipping the cache — To bypass the cache and fetch a fresh prompt from the API for an individual request, use the `skip_cache` parameter: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#skipping-the-cache
- [definition] Offline mode — For environments with limited or no network connectivity, you can pre-populate the cache and use it offline. Set `ttl_seconds` to `None` (Python) or `null` (TypeScript) to prevent cache entries from expiring and disable background refresh. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#offline-mode
- [definition] Cache operations — The cache supports several operations for managing cached prompts: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#cache-operations
- [definition] Cleanup — You can manually call `stop()` to stop the background refresh task: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#cleanup
- [definition] Use a prompt without LangChain — If you want to store your prompts in LangSmith but use them directly with a model provider's API, you can use our conversion methods. These convert your prompt into the payload required for the OpenAI or Anthropic API. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#use-a-prompt-without-langchain
- [definition] List, delete, and like prompts — You can also list, delete, and like/unlike prompts using the `list prompts`, `delete prompt`, `like prompt` and `unlike prompt` methods. See the [LangSmith SDK client](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langsmith-sdk) for extensive documentation on these methods. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts-programmatically#list-delete-and-like-prompts

## Manage prompts
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts>

- [snippet] Use tags in code: prompt = client.pull_prompt("joke-generator:production") — `prompt = client.pull_prompt("joke-generator:production")` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#use-tags-in-code
- [definition] Manage prompts — LangSmith provides several tools to help you manage your [_prompts_](/langsmith/prompt-engineering-concepts) effectively. This page describes the following features: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#manage-prompts
- [definition] Prompt detail page — Select a prompt from the [**Prompts** table](/langsmith/create-a-prompt#view-your-prompts) to open its detail page, which uses a two-pane layout: commit history and environments appear on the left, and commit details appear on the right. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#prompt-detail-page
- [definition] Environments — Environments represent named deployment targets, **Staging** and **Production**, that you can assign to specific commits. They let you track which version of a prompt is active in each environment and promote commits between them. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#environments
- [definition] Promote a commit — Promoting a commit assigns it to an environment. You can promote any commit to Staging or Production. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#promote-a-commit
- [definition] Roll back an environment — Each environment maintains an ordered history of which commits were assigned to it and when. To roll back to a previous commit: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#roll-back-an-environment
- [definition] Commit tags — [_Commit tags_](/langsmith/prompt-engineering-concepts#tags) are labels that reference a specific [_commit_](/langsmith/prompt-engineering-concepts#commits) in your prompt's version history. They help you mark significant versions and control which versions run in different environments. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#commit-tags
- [definition] Create a tag — To create a tag, select the commit you want to tag in the left pane of the prompt detail page. Click **Tag** at the top right of the right pane. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#create-a-tag
- [definition] Move a tag — To point a tag to a different commit, select the destination commit in the left pane of the prompt detail page. Click **Tag** at the top right of the right pane. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#move-a-tag
- [definition] Delete a tag — To delete a tag, click **Tag** at the top right of the right pane. (It does not matter which commit is selected). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#delete-a-tag
- [definition] Use tags in code — Tags provide a stable way to reference specific versions of your prompts in code. Instead of using commit hashes directly, you can reference tags that can be updated without changing your code. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#use-tags-in-code
- [definition] Prompt owners — The prompt owners feature gives you fine-grained control over who can tag commits and delete a specific prompt. This is useful for production promotion flows where you want to limit which team members can promote a commit to an environment by assigning or moving tags. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#prompt-owners
- [definition] Access modes — Each prompt has two access modes, configured under **Access and Permissions** in the [UI](https://smith.langchain.com?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-manage-prompts): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#access-modes
- [definition] Configure access and permissions — 1. Open the prompt in the LangSmith UI. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#configure-access-and-permissions
- [definition] Trigger a webhook on prompt commit — You can configure a webhook to be triggered whenever a commit is made to a prompt. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#trigger-a-webhook-on-prompt-commit
- [definition] Configure a webhook — Navigate to the **Prompts** section in the left-hand sidebar or from the application homepage. In the top right corner, click on the `+ Webhook` button. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#configure-a-webhook
- [definition] Trigger the webhook — Commit to a prompt to trigger the webhook you've configured. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#trigger-the-webhook
- [definition] Public prompt hub — LangSmith's public prompt hub is a collection of prompts that have been created by the LangChain community that you can use for reference. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-prompts#public-prompt-hub

- [definition] Exclude runs from the Messages view — Setting `LS_MESSAGE_VIEW_EXCLUDE` on a run's metadata tells the Messages view to skip that run.
