- [parameter] `restore_memory`: Omit it to resume from memory when the snapshot has it and cold-boot when it does not. `true` requires memory and fails the request if the snapshot has none. `false` always cold-boots. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#resume-from-memory
- [parameter] `preserve_memory_on_stop`: `true` suspends RAM on a voluntary stop (idle timeout or explicit stop) so the sandbox resumes where it left off when it next wakes, rather than cold-booting. Defaults to `false`, which keeps only the filesystem. Restarts triggered by infrastructure maintenance preserve memory either way. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#resume-from-memory
- [definition] Sandbox snapshots — A **snapshot** is a reusable sandbox filesystem. Build a custom snapshot from a container image when you want to boot sandboxes from a custom filesystem image. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#sandbox-snapshots
- [definition] Understand the default snapshot — When you create a sandbox without selecting a snapshot, LangSmith uses a built-in default snapshot. The default provides an Ubuntu 24.04 filesystem with common development tools. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#understand-the-default-snapshot
- [definition] Inspect the default snapshot filesystem in self-hosted deployments — In a self-hosted deployment, LangSmith creates the default snapshot from a filesystem embedded in the sandbox runtime container image, `sandbox-host`: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#inspect-the-default-snapshot-filesystem-in-self-hosted-deployments
- [definition] Build a snapshot from a container image — Build a snapshot by pointing at any container image. The call blocks until the snapshot is ready (default timeout is 60 seconds; bump it for large images). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#build-a-snapshot-from-a-container-image
- [definition] Verify a snapshot built from a container image — LangSmith builds a custom snapshot from the filesystem in the container image you provide. To independently verify those contents: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#verify-a-snapshot-built-from-a-container-image
- [definition] Private registries — To pull from a private registry, create a registry once with its credentials, then reference it by id when building a snapshot. Registries persist, so reuse one across snapshots. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#private-registries
- [definition] Build a snapshot from a Dockerfile — When you have a local `Dockerfile` but don't want to publish the image to a registry first, build a snapshot directly from the `Dockerfile` and its build context. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#build-a-snapshot-from-a-dockerfile
- [definition] Build args and target stage — Pass `build_args` / `buildArgs` to set Docker `ARG` values, and `target` to stop at a specific stage of a multi-stage build. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#build-args-and-target-stage
- [definition] Stream build logs — Pass a callback to `on_build_log` / `onBuildLog` to receive the build's stdout and stderr as it runs, which is useful for surfacing progress or debugging a failing build. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#stream-build-logs
- [definition] Speed up cold builds — `vcpus` / `vCpus` and `mem_bytes` / `memBytes` size the temporary builder sandbox. The build runs BuildKit plus the native snapshotter's layer copies inside it, which contend for the builder's default 0.5 vCPU, so giving the builder more CPU can cut a cold build's wall time substantially. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#speed-up-cold-builds
- [definition] Capture a snapshot from a running sandbox — Start a sandbox from an existing snapshot, install packages or prepare data, then capture the result as a new snapshot. The returned snapshot has its `source_sandbox_id` set to the sandbox it was captured from, and can be used as the `snapshot_id` for any later `create_sandbox` call. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#capture-a-snapshot-from-a-running-sandbox
- [definition] Tune capture timing — `capture_snapshot` blocks until the new snapshot is ready. Raise the `timeout` kwarg (default 60s) if your filesystem is large or your storage backend is slow. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#tune-capture-timing
- [definition] Resume from memory — A snapshot can carry the sandbox's RAM alongside its filesystem. Boot from one and the sandbox resumes where it left off, with its processes still running, instead of cold-booting. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#resume-from-memory
- [definition] Stopped sandboxes — A stopped sandbox keeps its filesystem, and the next request wakes it automatically. You do not need to start it yourself: send the command you wanted to run and the sandbox comes back up to serve it. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/sandbox-snapshots#stopped-sandboxes

## Scalability & resilience
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/scalability-and-resilience>

- [definition] Scalability & resilience — LangSmith is designed to scale horizontally with your workload. Each instance of the service is stateless, and keeps no resources in memory. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/scalability-and-resilience#scalability-resilience
- [definition] Server scalability — As you add more instances to a service, they will share the HTTP load as long as an appropriate load balancer mechanism is placed in front of them. In most deployment modalities we configure a load balancer for the service automatically. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/scalability-and-resilience#server-scalability
- [definition] Queue scalability — As you add more queue workers to a service, they will increase run throughput linearly, as each queue worker is configured to execute a set number of concurrent runs (`N_JOBS_PER_WORKER`, by default 10). This value governs concurrent run execution, not how many API requests the deployment can serve. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/scalability-and-resilience#queue-scalability
- [definition] Resilience — While a run is being handled by a queue instance, a periodic heartbeat timestamp will be recorded in Redis by that queue worker. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/scalability-and-resilience#resilience
- [definition] Postgres resilience — For deployment modalities where LangSmith manages the Postgres database, there are periodic backups and continuously replicated standby replicas for automatic failover. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/scalability-and-resilience#postgres-resilience
- [definition] Redis resilience — All data that requires durable storage is stored in Postgres, not Redis. Redis is used only for ephemeral metadata, and communication between instances. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/scalability-and-resilience#redis-resilience

- [definition] Google Cloud Storage lifecycle rules — You will need to setup lifecycle conditions for your GCS buckets that you are using. - [definition] Azure blob storage lifecycle management — You will need to configure a [lifecycle management policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/lifecycle-management-policy-configure) on the container in order to expire objects matching the prefixes above. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-blob-storage#azure-blob-storage-lifecycle-management

## Minimum versions for self-hosting dependencies
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-dependency-versions>

- [parameter] [PostgreSQL](/langsmith/self-host-external-postgres): Minimum version=14; Notes=Primary relational store for operational data. Required for both LangSmith and standalone Agent Server deployments. Used to install the `btree_gin`, `btree_gist`, `pgcrypto`, `citext`, `ltree`, and `pg_trgm` extensions. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-dependency-versions#datastores
- [parameter] [Redis](/langsmith/self-host-external-redis): Minimum version=6.2; Notes=Used for queueing and caching. Standalone and Redis Cluster modes are both supported. As of Agent Server 0.8.0, the Redis-backed run queue requires Redis 6.2 or later: it enqueues runs with the `ZADD ... LT` flag, which was added in 6.2. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-dependency-versions#datastores
- [parameter] [Valkey](/langsmith/self-host-external-redis): Minimum version=8; Notes=Officially supported as a drop-in replacement for Redis. Standalone and Cluster modes are both supported. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-dependency-versions#datastores
- [parameter] [ClickHouse](/langsmith/self-host-external-clickhouse): Minimum version=Version specified in the [LangSmith Helm chart](https://github.com/langchain-ai/helm/releases) or greater; Notes=Stores traces and feedback. ClickHouse versions >= 24.2 require LangSmith v0.6 or later. Downgrades are not supported. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-dependency-versions#datastores
- [parameter] [Kubernetes](/langsmith/kubernetes): Minimum version=Any version supported by the [upstream Kubernetes release cycle](https://kubernetes.io/releases/); Notes=LangSmith is regularly tested on GKE, EKS, AKS, Minikube, and Kind. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-dependency-versions#compute-and-orchestration
- [parameter] [OpenShift](/langsmith/kubernetes): Minimum version=4.14; Notes=Supported as a Kubernetes distribution for LangSmith. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-dependency-versions#compute-and-orchestration
- [parameter] [Helm](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/): Minimum version=3; Notes=Used to install and upgrade the LangSmith Helm chart. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-dependency-versions#compute-and-orchestration
- [parameter] Docker: Minimum version=A version compatible with [Docker Compose v2](https://docs.docker.com/compose/); Notes=Required for Docker-based standalone Agent Server deployments. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-dependency-versions#compute-and-orchestration
- [parameter] [LangSmith Helm chart](https://github.com/langchain-ai/helm/releases): Minimum version=Latest stable release; Notes=We recommend pinning to the latest stable chart release. Refer to the [self-hosted changelog](/langsmith/self-hosted-changelog) for per-release upgrade notes. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-dependency-versions#langsmith-chart-and-platform
- [parameter] Egress to `https://beacon.langchain.com`: Minimum version=LangSmith 0.9.0 or later; Notes=Required for license verification and usage reporting unless running in [offline mode](/langsmith/self-host-egress). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-dependency-versions#langsmith-chart-and-platform
- [definition] Minimum versions for self-hosting dependencies — This page lists the minimum supported versions for the databases, tools, and infrastructure used by self-hosted LangSmith. Install a version that meets or exceeds the minimum before deploying or upgrading. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-dependency-versions#minimum-versions-for-self-hosting-dependencies

## Disaster recovery for self-hosted LangSmith
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery>

- [parameter] LangSmith services: Components=`langsmith-frontend`, `langsmith-backend`, `langsmith-platform-backend`, `langsmith-queue`, `langsmith-ingest-queue`, `langsmith-playground`, `langsmith-ace-backend`; State=Stateless; Recovery action=Reinstall the Helm chart — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#what-you-are-recovering
- [parameter] PostgreSQL: Components=Operational data: orgs, workspaces, users, API keys, datasets, prompts, projects, deployments metadata; State=**Durable**; Recovery action=Restore from backup or replica — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#what-you-are-recovering
- [parameter] ClickHouse: Components=Traces and feedback (high volume analytical data); State=**Durable**; Recovery action=Restore from backup or replica — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#what-you-are-recovering
- [parameter] Blob storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob): Components=Run inputs, outputs, errors, manifests, extras, events, attachments (when enabled); State=**Durable**; Recovery action=Restore from versioned bucket or replica — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#what-you-are-recovering
- [parameter] Redis (or Valkey): Components=Ephemeral queue state, pub/sub, cache, run heartbeats; State=Ephemeral; Recovery action=Reprovision; no restore required — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#what-you-are-recovering
- [parameter] Kubernetes objects: Components=Helm values, `Secret`s, TLS material, IRSA / Workload Identity bindings; State=Configuration; Recovery action=Re-apply from source control or back up cluster state — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#what-you-are-recovering
- [parameter] Snapshot-only: Typical RPO=6 to 24 hours; Typical RTO=Hours; Approach=Daily managed backups of each store. Lowest cost, longest restore. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#plan-your-rpo-and-rto
- [parameter] Multi-AZ HA: Typical RPO=Seconds; Typical RTO=Minutes (zone failure); Approach=Synchronous standby in another AZ for Postgres and ClickHouse, Multi-AZ Redis, zone-redundant blob storage. Standard production posture. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#plan-your-rpo-and-rto
- [parameter] Cross-region DR: Typical RPO=Minutes to hours; Typical RTO=Hours; Approach=Backups of Postgres, ClickHouse, and blob storage copied to a second region, restored on demand. Optionally a Postgres cross-region replica for a tighter Postgres RPO. Highest cost, slower recovery than Multi-AZ, but protects against a regional outage. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#plan-your-rpo-and-rto
- [definition] Disaster recovery for self-hosted LangSmith — This page describes how to plan, configure, and operate disaster recovery (DR) for self-hosted LangSmith Observability and Evaluation. It covers what data must be protected, where it lives, how to back it up, and how to recover the platform after a regional or zonal failure. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#disaster-recovery-for-self-hosted-langsmith
- [definition] What you are recovering — Self-hosted LangSmith is composed of stateless services backed by four state stores. Recovery planning is almost entirely about the state stores. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#what-you-are-recovering
- [definition] Plan your RPO and RTO — Before designing your DR architecture, define two targets: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#plan-your-rpo-and-rto
- [definition] Postgres — LangSmith uses PostgreSQL as the primary store for operational and transactional data. **All communication with Postgres uses retries for retry-able errors**, so a brief outage during failover usually does not surface as user-visible errors. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#postgres
- [definition] Use a managed service — We strongly recommend running Postgres on a managed service in production. Managed services provide built-in automated backups, PITR, and HA failover. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#use-a-managed-service
- [definition] In-cluster Postgres — If you must run Postgres in-cluster from the bundled chart, you are responsible for backing up the underlying PersistentVolume. Snapshot the PVC on a regular cadence using your CSI driver's snapshot class, and copy snapshots to object storage or a different region. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#in-cluster-postgres
- [definition] ClickHouse — ClickHouse holds the high-volume trace and feedback data and is typically the largest data store in a LangSmith deployment. Backups and replication need to be planned for cost and restore-time impact. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#clickhouse
- [definition] Managed ClickHouse — The fastest path to a resilient ClickHouse is a managed option. See [Connect external ClickHouse](/langsmith/self-host-external-clickhouse). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#managed-clickhouse
- [definition] Self-managed replicated cluster — If you self-manage ClickHouse for compliance or air-gap reasons, use a replicated cluster. A single-node ClickHouse instance cannot meet a meaningful RPO. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#self-managed-replicated-cluster
- [definition] Blob storage — If you have enabled [blob storage](/langsmith/self-host-blob-storage) (recommended for production), your run inputs, outputs, errors, manifests, extras, events, and attachments live in S3, GCS, or Azure Blob Storage. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#blob-storage
- [definition] Redis — Redis stores ephemeral metadata, queue state, and cross-instance pub/sub. **No durable data is stored in Redis, so you do not need to back it up.** Communication with Redis is retried for retry-able errors. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#redis
- [definition] Kubernetes configuration and secrets — The Helm chart values, Kubernetes `Secret`s, and identity bindings are as important as your data backups. A complete restore requires both. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#kubernetes-configuration-and-secrets
- [definition] Single region with Multi-AZ HA (recommended baseline) — This is the minimum production posture and protects against zonal failures. It does not protect against a regional outage. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#single-region-with-multi-az-ha-recommended-baseline
- [definition] Cross-region active/passive DR — This protects against a regional outage. It is significantly more expensive but is the right pattern for tier-1 deployments. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#cross-region-activepassive-dr
- [definition] Restore after a zonal failure — In a single-region Multi-AZ deployment, zonal failures are handled automatically by your cloud provider: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-after-a-zonal-failure
- [definition] Restore after a regional failure — This is the cross-region failover runbook. Adapt to your specific infrastructure. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-after-a-regional-failure
- [definition] Declare failover — Confirm the primary region is unavailable. Communicate to stakeholders that you are failing over and what the expected RTO is. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-after-a-regional-failure
- [definition] Promote data stores — Promote the Postgres cross-region replica to primary in the DR region. For ClickHouse Cloud or LangSmith Managed ClickHouse, initiate the documented region failover. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-after-a-regional-failure
- [definition] Repoint blob storage — Update the LangSmith Helm `config.blobStorage.bucketName` and `apiURL` to point at the DR bucket. Confirm the bucket has the same TTL lifecycle rules. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-after-a-regional-failure
- [definition] Provision Redis — Create a fresh managed Redis instance in the DR region. Update the LangSmith Helm `redis.external` values to point at it. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-after-a-regional-failure
- [definition] Scale the DR cluster — If running warm/cold, scale the LangSmith deployments to their production replica counts. Apply any pending Helm value updates from source control. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-after-a-regional-failure
- [definition] Run smoke tests — Submit a test trace, verify it lands in ClickHouse and (if blob storage is enabled) in the DR bucket. Open the UI and confirm traces, datasets, and projects load. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-after-a-regional-failure
- [definition] Cut DNS over — Update DNS to route traffic to the DR ingress. Communicate the cutover to stakeholders. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-after-a-regional-failure
- [definition] Plan failback — Once the primary region is healthy, plan a controlled failback. This is typically scheduled into a maintenance window and involves rebuilding the primary as the new DR replica before swapping again. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-after-a-regional-failure
- [definition] Restore from snapshot — If you have lost the primary data store entirely and need to restore from snapshot: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-from-snapshot
- [definition] Stop ingestion — Scale `langsmith-queue` and `langsmith-ingest-queue` to zero so no new traces are written while you restore. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-from-snapshot
- [definition] Restore Postgres — Restore the Postgres backup to a new instance or perform PITR to the latest pre-incident timestamp. Update the LangSmith Helm `postgres.external` connection details to point to the restored instance. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-from-snapshot
- [definition] Restore ClickHouse — Restore the most recent ClickHouse backup that aligns in time with the Postgres restore point. Restore time scales with data size. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-from-snapshot
- [definition] Restore blob storage — If you lost blob data (rare), restore versioned objects from S3/GCS/Azure or copy from a replicated DR bucket. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-from-snapshot
- [definition] Resume ingestion — Scale `langsmith-queue` and `langsmith-ingest-queue` back to production replica counts. Submit a smoke-test trace and verify it lands. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#restore-from-snapshot
- [definition] Testing your DR plan — A backup is only as good as the last successful restore. Schedule the following exercises: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-disaster-recovery#testing-your-dr-plan

## Configure environment variables in the Helm chart
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables>

- [snippet] commonEnv: commonEnv: — `commonEnv:` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#commonenv
- [snippet] Services that do not receive commonEnv: playground: — `playground:` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#services-that-do-not-receive-commonenv
- [snippet] extraEnv: backend: — `backend:` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#extraenv
- [snippet] No duplicate variable names: Duplicate keys detected: [MY_ENV_VAR] — `Duplicate keys detected: [MY_ENV_VAR]` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#no-duplicate-variable-names
- [snippet] Example: set a variable on most services but override it on one: commonEnv: — `# Apply to all services that receive commonEnv` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#example-set-a-variable-on-most-services-but-override-it-on-one
- [snippet] Reduce batched-run persistence logging: commonEnv: — `commonEnv:` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#reduce-batched-run-persistence-logging
- [definition] Configure environment variables in the Helm chart — The LangSmith Helm chart provides two ways to inject environment variables into services: `commonEnv` and `extraEnv`. Understanding the difference between them helps you configure your deployment correctly and avoid runtime errors. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#configure-environment-variables-in-the-helm-chart
- [definition] commonEnv — `commonEnv` is a top-level field in `values.yaml` that applies to **all deployments and statefulsets except the `playground` and `aceBackend` services**, which are sandboxed and do not receive `commonEnv` values. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#commonenv
- [definition] Services that receive commonEnv — The following services receive `commonEnv`: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#services-that-receive-commonenv
- [definition] Services that do not receive commonEnv — The following services are sandboxed and do **not** receive `commonEnv`: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#services-that-do-not-receive-commonenv
- [definition] extraEnv — `extraEnv` is a per-service field that adds environment variables to a specific service only. Each service that supports `extraEnv` exposes it under `<service>.deployment.extraEnv`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#extraenv
- [definition] No duplicate variable names — The chart uses a `detectDuplicates` helper to validate environment variable names for each service. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#no-duplicate-variable-names
- [definition] Example: set a variable on most services but override it on one — To use a common value for most services while overriding it for a specific service, set it in `commonEnv` and add the override to that service's `extraEnv`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#example-set-a-variable-on-most-services-but-override-it-on-one
- [definition] Reduce batched-run persistence logging — By default, LangSmith logs a success message for every batch of runs it persists via the Go-based ingest queue. On deployments that process a high volume of traces, this can produce excessive log noise. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-environment-variables#reduce-batched-run-persistence-logging

- [parameter] `langchain/langsmith-frontend`: `langchain/langsmith-frontend-fips` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-fips#how-the-images-are-built
- [parameter] `langchain/langgraph-operator`: `langchain/langgraph-operator-fips` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-fips#how-the-images-are-built
- [definition] FIPS-compliant images — FIPS and airgapped LangSmith deployments require a conversation with your LangChain account executive before rollout. Reach out to scope licensing, supported configurations, and upgrade paths before you change your installation. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-fips#fips-compliant-images
- [definition] How the images are built — The `-fips` variants are built on top of [Chainguard FIPS container images](https://edu.chainguard.dev/chainguard/fips/fips-images/), which ship NIST-validated cryptographic modules (OpenSSL FIPS provider, Bouncy Castle FIPS, or BoringCrypto depending on the base). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-fips#how-the-images-are-built
- [definition] ACE backend FIPS boundary note — `langsmith-ace-backend-fips` is built on the same Chainguard FIPS base as all other `-fips` images, but its code-execution runtimes (Deno and Pyodide/WebAssembly) bundle their own cryptographic libraries and do not dynamically link the system FIPS-validated OpenSSL, so the execution runtime itself… — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-fips#ace-backend-fips-boundary-note
- [definition] Use FIPS images — Update `values.yaml` in your LangSmith Helm installation to point each LangChain image repository at its `-fips` counterpart, keeping your existing tag. Replace `0.16.21` with the [LangSmith version](/langsmith/self-hosted-changelog) you want to deploy: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-fips#use-fips-images
- [definition] Verify FIPS mode — Chainguard ships the `openssl-fips-test` tool inside every FIPS image. Running it against a pod prints the FIPS self-tests, the active FIPS provider version, and a link to the applicable CMVP certificate. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-fips#verify-fips-mode
- [definition] Mirror for airgapped deployments — The `-fips` naming convention applies identically when mirroring images to a private registry. Follow the [image mirroring guide](/langsmith/self-host-mirroring-images) and substitute each repository with its `-fips` counterpart. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-fips#mirror-for-airgapped-deployments

- [definition] Trace querying (read path) — Common usage that puts load on the read path: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-scale#trace-querying-read-path

- [definition] Example LangSmith configurations for scale — Below we provide some example LangSmith configurations based on expected read and write loads. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-scale#example-langsmith-configurations-for-scale
- [definition] Low reads, low writes <a name="low-reads-low-writes"></a> — The default LangSmith configuration will handle this load. No custom resource configuration is needed here. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-scale#low-reads-low-writes-a-namelow-reads-low-writesa
- [definition] Low reads, high writes <a name="low-reads-high-writes"></a> — You have a very high scale of trace ingestions, but single digit number of users on the frontend querying traces at any one time. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-scale#low-reads-high-writes-a-namelow-reads-high-writesa
- [definition] High reads, low writes <a name="high-reads-low-writes"></a> — You have a relatively low scale of trace ingestions, but many frontend users querying traces and/or have scripts that hit the `/runs/query` or `/runs/<run-id>` endpoints frequently. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-scale#high-reads-low-writes-a-namehigh-reads-low-writesa
- [definition] Medium reads, medium writes <a name="medium-reads-medium-writes"></a> — This is a good all around configuration that should be able to handle most usage patterns of LangSmith. In internal testing, this configuration allowed us to scale to 100 traces ingested per second and 40 read requests per second. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-scale#medium-reads-medium-writes-a-namemedium-reads-medium-writesa
- [definition] High reads, high writes <a name="high-reads-high-writes"></a> — You have a very high rate of trace ingestion (approaching 1000 traces submitted per second) and also have many users querying traces on the frontend (over 50 users) and/or scripts that are consistently making requests to `/runs/query` or `/runs/<run-id>` endpoints. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-scale#high-reads-high-writes-a-namehigh-reads-high-writesa

- [definition] Set up SSO with OAuth2.0 and OIDC — LangSmith [Self-Hosted](/langsmith/self-hosted) provides SSO via OAuth2.0 and OIDC, which delegates authentication to your Identity Provider (IdP) to manage access to LangSmith. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-sso#set-up-sso-with-oauth20-and-oidc
- [definition] Prerequisites — You must have the following to complete the [Provider setup](#provider-setup): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-sso#prerequisites
- [definition] Microsoft Entra ID IdP setup — Configure Microsoft Entra ID as a single sign-on provider using OAuth2.0 and OIDC. - [definition] Google workspace IdP setup — You can use Google Workspace as a single sign-on (SSO) provider using [OAuth2.0 and OIDC](https://developers.google.com/identity/openid-connect/openid-connect) without PKCE. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-sso#google-workspace-idp-setup

- [definition] Scope encoding for strict identity providers — By default, LangSmith encodes the spaces between `oauthScopes` in the authorization request as `+` (the `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` convention). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-sso#scope-encoding-for-strict-identity-providers
- [definition] Override sub claim — In some scenarios, it may be necessary to override which claim is used as the `sub` claim from your identity provider. For example, in SCIM, the resolved `sub` claim and SCIM `externalId` must match in order for login to succeed. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-sso#override-sub-claim
- [definition] SSO Groups Sync — SSO Groups Sync on self-hosted requires LangSmith chart version **0.15.0-rc.3** (application version **0.15.2rc1**) or later. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-sso#sso-groups-sync
- [definition] PKCE flow (deprecated) — We recommend running with a [`Client Secret`](#provider-setup). However, if your IdP does not support this, you can use the `Authorization Code with PKCE` flow. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-sso#pkce-flow-deprecated
- [definition] Requirements — This flow does **not** require a `Client Secret`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-sso#requirements

- [parameter] `langsmith_irsa_role`: Defined in=`modules/eks`; Used by=`backend`, `platform-backend`, `queue`, `ingest-queue`, host-backend, listener; Permissions=`s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:ListBucket` on the LangSmith bucket — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#irsa-roles

- [parameter] ALB (AWS LBC): Variable=_default_; Split=No; Traffic path=`ALB → frontend NodePort`; When to use=Default. Single-namespace deployments, POC, simplest TLS via ACM. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#ingress-options
- [parameter] NGINX Ingress: Variable=`enable_nginx_ingress = true`; Split=No; Traffic path=`ALB → TGB → NGINX controller → frontend ClusterIP`; When to use=When NGINX is the standard ingress in your organization. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#ingress-options
- [parameter] Envoy Gateway: Variable=`enable_envoy_gateway = true`; Split=Yes; Traffic path=`ALB → TGB → Envoy service:8080 → HTTPRoute → services`; When to use=Cross-namespace HTTPRoute routing. Recommended for split dataplane on new AWS deployments. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#ingress-options
- [parameter] Istio: Variable=`enable_istio_gateway = true`; Split=Yes; Traffic path=`ALB → TGB → istio-ingressgateway:80 → VirtualService → services`; When to use=Clusters with Istio already installed, or when an mTLS mesh is required. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#ingress-options
- [parameter] `none`: Behavior=HTTP only, no certificate; Compatible gateways=Any — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#tls-and-dns
- [parameter] `acm`: Behavior=HTTPS:443 with HTTP→HTTPS redirect. ACM certificate, auto-provisioned or BYO.; Compatible gateways=ALB, NGINX — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#tls-and-dns
- [parameter] `letsencrypt`: Behavior=HTTPS via cert-manager and Let's Encrypt, using an HTTP-01 challenge solved through the ALB; Compatible gateways=ALB — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#tls-and-dns
- [parameter] Let's Encrypt _(default)_: Public domain, internet access, free — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#why-acm-versus-cert-manager
- [parameter] ACM Private CA (`aws-privateca-issuer`): AWS-native, air-gap friendly, private domains, paid — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#why-acm-versus-cert-manager
- [parameter] Venafi (`cert-manager-venafi`): Enterprise PKI, regulated environments — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#why-acm-versus-cert-manager
- [parameter] HashiCorp Vault (`cert-manager-vault`): Self-hosted PKI — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#why-acm-versus-cert-manager
- [parameter] DigiCert, Sectigo, others: ACME or custom issuer plugins — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#why-acm-versus-cert-manager
- [parameter] Network Firewall: Variable=`create_firewall`; Default=`false`; Purpose=FQDN-based egress filtering. Allows only domains in `firewall_allowed_fqdns` (TLS SNI + HTTP Host). Requires `create_vpc = true`. Cost ≈ `$0.40/hr/endpoint + $0.065/GB processed`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#opt-in-security-modules
- [parameter] ALB access logs: Variable=`alb_access_logs_enabled`; Default=`false`; Purpose=Traffic analysis and compliance — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#opt-in-security-modules
- [parameter] CloudTrail: Variable=`create_cloudtrail`; Default=`false`; Purpose=API call logging. Skip if an organization trail already exists. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#opt-in-security-modules
- [parameter] WAF: Variable=`create_waf`; Default=`false`; Purpose=WAFv2 Web ACL: OWASP Top 10, IP reputation, known bad inputs — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#opt-in-security-modules
- [parameter] EKS node: Default=`m5.4xlarge`; vCPU=16; Memory=64 GB — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#default-resource-sizes
- [parameter] RDS PostgreSQL: Default=`db.t3.large`; vCPU=2; Memory=8 GB — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#default-resource-sizes
- [parameter] ElastiCache Redis: Default=`cache.m6g.xlarge`; vCPU=4; Memory=13.07 GB — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#default-resource-sizes
- [parameter] RDS storage: Default=10 GB; vCPU=—; Memory=— — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#default-resource-sizes
- [parameter] 1: Area=ACM wildcard SANs; Constraint or fix=`langchain.com` has `0 issue "amazon.com"` CAA but not `0 issuewild "amazon.com"`. Wildcard SANs fail with `CAA_ERROR`. The `dns` module requests only the apex domain. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#validated-behaviors-and-known-constraints
- [parameter] 2: Area=In-cluster Redis; Constraint or fix=The LangSmith Helm chart deploys Redis without `requirepass`. The `k8s_bootstrap` module writes `redis://langsmith-redis:6379`. Do not add an auth token unless you also configure the Helm chart Redis values. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#validated-behaviors-and-known-constraints
- [parameter] 3: Area=`name_prefix` length; Constraint or fix=Maximum 15 characters. Names like `dz-nginx-tst` (12 characters) are valid. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#validated-behaviors-and-known-constraints
- [parameter] 4: Area=Istio port; Constraint or fix=Istio 1.23+ ingressgateway listens on port 80 via `NET_BIND_SERVICE`, not port 8080. ALB TGB health check and security group rules must target port 80. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#validated-behaviors-and-known-constraints
- [parameter] 5: Area=NGINX TGB port; Constraint or fix=NGINX ingress-nginx controller pods listen on port 80. The TargetGroupBinding target type is `ip`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#validated-behaviors-and-known-constraints
- [parameter] 6: Area=Envoy Gateway port; Constraint or fix=The Envoy Gateway proxy is exposed on a Kubernetes service at port 8080. The ALB TargetGroupBinding `servicePort` must be 8080, with target type `ip`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#validated-behaviors-and-known-constraints
- [parameter] 7: Area=Destroy order; Constraint or fix=Always run `terraform destroy` first and let Terraform handle namespace and Helm release lifecycle. Pre-deleting namespaces causes the `helm_release` resource to time out because Helm cannot uninstall cleanly into a terminating namespace. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#validated-behaviors-and-known-constraints
- [parameter] 8: Area=Stuck terminating namespaces; Constraint or fix=KEDA's stale `external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1` API group causes `NamespaceDeletionDiscoveryFailure`. Fix: `kubectl delete apiservice v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io` before re-running `terraform destroy`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#validated-behaviors-and-known-constraints
- [definition] AWS Terraform architecture — Understand what the [AWS Terraform modules](https://github.com/langchain-ai/terraform/tree/main/modules/aws) provision and how the pieces fit together, so you can size, secure, and customize your LangSmith deployment before running `make apply`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#aws-terraform-architecture
- [definition] Platform layers — LangSmith on AWS deploys in two stages with one optional add-on. The infrastructure stage provisions the cloud foundation. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#platform-layers
- [definition] Application core services — These pods run on every deployment. All write logs and metrics; the busier components (backend, queue, ingest-queue) scale horizontally. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#application-core-services
- [definition] One-time jobs — The Helm chart runs three jobs at install and upgrade time: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#one-time-jobs
- [definition] LangSmith Deployment add-on — When `enable_deployments = true`, three additional services are installed and a `LangGraphPlatform` CRD is registered. Each deployment the user creates in the LangSmith UI produces a Kubernetes Deployment in the `langsmith` namespace, managed by the operator. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#langsmith-deployment-add-on
- [definition] AWS managed services — When `postgres_source = "external"` and `redis_source = "external"` (the recommended production setting), Terraform provisions the following AWS managed services: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#aws-managed-services
- [definition] Cluster infrastructure — Two Terraform modules install the cluster-level services LangSmith depends on. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#cluster-infrastructure
- [definition] IRSA roles — IRSA replaces static credentials. The EKS cluster's OIDC issuer is the trust anchor; service accounts in `langsmith` and `kube-system` are annotated with role ARNs and pods receive temporary credentials via the EKS token webhook. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#irsa-roles
- [definition] Envoy Gateway (opt-in) — With the Terraform default (`enable_envoy_gateway = true`), the pre-provisioned ALB stays in front and binds to the Envoy service on port 8080 through a `TargetGroupBinding`, as shown in the [ingress options](#ingress-options) table. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#envoy-gateway-opt-in
- [definition] Egress path with Network Firewall — When `create_firewall = true`, all outbound internet traffic from private subnets is inspected before reaching the NAT gateway: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#egress-path-with-network-firewall
- [definition] Ingress options — Four mutually exclusive ingress options ship with the modules. The choice determines whether split dataplane (agent pods in a separate namespace) is supported. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#ingress-options
- [definition] Why ALB cannot support split dataplane — Standard Kubernetes Ingress is namespace-scoped. The ALB controller routes only to services in the same namespace as the Ingress resource. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#why-alb-cannot-support-split-dataplane
- [definition] ALB plus Envoy Gateway (chained) — When the existing ALB already provides SSO (Okta or Cognito OIDC), WAF, and TLS, Envoy Gateway slots in behind it instead of replacing it: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#alb-plus-envoy-gateway-chained
- [definition] TLS and DNS — The `tls_certificate_source` variable controls the certificate strategy: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#tls-and-dns
- [definition] Why ACM versus cert-manager — ACM certificates are non-exportable. AWS attaches them directly to the ALB, which makes ACM the right choice when TLS terminates at the ALB. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#why-acm-versus-cert-manager
- [definition] Auto-provisioned DNS — When `langsmith_domain` is set and `acm_certificate_arn` is empty, Terraform activates the `dns` module which creates: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#auto-provisioned-dns
- [definition] Bring your own certificate — Set `acm_certificate_arn` directly to skip the `dns` module. For in-cluster gateways, create a Kubernetes TLS Secret manually and reference it in the Gateway or VirtualService. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#bring-your-own-certificate
- [definition] Validated behaviors and known constraints — These constraints were validated during the April 2026 gateway permutation test run. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-architecture#validated-behaviors-and-known-constraints

- [definition] Deploy LangSmith on AWS with Terraform — Deploy LangSmith to AWS with the public [Terraform modules](https://github.com/langchain-ai/terraform/tree/main/modules/aws). Managing the deployment as code lets you version, review, and reproduce your LangSmith environment across accounts instead of clicking through the AWS Console. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#deploy-langsmith-on-aws-with-terraform
- [definition] Required AWS IAM permissions — The IAM user or role running Terraform needs permission to create and manage the cloud foundation. The following managed policies cover the full surface area. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#required-aws-iam-permissions
- [definition] License key and domain — Two non-AWS items must be ready before `terraform apply`: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#license-key-and-domain
- [definition] Cluster sizing reference — Two independent settings control capacity: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#cluster-sizing-reference
- [definition] Quickstart — For a condensed cheat sheet of `make` targets, required variables, and common constraints, see the [AWS quick reference](/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#quickstart
- [definition] Provision infrastructure — Terraform provisions the following AWS resources: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#provision-infrastructure
- [definition] Apply — Provisioning the AWS cloud foundation takes 20 to 25 minutes on a clean account. Do not interrupt the apply. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#apply
- [definition] Deploy LangSmith — Two deployment paths are supported. Pick one. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#deploy-langsmith
- [definition] Script-driven Helm deploy (recommended) — Best for most deployments. Interactive prompts guide you through sizing and product choices. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#script-driven-helm-deploy-recommended
- [definition] Terraform-managed Helm deploy — Best for teams that want the full deployment in Terraform state, or for "bring your own infrastructure" scenarios. The `app/` module manages the External Secrets Operator wiring, the `helm_release`, and feature toggles directly. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#terraform-managed-helm-deploy
- [definition] Enable add-ons — Each add-on is gated by a flag in `infra/terraform.tfvars`. Set the flag, re-run `make init-values` to copy the matching values file, then re-run `make deploy`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#enable-add-ons
- [definition] Fleet — Fleet is the current form of the feature formerly called Agent Builder, deployed as a standalone service (chart v0.15+). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#fleet
- [definition] Optional: private EKS cluster with bastion — For deployments that must run a fully private EKS API endpoint, the modules ship a bastion host pattern: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#optional-private-eks-cluster-with-bastion
- [definition] Optional: Envoy Gateway ingress — The default ingress is the AWS Load Balancer Controller (ALB). Set `enable_envoy_gateway = true` in `terraform.tfvars` to install [Envoy Gateway](https://gateway.envoyproxy.io/) instead. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-deploy#optional-envoy-gateway-ingress

- [snippet] First-time setup: make quickdeploy        # interactive (prompts before terraform apply) — `make quickdeploy        # interactive (prompts before terraform apply)` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#first-time-setup
- [snippet] Day-2 operations: make status — `# Check deployment state across all layers; print next-step guidance` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#day-2-operations
- [snippet] Preflight checks: make preflight — `# Pre-Terraform: AWS credentials + IAM permissions` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#preflight-checks
- [snippet] Add-ons: enable_deployments     = true   # LangGraph Platform (required for Fleet, Agent Builder, and Polly) — `# infra/terraform.tfvars` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#add-ons
- [snippet] Add-ons: make init-values — `make init-values` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#add-ons
- [snippet] Sizing profiles: sizing_profile = "production"        # multi-replica with HPA (recommended) — `sizing_profile = "production"        # multi-replica with HPA (recommended)` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#sizing-profiles
- [snippet] kubectl: kubectl get pods -n langsmith — `# Pod health` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#kubectl
- [snippet] AWS CLI: aws eks list-clusters --region <region> — `# EKS` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#aws-cli
- [snippet] Terraform: cd modules/aws/infra — `cd modules/aws/infra` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#terraform
- [snippet] Teardown: cd terraform/modules/aws — `cd terraform/modules/aws` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#teardown
- [parameter] `make quickstart`: Interactive wizard. Generates `infra/terraform.tfvars` (region, node size, TLS method, add-ons). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#setup-and-secrets
- [parameter] `make setup-env`: Prints the exact `source` command for loading secrets into your shell. Cannot export variables directly. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#setup-and-secrets
- [parameter] `make secrets`: Show SSM secrets status (`✓ SET` / `✗ MISSING`) per parameter, check `TF_VAR_*` exports, give next steps. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#setup-and-secrets
- [parameter] `make secrets-list`: List all SSM parameters for this deployment with last-modified timestamps. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#setup-and-secrets
- [parameter] `make ssm`: Interactive SSM parameter manager. View, set, rotate, validate, diff vs the cluster Secret. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#setup-and-secrets
- [parameter] `make preflight`: Verify AWS credentials, IAM permissions, and required CLI tools before Terraform runs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#preflight
- [parameter] `make preflight-post`: Run after `make apply`. Checks kubectl context, cluster reachability, SSM params populated, Helm values present, TLS config. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#preflight
- [parameter] `make preflight-ssm`: Check SSM params only. Narrower scope than `preflight-post`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#preflight
- [parameter] `make init`: `terraform init`. Downloads providers and modules. Safe to re-run. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#infrastructure
- [parameter] `make plan`: `terraform plan`. Preview changes. Review before every apply. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#infrastructure
- [parameter] `make apply`: `terraform apply`. Provisions VPC, EKS, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, ALB, IRSA. 20 to 25 minutes. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#infrastructure
- [parameter] `make destroy`: `terraform destroy`. Tears down all infrastructure. Run `make uninstall` first. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#infrastructure
- [parameter] `make init-values`: Generate `helm/values/langsmith-values-overrides.yaml` from Terraform outputs. Copy add-on values files based on `enable_*` flags. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#helm-deploy
- [parameter] `make deploy`: Deploy or upgrade LangSmith via Helm. Runs preflight, ESO sync, layered values build, and core readiness checks. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#helm-deploy
- [parameter] `make apply-eso`: Re-apply ESO `ClusterSecretStore` and `ExternalSecret` only. Use after rotating secrets without a full Helm redeploy. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#helm-deploy
- [parameter] `make uninstall`: Uninstall the LangSmith Helm release. Terraform infrastructure stays intact. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#helm-deploy
- [parameter] `make init-app`: Pull live infra Terraform outputs into `app/infra.auto.tfvars.json`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#terraform-managed-helm
- [parameter] `make plan-app`: `terraform plan` for the `app/` module. Auto-runs `init-app` first. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#terraform-managed-helm
- [parameter] `make apply-app`: Deploy LangSmith Helm release via Terraform (`app/` module). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#terraform-managed-helm
- [parameter] `make destroy-app`: Destroy the Helm release via Terraform. Infrastructure stays intact. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#terraform-managed-helm
- [parameter] `make quickdeploy`: Full deploy in one command. Chains `terraform apply` → `kubeconfig` → `init-values` → `helm deploy` with gates. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#fast-path
- [parameter] `make quickdeploy-auto`: Same as `quickdeploy` but non-interactive. Passes `-auto-approve` to terraform. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#fast-path
- [parameter] `make deploy-all`: `make apply` → `make kubeconfig` → `make init-values` → `make deploy` in sequence. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#fast-path
- [parameter] `make deploy-all-tf`: `make apply` → `make init-values` → Terraform `app/` plan and apply in sequence. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#fast-path
- [parameter] `make status`: Check deployment state across all layers, print what to run next. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#utilities
- [parameter] `make status-quick`: Same as `status` but skips SSM and Kubernetes queries (faster). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#utilities
- [parameter] `make kubeconfig`: Print a `source infra/scripts/set-kubeconfig.sh` command to run. Sourcing it exports `KUBECONFIG` to a dedicated `~/.kube/langsmith-<cluster>` file rather than editing `~/.kube/config`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#utilities
- [parameter] `make tls`: BYO ACM cert + Route 53 A alias. Use when `langsmith_domain` is set and you need DNS wiring. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#utilities
- [parameter] `make clean`: Remove all local generated and sensitive files. Run after `make destroy`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#utilities
- [parameter] `make test-e2e`: End-to-end gateway tests (ALB or Envoy Gateway) against the current cluster. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#testing
- [parameter] `make test-permutations`: Permutation tests sequentially on the current cluster. Use `ARGS="1 2 5"` for a subset. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#testing
- [parameter] `make test-parallel`: Permutation tests in parallel across isolated clusters. Your cluster is untouched. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#testing
- [definition] AWS Terraform quick reference — Command cheat sheet for day-to-day operations against an AWS LangSmith deployment provisioned with the [AWS Terraform modules](https://github.com/langchain-ai/terraform/tree/main/modules/aws). All `make` targets run from `modules/aws/`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#aws-terraform-quick-reference
- [definition] Add-ons — Add-ons are controlled by `enable_*` flags in `infra/terraform.tfvars`. Set the flags, re-run `init-values` to copy the matching values files, then re-deploy. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#add-ons
- [definition] Sizing profiles — Set `sizing_profile` in `terraform.tfvars`, then re-run `make init-values && make deploy`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-quick-reference#sizing-profiles

## AWS Terraform troubleshooting
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-troubleshooting>

- [snippet] Automated diagnostics: make status — `# Deployment status across all layers + next-step guidance` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-troubleshooting#automated-diagnostics
- [snippet] EKS node group creation fails: CREATE_FAILED: Error: waiting for EKS Node Group creation: unexpected state 'CREATE_FAILED' — `Error: waiting for EKS Node Group creation: unexpected state 'CREATE_FAILED'` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-troubleshooting#eks-node-group-creation-fails-create-failed
- [snippet] EKS node group creation fails: CREATE_FAILED: aws eks wait cluster-active --name <cluster-name> --region <region> — `aws eks wait cluster-active --name <cluster-name> --region <region>` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-terraform-aws-troubleshooting#eks-node-group-creation-fails-create-failed
