- [parameter] `*TaskPushNotificationConfig`: v0.3 name=—; Supported=Not yet — returns `-32601` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#supported-methods
- [parameter] A2A endpoint: `langgraph-api >= 0.4.21` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#requirements
- [parameter] Inbound `FilePart`: `0.12.0` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#requirements
- [parameter] Tool-result `DataPart`s: `0.12.2` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#requirements
- [parameter] `A2A_ALLOWED_TOOL_CALL_RESULTS`: `0.12.4` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#requirements
- [parameter] Outbound `FilePart`, configurable card modes: `0.13.0` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#requirements
- [parameter] A2UI v0.9: `0.15.0` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#requirements
- [parameter] `historyScope`: `0.15.0` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#requirements
- [parameter] Response wire shape is still v0.3: Tasks, messages and parts carry `kind` and `mimeType` instead of v1.0 member-presence discrimination — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#what-agent-server-currently-fails
- [parameter] Streaming events are flat: SSE emits v0.3 objects with `final`, not `statusUpdate` / `artifactUpdate` wrappers — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#what-agent-server-currently-fails
- [parameter] `tool_results` is snake_case: v1.0 expects `toolResults`. Kept deliberately, because live A2UI clients read this key — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#what-agent-server-currently-fails
- [parameter] Timestamps: Serialized as `+00:00` rather than an ISO 8601 `Z` suffix — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#what-agent-server-currently-fails
- [parameter] `SubscribeToTask`: Returns `-32601` where the spec requires `-32001` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#what-agent-server-currently-fails
- [parameter] Push notification config: Returns `-32601` where the spec requires `-32003` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#what-agent-server-currently-fails
- [parameter] Errors carry no `data`: No `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` reason or domain is attached — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#what-agent-server-currently-fails
- [parameter] `A2A-Version` request header: Not read, so an unsupported version is processed instead of returning `-32009` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#what-agent-server-currently-fails
- [parameter] Agent card caching: No `Cache-Control`, `ETag` or `Last-Modified` headers — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#what-agent-server-currently-fails
- [parameter] `GetExtendedAgentCard`: Served, but never advertised via `capabilities.extendedAgentCard` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#what-agent-server-currently-fails
- [definition] A2A endpoint in Agent Server — [Agent2Agent (A2A)](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/) is Google's protocol for enabling communication between conversational AI agents. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#a2a-endpoint-in-agent-server
- [definition] Protocol version — Agent Server speaks the A2A **v1.0** JSON-RPC binding and also accepts the v0.3 method names, so existing v0.3 clients keep working. The agent card declares one interface: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#protocol-version
- [definition] Task history in responses — A context holds many tasks. By default `SendMessage`, `GetTask` and `ListTasks` return the history of the **whole context**, not just the task you asked about. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#task-history-in-responses
- [definition] Agent card discovery — Each assistant automatically exposes an A2A Agent Card that describes its capabilities and provides the information needed for other agents to connect. You can retrieve the agent card for any assistant using: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#agent-card-discovery
- [definition] Optional capabilities — These are configured per assistant through `metadata.a2a` on the Assistants API. `langgraph.json` cannot set assistant metadata, so patch the assistant after deploy. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#optional-capabilities
- [definition] File parts — `FilePart` works in both directions. Inbound file, image, audio and video parts become LangChain content blocks. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#file-parts
- [definition] Filter tool results — By default every correlated tool result is published as a `DataPart`. To publish only some, set an allowlist of tool names on the deployment: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#filter-tool-results
- [definition] Creating an A2A-compatible agent — This example creates an A2A-compatible agent that processes incoming messages using OpenAI's API and maintains conversational state. The agent defines a message-based state structure and handles the A2A protocol's message format. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#creating-an-a2a-compatible-agent
- [definition] Agent-to-agent communication — Once your agents are running locally via `langgraph dev` or [deployed to production](/langsmith/deployment), you can facilitate communication between them using the A2A protocol. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#agent-to-agent-communication
- [definition] Distributed tracing — When multiple agents communicate over A2A, LangSmith can group all their [traces](/langsmith/observability-concepts#traces) into a single [thread](/langsmith/observability-concepts#threads), which gives you a unified view of the entire multi-agent conversation. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#distributed-tracing
- [definition] How contextId maps to thread_id — The Agent Server A2A endpoint automatically converts the A2A `contextId` to `thread_id` for LangSmith tracing. This means every message in a conversation, across all participating agents, is grouped under the same thread in LangSmith without any extra configuration on your part. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#how-contextid-maps-to-thread-id
- [definition] Tracing across multiple agents — When agents from different frameworks communicate over A2A, `contextId` is what unifies their traces. Reuse the `contextId` returned by the first agent on every later request, to that agent and to the others. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#tracing-across-multiple-agents
- [definition] Receive thread_id in non-LangGraph agents — The [previous section](#tracing-across-multiple-agents) covers the client side — propagating `contextId` when sending messages. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#receive-thread-id-in-non-langgraph-agents
- [definition] View traces in LangSmith — After running a multi-agent conversation, open the [LangSmith UI](https://smith.langchain.com?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-server-a2a) and navigate to **Threads**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#view-traces-in-langsmith
- [definition] Against the official conformance suite — A2A publishes a Technology Compatibility Kit at [a2aproject/a2a-tck](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-tck). It grades an implementation by RFC 2119 level and works against any A2A endpoint, including yours. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#against-the-official-conformance-suite
- [definition] What Agent Server currently fails — Agent Server runs the TCK on every CI build as a required check, gated against a checked-in list of known failures. CI fails if a new failure appears, and also if a listed requirement starts passing, so the list cannot drift from what the server actually does. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#what-agent-server-currently-fails
- [definition] Disable A2A — To disable the A2A endpoint, set `disable_a2a` to `true` in your `langgraph.json` configuration file: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/server-a2a#disable-a2a

## Set up hierarchy
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-hierarchy>

- [definition] Set up hierarchy — This page describes setting up and managing your LangSmith [_organization_](/langsmith/administration-overview#organizations) and [_workspaces_](/langsmith/administration-overview#workspaces): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-hierarchy#set-up-hierarchy
- [definition] Set up an organization — If you're interested in managing your organization and workspaces programmatically, refer to [Manage organizations using the API](/langsmith/manage-organization-by-api). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-hierarchy#set-up-an-organization
- [definition] Create an organization — When you log into the [UI](https://smith.langchain.com?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-set-up-hierarchy) for the first time, LangSmith will create a personal organization for you automatically. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-hierarchy#create-an-organization
- [definition] Manage and navigate workspaces — Once you've subscribed to a [plan](/langsmith/pricing-plans) that allows for multiple users per organization, you can set up [workspaces](/langsmith/administration-overview#workspaces) to collaborate more effectively and isolate LangSmith resources between different groups of users. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-hierarchy#manage-and-navigate-workspaces
- [definition] Manage users — Manage membership in your shared organization in the **Members and roles** tabs on the [Settings page](https://smith.langchain.com/settings). Here you can: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-hierarchy#manage-users
- [definition] Set up a workspace — When you log in for the first time, LangSmith will create a default [workspace](/langsmith/administration-overview#workspaces) for you in your personal organization. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-hierarchy#set-up-a-workspace
- [definition] Create a workspace — To create a new workspace, navigate to the [**Settings** page](https://smith.langchain.com/settings) **Workspaces** tab in your shared organization and click **Add Workspace**. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-hierarchy#create-a-workspace
- [definition] Manage users — Only [workspace admins](/langsmith/rbac#workspace-admin) can manage workspace membership and, if RBAC is enabled, change a user's workspace role. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-hierarchy#manage-users
- [definition] Configure workspace settings — Workspace configuration exists in the [**Workspaces settings** page](https://smith.langchain.com/settings/workspaces) tab. Select the workspace to configure and then the desired configuration sub-tab. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-hierarchy#configure-workspace-settings
- [definition] Delete a workspace — Deleting a workspace will permanently delete the workspace and all associated data. This action cannot be undone. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-hierarchy#delete-a-workspace
- [definition] Set up applications — You can create applications within a workspace to further organize resources, such as tracing projects and datasets. A workspace may have zero or more applications. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-hierarchy#set-up-applications

- [snippet] Create a tag value: response = requests.post( — `response = requests.post(` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#create-a-tag-value

- [snippet] Assign a tag to a resource: tags = requests.get( — `tags = requests.get(` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#assign-a-tag-to-a-resource
- [snippet] Tag a resource at creation time: tags = requests.get( — `# Look up the tag value IDs you want to apply` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#tag-a-resource-at-creation-time
- [snippet] Query tags: tags = requests.get( — `# All tag keys and values in the workspace` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#query-tags
- [snippet] Remove a tag from a resource: requests.delete( — `requests.delete(` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#remove-a-tag-from-a-resource
- [snippet] Delete a tag key or value: requests.delete( — `# Delete a value (removes all resource assignments for that value)` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#delete-a-tag-key-or-value
- [parameter] `POST /api/v1/sessions`: Create a tracing project — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#tag-a-resource-at-creation-time
- [parameter] `POST /api/v1/datasets`: Create a dataset (also accepted on CSV upload and experiment upload variants) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#tag-a-resource-at-creation-time
- [parameter] `POST /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/clone`: Clone a dataset — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#tag-a-resource-at-creation-time
- [parameter] `POST /api/v1/repos`: Create a prompt — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#tag-a-resource-at-creation-time
- [parameter] `POST /api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/fork`: Fork a prompt — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#tag-a-resource-at-creation-time
- [definition] Set up resource tags — Resource tags are available for [Plus and Enterprise plans](/langsmith/pricing-plans). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#set-up-resource-tags
- [definition] Create a tag — To create resource tags, you must have the [`workspaces:manage` permission](/langsmith/organization-workspace-operations) (granted to the [workspace admin](/langsmith/rbac#workspace-admin) role by default). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#create-a-tag
- [definition] Assign a tag to a resource — Within the same side panel for creating a new tag, you can also assign resources to tags. Search for corresponding resources in the **Assign resources** section and select the resources you want to tag. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#assign-a-tag-to-a-resource
- [definition] Delete a tag — You can delete either a key or a value of a tag from the [**Settings** page > **Resource tags** page](https://smith.langchain.com/settings/workspaces/resource_tags). To delete a key, click the <Icon icon="trash" /> trash icon next to the key. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#delete-a-tag
- [definition] Manage tags via API — You can create, assign, and query resource tags programmatically using the LangSmith REST API. All tag endpoints live under `/api/v1/workspaces/current/` and require an [API key](/langsmith/create-account-api-key). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#manage-tags-via-api
- [definition] Set up — Import the `requests` library and configure your API key and headers. All the following examples assume these variables are in scope: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#set-up
- [definition] Create a tag key — Creating tag keys requires the [`workspaces:manage`](/langsmith/organization-workspace-operations) permission. If you want to apply the default **Application** key, skip this step and list existing keys instead. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#create-a-tag-key
- [definition] Tag a resource at creation time — You can supply `tag_value_ids` when creating a project, dataset, or prompt (including fork and clone operations). The tags are applied atomically in the same transaction as resource creation, so the resource is never briefly untagged — important when [ABAC policies](/langsmith/abac) are enforced. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/set-up-resource-tags#tag-a-resource-at-creation-time

## LangSmith shared responsibility model
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/shared-responsibility-model>

- [parameter] **Infrastructure**: LangChain responsibility (provider)=We manage the underlying cloud infrastructure (via AWS and GCP), including servers, networking, OS patching, and capacity planning. AWS and GCP own the physical data centers.; Customer responsibility (user)=N/A. You do not provision or maintain compute resources in the SaaS environment. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/shared-responsibility-model#responsibility-matrix
- [parameter] **Application**: LangChain responsibility (provider)=We secure the LangSmith application code, API endpoints, and database clusters, including code scanning and penetration testing.; Customer responsibility (user)=You are responsible for the security and safety of the AI chains and agents you build using our SDKs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/shared-responsibility-model#responsibility-matrix
- [parameter] **Data**: LangChain responsibility (provider)=We enforce tenant isolation and encrypt data at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.; Customer responsibility (user)=You control what data is sent to us and must filter sensitive PII via the SDK before it leaves your environment. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/shared-responsibility-model#responsibility-matrix
- [parameter] **Identity**: LangChain responsibility (provider)=We provide the guardrails, including SSO/SCIM, MFA enforcement options, and RBAC frameworks.; Customer responsibility (user)=You manage your user roster, assign roles (e.g., Admin vs. Viewer), and revoke access for terminated employees. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/shared-responsibility-model#responsibility-matrix
- [parameter] **Secrets**: LangChain responsibility (provider)=We securely store the secrets you entrust to the platform.; Customer responsibility (user)=You are responsible for rotating your API keys and ensuring they are not hard-coded in your applications. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/shared-responsibility-model#responsibility-matrix
- [definition] LangSmith shared responsibility model — LangSmith is a multi-tenant SaaS product. Under the shared responsibility model, LangChain secures the platform infrastructure and application, and you secure your usage, data inputs, and the agents you build. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/shared-responsibility-model#langsmith-shared-responsibility-model
- [definition] Customer security best practices — To align with the security assumptions in our SOC 2 Type II framework, we recommend customers maintain the following internal guidelines: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/shared-responsibility-model#customer-security-best-practices

- [definition] Migrate feedback and sharing methods to SmithDB — These methods add runs to annotation queues, share runs publicly, and create feedback. For deprecation dates, minimum SDK versions, and the agent prompt that applies to every method, see [Migrate to SmithDB-backed SDK methods](/langsmith/smithdb-sdk-migration). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/smithdb-sdk-migration-feedback#migrate-feedback-and-sharing-methods-to-smithdb
- [definition] Annotation queues: add runs — Add runs to an annotation queue. The SmithDB-backed path takes each run's full lookup key—its ID plus the `session_id` (project UUID) and `start_time` partition keys—so the run can be located directly instead of scanned for. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/smithdb-sdk-migration-feedback#annotation-queues-add-runs
- [definition] Share and read public runs — Share a trace, remove its public access, or read the runs in a publicly shared trace. The v2 methods use explicit SmithDB coordinates and return select-driven run objects. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/smithdb-sdk-migration-feedback#share-and-read-public-runs
- [definition] Examples — The examples query the public trace before the point read because `public.runs.retrieve` requires the run's exact stored `start_time`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/smithdb-sdk-migration-feedback#examples
- [definition] Feedback: create — Create feedback (a score, correction, or comment) for a run. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/smithdb-sdk-migration-feedback#feedback-create

- [definition] Migrate thread methods to SmithDB — These methods query threads and list the traces inside a thread. For deprecation dates, minimum SDK versions, and the agent prompt that applies to every method, see [Migrate to SmithDB-backed SDK methods](/langsmith/smithdb-sdk-migration). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/smithdb-sdk-migration-threads#migrate-thread-methods-to-smithdb
- [definition] Threads: query — Query threads within a project, with cursor-based pagination. Returns threads matching the given time range and optional filter. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/smithdb-sdk-migration-threads#threads-query
- [definition] Threads: list traces — Retrieve all traces belonging to a specific thread within a project. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/smithdb-sdk-migration-threads#threads-list-traces

## Isolate store data per user

- [snippet] Use namespaces in agent code: from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableConfig — `from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableConfig` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#use-namespaces-in-agent-code

- [parameter] **Explicit namespace + deny**: Where user scope is set=Application code puts `user_id` first in every namespace; Best when=You already pass user identity into graph code, or you want namespaces to reflect the full storage path — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#choose-a-store-authorization-pattern
- [parameter] **Automatic prefix rewriting**: Where user scope is set=Auth handler prepends `ctx.user.identity` to logical namespaces; Best when=You want simpler agent code and transparent isolation at the API layer — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#choose-a-store-authorization-pattern
- [parameter] Conversation history: Mechanism=Thread metadata filters (`owner`); Scopes=Per-thread checkpoints and messages — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#combine-with-thread-isolation
- [parameter] Long-term memory: Mechanism=Store namespace rewriting; Scopes=Cross-thread memories, preferences, and documents — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#combine-with-thread-isolation
- [definition] Isolate store data per user — Every [LangSmith Deployment](/langsmith/deployment) includes a Postgres-backed [store](/oss/python/langgraph/stores) for long-term memory and cross-thread data. By default, store namespaces are shared across all callers. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#isolate-store-data-per-user
- [definition] How it works — Store items are organized by a **namespace** tuple (for example, `("memories", "preferences")`) and a **key**. Unlike threads and assistants, store namespaces are defined by your application, so authorization works differently: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#how-it-works
- [definition] Configure auth in LangSmith Deployment — Point your deployment at your auth module in [`langgraph.json`](/langsmith/application-structure#configuration-file-concepts): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#configure-auth-in-langsmith-deployment
- [definition] Choose a store authorization pattern — Store isolation requires a `@auth.on.store` handler. Two common patterns work well; pick one based on where you want user scoping to live. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#choose-a-store-authorization-pattern
- [definition] Explicit namespace + deny — Your application code includes the user's identity as the first segment of every namespace (for example, `("user-123", "memories")`). The auth handler validates that the caller matches that prefix and rejects mismatches: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#explicit-namespace-deny
- [definition] Automatic prefix rewriting — Your application code uses logical namespaces without a user prefix (for example, `("memories", "preferences")`). The auth handler prepends the authenticated user's identity on every store operation: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#automatic-prefix-rewriting
- [definition] Use namespaces in agent code — If you use automatic prefix rewriting, your graph code uses logical namespaces without the user prefix. The auth layer adds the user scope automatically at request time. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#use-namespaces-in-agent-code
- [definition] Deep Agents and StoreBackend — If you use [Deep Agents](/oss/python/deepagents/overview) with a [`StoreBackend`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/deepagents/backends/store/StoreBackend), align your namespace factory with the auth-scoped layout. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#deep-agents-and-storebackend
- [definition] Test store isolation — With `langgraph dev` running and two test users configured in your auth handler, verify that store data does not leak across users: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#test-store-isolation
- [definition] Combine with thread isolation — Store isolation and [thread isolation](/langsmith/resource-auth) solve different problems: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/store-auth#combine-with-thread-isolation

- [parameter] **SDK method**: Thread streaming=`client.threads.join_stream()`; Run streaming=`client.runs.stream()` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#compare-thread-and-run-streaming
- [parameter] **REST endpoint**: Thread streaming=`GET /threads/{thread_id}/stream`; Run streaming=`POST /threads/{thread_id}/runs/stream` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#compare-thread-and-run-streaming
- [parameter] **Scope**: Thread streaming=All runs on a thread; Run streaming=A single run — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#compare-thread-and-run-streaming
- [parameter] **Connection lifetime**: Thread streaming=Open indefinitely; Run streaming=Closes when the run completes — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#compare-thread-and-run-streaming
- [parameter] **Creates a run**: Thread streaming=No; Run streaming=Yes — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#compare-thread-and-run-streaming
- [parameter] **Use case**: Thread streaming=Monitor ongoing thread activity; Run streaming=Execute and stream a single interaction — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#compare-thread-and-run-streaming
- [parameter] `run_modes` (default): Streams all run events, equivalent to `client.runs.stream()` output. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#thread-stream-modes
- [parameter] `lifecycle`: Streams only run start and end events. Use this for lightweight monitoring of run status without the full output. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#thread-stream-modes
- [parameter] `state_update`: Streams only state update events, providing the thread state after each run completes. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#thread-stream-modes
- [definition] Streaming API — The [LangGraph SDK](/langsmith/langgraph-python-sdk) lets you stream outputs from the [LangSmith Deployment API](/langsmith/server-api-ref) in multiple modes, from full state snapshots after each step to token-by-token LLM output. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#streaming-api
- [definition] Stream multiple modes — You can pass a list as the `stream_mode` parameter to stream multiple modes at once. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#stream-multiple-modes
- [definition] Stream graph state — Use the stream modes `updates` and `values` to stream the state of the graph as it executes. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#stream-graph-state
- [definition] Stream mode: `updates` — Use this to stream only the **state updates** returned by the nodes after each step. The streamed outputs include the name of the node as well as the update. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#stream-mode-updates
- [definition] Stream mode: `values` — Use this to stream the **full state** of the graph after each step. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#stream-mode-values
- [definition] Subgraphs — To include outputs from [subgraphs](/oss/python/langgraph/use-subgraphs) in the streamed outputs, you can set `subgraphs=True` in the `.stream()` method of the parent graph. This will stream outputs from both the parent graph and any subgraphs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#subgraphs
- [definition] Debugging — Use the `debug` streaming mode to stream as much information as possible throughout the execution of the graph. The streamed outputs include the name of the node as well as the full state. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#debugging
- [definition] LLM tokens — Use the `messages-tuple` streaming mode to stream Large Language Model (LLM) outputs **token by token** from any part of your graph, including nodes, tools, subgraphs, or tasks. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#llm-tokens
- [definition] Stream events — To stream all events, including the state of the graph: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#stream-events
- [definition] Stateless runs — If you don't want to **persist the outputs** of a streaming run in the [checkpointer](/oss/python/langgraph/persistence) DB, you can create a stateless run without creating a thread: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#stateless-runs
- [definition] Join and stream — LangSmith allows you to join an active [background run](/langsmith/background-run) and stream outputs from it. To do so, you can use [LangGraph SDK's](/langsmith/langgraph-python-sdk) `client.runs.join_stream` method: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#join-and-stream
- [definition] Stream a thread — Thread streaming opens a long-lived connection for a thread and streams output from **every run** executed on that thread. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#stream-a-thread
- [definition] Thread stream modes — Thread streaming supports three stream modes that control which events are returned. Pass one or more modes via the `stream_mode` parameter. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#thread-stream-modes
- [definition] Resume from last event — Thread streams support resumability via the `Last-Event-ID` header. If the connection drops, pass the ID of the last event you received to resume without missing events. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#resume-from-last-event
- [definition] API reference — For API usage and implementation, refer to the [API reference](/langsmith/server-api-ref). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/streaming#api-reference

- [definition] Group a conversation into a thread — Each wrapped session is captured as its own trace with its own thread ID. - [definition] Use Google ADK — Use this approach when ADK owns the Gemini Live session and tool loop. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-gemini-live#use-google-adk
- [definition] Set up tracing — Import `LangSmithGoogleADKLivePlugin` and register it on your `Runner`. It runs alongside your `run_live` loop, so your loop only handles audio playback, barge-ins, and UI updates: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-gemini-live#set-up-tracing
- [definition] Group a conversation into a thread — Each conversation is captured as its own trace with its own thread ID. ## Trace query syntax
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax>

- [snippet] Logical operators: and(eq(run_type, "llm"), gt(latency, "2s")) — `and(eq(run_type, "llm"), gt(latency, "2s"))` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#logical-operators
- [snippet] Filter by run name: eq(name, "my_chain") — `eq(name, "my_chain")` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-by-run-name
- [snippet] Filter by error status: eq(status, "error") — `# Runs that errored` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-by-error-status
- [snippet] Filter by latency: gt(latency, "5s") — `# Runs slower than 5 seconds` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-by-latency
- [snippet] Filter by time range: and(gt(start_time, "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"), lt(start_time, "2024-02-01T00:00:00Z")) — `and(gt(start_time, "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"), lt(start_time, "2024-02-01T00:00:00Z"))` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-by-time-range
- [snippet] Filter by tags: has(tags, "production") — `has(tags, "production")` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-by-tags
- [snippet] Filter by metadata key or value: eq(metadata_key, "user_id") — `# Runs with a "user_id" metadata key` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-by-metadata-key-or-value
- [snippet] Filter by thread ID: and(in(metadata_key, ["session_id", "thread_id"]), eq(metadata_value, "<your_thread_id>")) — `and(in(metadata_key, ["session_id", "thread_id"]), eq(metadata_value, "<your_thread_id>"))` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-by-thread-id
- [snippet] Filter by feedback score: and(eq(feedback_key, "thumbs_up"), eq(feedback_score, 1)) — `# Runs with a "thumbs_up" score of 1` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-by-feedback-score
- [snippet] Full-text search across all string fields: search("my search term") — `search("my search term")` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#full-text-search-across-all-string-fields
- [snippet] Combining conditions: and(gt(start_time, "2024-06-01T00:00:00Z"), eq(status, "error")) — `# Errors that started after a specific time` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#combining-conditions
- [snippet] Using trace_filter and tree_filter: eq(name, "RetrieveDocs") — `# filter: the run you want` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#using-trace-filter-and-tree-filter
- [parameter] `project_id` / `project_name`: The project(s) to fetch runs from, as a single project or a list of projects. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `trace_id`: Fetch runs that are part of a specific trace. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `run_type`: The [type of run](/langsmith/run-data-format#run-types) to get, for example, `llm`, `chain`, `tool`, `retriever`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `dataset_name` / `dataset_id`: Fetch runs that are associated with an example row in the specified dataset. This is useful for comparing prompts or models over a given dataset. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `reference_example_id`: Fetch runs that are associated with a specific example row. This is useful for comparing prompts or models on a given input. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `parent_run_id`: Fetch runs that are children of a given run. This is useful for fetching runs grouped together using the context manager or for fetching an agent trajectory. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `error`: Fetch runs that errored or did not error. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `run_ids`: Fetch runs with a given list of run ids. Note: **This will ignore all other filtering arguments.** — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `filter`: Fetch runs that match a given structured filter statement. For more details, refer to the [filter query language](#filter-query-language) section. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `trace_filter`: Filter applied to the root run of the trace. Use with `filter` to narrow by attributes of the root run. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `tree_filter`: Filter applied to any run in the trace tree (root, sibling, or child). Use with `filter` to narrow by attributes of any run within a trace. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `is_root`: Only return root runs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `select`: Select the fields to return in the response. By default, all fields are returned. See [run data format](/langsmith/run-data-format) for available fields. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `query` (_experimental_): Natural language query, which translates your query into a filter statement. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-arguments
- [parameter] `eq`: Description=Equal to; Example=`eq(run_type, "llm")` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#comparators
- [parameter] `neq`: Description=Not equal to; Example=`neq(status, "error")` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#comparators
- [parameter] `gt`: Description=Greater than; Example=`gt(latency, "5s")` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#comparators
- [parameter] `gte`: Description=Greater than or equal to; Example=`gte(latency, 1.5)` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#comparators
- [parameter] `lt`: Description=Less than; Example=`lt(start_time, "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z")` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#comparators
- [parameter] `lte`: Description=Less than or equal to; Example=`lte(feedback_score, 0.5)` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#comparators
- [parameter] `has`: Description=Check if the run contains a tag or metadata key-value; Example=`has(tags, "production")` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#comparators
- [parameter] `search`: Description=Search for a substring across all string fields; Example=`search("invoice")` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#comparators
- [parameter] `in`: Description=Check if a field value is in a list; Example=`in(metadata_key, ["session_id", "thread_id"])` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#comparators
- [parameter] `id`: Type=string (UUID); Notes=Run ID — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filterable-fields
- [parameter] `name`: Type=string; Notes=Name of the run — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filterable-fields
- [parameter] `run_type`: Type=string; Notes=One of `llm`, `chain`, `tool`, `retriever`, `embedding`, `prompt`, `parser` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filterable-fields
- [parameter] `status`: Type=string; Notes=`"success"`, `"error"`, or `"pending"`. Use this to filter errored vs. successful runs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filterable-fields
- [parameter] `start_time`: Type=ISO 8601 string; Notes=e.g. `"2024-01-15T00:00:00Z"` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filterable-fields
- [parameter] `end_time`: Type=ISO 8601 string — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filterable-fields
- [parameter] `latency`: Type=duration string or number; Notes=Seconds, e.g. `"5s"`, `"1.5s"`, or `1.5`. Only the `s` suffix is supported. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filterable-fields
- [parameter] `tags`: Type=list of strings; Notes=Use `has(tags, "value")` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filterable-fields
- [parameter] `metadata_key`: Type=string; Notes=Key in the run's metadata dict — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filterable-fields
- [parameter] `metadata_value`: Type=string; Notes=Value in the run's metadata dict — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filterable-fields
- [parameter] `feedback_key`: Type=string; Notes=Name of a feedback score — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filterable-fields
- [parameter] `feedback_score`: Type=number; Notes=Numeric value of a feedback score — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filterable-fields
- [definition] Trace query syntax — The [LangSmith SDK](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langsmith/) and [REST API](/langsmith/smith-api-ref) let you filter, query, and export [runs](/langsmith/observability-concepts#runs) programmatically using a set of filter arguments and a structured filter query language. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#trace-query-syntax
- [definition] Filter query language — LangSmith supports filtering capabilities with a filter query language to permit complex filtering operations when fetching runs. This is especially useful when querying traces programmatically via the SDK or API. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#filter-query-language
- [definition] Comparators — The filtering grammar is based on comparator functions applied to fields of the run object: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#comparators
- [definition] Logical operators — Use `and` and `or` to combine multiple comparators: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#logical-operators
- [definition] Quick reference examples — The following examples show the filter string only. Pass the string as the `filter`, `trace_filter`, or `tree_filter` argument in `client.list_runs()` or the `/runs/query` API endpoint. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#quick-reference-examples
- [definition] Using trace_filter and tree_filter — `filter` applies to the returned run. `trace_filter` applies to the root run of the trace. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-query-syntax#using-trace-filter-and-tree-filter

## Voice tracing fundamentals
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals>

- [snippet] Trace each conversation as a single trace: conversation                      ← root run (whole conversation; combined audio; ls_modality="audio") — `conversation                      ← root run (whole conversation; combined audio; ls_modality="audio` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals#trace-each-conversation-as-a-single-trace
- [snippet] Trace each conversation as a single trace: conversation                      ← root run (whole conversation; combined audio; ls_modality="audio") — `conversation                      ← root run (whole conversation; combined audio; ls_modality="audio` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals#trace-each-conversation-as-a-single-trace
- [snippet] Python: from langsmith import traceable — `from langsmith import traceable` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals#record-a-single-combined-audio-file
- [snippet] Python: from langsmith import traceable — `from langsmith import traceable` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals#mark-the-trace-as-audio
- [definition] Voice tracing fundamentals — [Tracing](/langsmith/observability-concepts#traces) a voice agent is different from tracing a text agent. A conversation is continuous, bidirectional, and interruptible: users talk over the agent, change topics mid-sentence, and expect sub-second responses. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals#voice-tracing-fundamentals
- [definition] Two architectures, two trace shapes — How you build a voice agent determines what the trace looks like. There are two common architectures, and they produce fundamentally different traces. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals#two-architectures-two-trace-shapes
- [definition] Cascade — A cascade chains together separate, single-purpose models: speech-to-text (STT) transcribes the user's audio, a language model (LLM) reasons over the text and decides what to do, and text-to-speech (TTS) synthesizes the reply. Middleware, tool calls, and retrieval steps sit in between. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals#cascade
- [definition] Speech-to-speech (S2S) — A speech-to-speech model (such as the [OpenAI Realtime API](/langsmith/trace-openai-realtime) or [Gemini Live](/langsmith/trace-gemini-live)) processes audio natively and replies with audio over a single persistent connection, typically a WebSocket. There is no STT/LLM/TTS decomposition to trace. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals#speech-to-speech-s2s
- [definition] Core conventions — These are the practices we recommend for getting the most out of voice traces in LangSmith. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals#core-conventions
- [definition] Trace each conversation as a single trace — A conversation is a single interaction, so we recommend keeping it in a single trace, with the individual model calls or events nested underneath one root run that represents the whole conversation. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals#trace-each-conversation-as-a-single-trace
- [definition] Record a single combined audio file — Attach **one** audio file to the root run that contains **both** the user and the agent, recorded from **what was actually played to the client**, not the audio the model generated. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals#record-a-single-combined-audio-file
- [definition] Mark the trace as audio — Set the `ls_modality` metadata field to `"audio"` on the root run. This flags the trace as a voice trace so LangSmith can render it appropriately and so you can [filter](/langsmith/filter-traces-in-application) for voice traces in your project. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-voice-fundamentals#mark-the-trace-as-audio

## Trace with API
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-api>

- [snippet] expandable wrap: import openai — `import openai` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-api#basic-tracing
- [snippet] expandable: import json — `import json` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-api#batch-ingestion
- [definition] Trace with API — This guide covers two approaches to tracing with the [REST API](/langsmith/smith-api-ref): basic tracing using the `POST /runs` and `PATCH /runs` endpoints, and batch ingestion using `POST /runs/multipart` for higher throughput. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-api#trace-with-api
- [definition] Basic tracing — The simplest way to log runs is via the `POST /runs` and `PATCH /runs` endpoints. This approach requires minimal information to establish the trace hierarchy. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-api#basic-tracing
- [definition] Batch ingestion — For faster ingestion and higher rate limits, use the [`POST /runs/multipart`](/langsmith/smith-api/runs/ingest-runs-multipart) endpoint. This requires the [`requests-toolbelt`](https://pypi.org/project/requests-toolbelt/) and [`uuid-utils`](https://pypi.org/project/uuid-utils/) packages. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-api#batch-ingestion

- [parameter] `TRACE_TO_LANGSMITH`: Required=Yes; Default=-; Description=Set to `"true"` to enable tracing. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#environment-variables
- [parameter] `LANGSMITH_CODEX_API_KEY`: Required=Conditional; Default=-; Description=LangSmith API key. Falls back to `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`. Required unless every replica provides its own API key. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#environment-variables
- [parameter] `LANGSMITH_CODEX_ENDPOINT`: Required=No; Default=`https://api.smith.langchain.com`; Description=LangSmith API URL. Falls back to `LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#environment-variables
- [parameter] `LANGSMITH_CODEX_PROJECT`: Required=No; Default=`codex`; Description=LangSmith project name. Falls back to `LANGSMITH_PROJECT`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#environment-variables
- [parameter] `LANGSMITH_CODEX_METADATA`: Required=No; Default=-; Description=JSON object merged into root trace metadata. Falls back to `LANGSMITH_METADATA`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#environment-variables
- [parameter] `LANGSMITH_CODEX_RUNS_ENDPOINTS`: Required=No; Default=-; Description=JSON array of replica destinations. Falls back to `LANGSMITH_RUNS_ENDPOINTS`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#environment-variables
- [parameter] `enabled`: Environment variable=`TRACE_TO_LANGSMITH`; Default=`false`; Description=Set to `true` to enable tracing. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#config-file
- [parameter] `api_key`: Environment variable=`LANGSMITH_CODEX_API_KEY`, `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`; Default=-; Description=LangSmith API key. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#config-file
- [parameter] `api_url`: Environment variable=`LANGSMITH_CODEX_ENDPOINT`, `LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT`; Default=LangSmith default; Description=LangSmith API URL. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#config-file
- [parameter] `project`: Environment variable=`LANGSMITH_CODEX_PROJECT`, `LANGSMITH_PROJECT`; Default=`codex`; Description=LangSmith project name. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#config-file
- [parameter] `metadata`: Environment variable=`LANGSMITH_CODEX_METADATA`, `LANGSMITH_METADATA`; Default=-; Description=Object merged into root trace metadata. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#config-file
- [parameter] `replicas`: Environment variable=`LANGSMITH_CODEX_RUNS_ENDPOINTS`, `LANGSMITH_RUNS_ENDPOINTS`; Default=-; Description=Additional LangSmith destinations to replicate traces to. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#config-file
- [parameter] `apiUrl`: Required=Yes; Description=LangSmith API URL (typically `https://api.smith.langchain.com`). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#trace-to-multiple-destinations
- [parameter] `apiKey`: Required=Yes; Description=API key for the destination workspace. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#trace-to-multiple-destinations
- [parameter] `projectName`: Required=Yes; Description=Project name in the destination workspace. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#trace-to-multiple-destinations
- [parameter] `updates`: Required=No; Description=Optional run fields to override on replicated runs, such as extra metadata. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#trace-to-multiple-destinations
- [definition] Trace OpenAI Codex sessions — The [`langsmith-codex-plugins`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langsmith-codex-plugins) marketplace ships a tracing plugin that sends [OpenAI Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex) session data to LangSmith. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#trace-openai-codex-sessions
- [definition] Prerequisites — Before setting up tracing, ensure you have: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#prerequisites
- [definition] Install and enable the plugin — Add the marketplace using the Codex CLI: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#install-and-enable-the-plugin
- [definition] Configure tracing — Tracing is disabled until either `TRACE_TO_LANGSMITH` is `"true"` or `enabled` is `true` in a config file. Configure credentials with environment variables, a JSON config file, or both. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#configure-tracing
- [definition] Environment variables — The plugin reads Codex-specific variables first, then falls back to the generic LangSmith SDK variables. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#environment-variables
- [definition] Config file — Use `<project>/.codex/langsmith.json` for project-level settings or `~/.codex/langsmith.json` for global defaults. The global file loads first, the project file overrides it, and matching environment variables take precedence over both. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#config-file
- [definition] Trace to multiple destinations — Set `replicas` in `langsmith.json` or `LANGSMITH_CODEX_RUNS_ENDPOINTS` to send the same trace data to additional LangSmith workspaces or projects. When set, the replica list overrides the other client settings. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#trace-to-multiple-destinations
- [definition] View traces in LangSmith — Open the configured LangSmith project and complete a Codex turn. By default traces appear in the `codex` project. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-codex#view-traces-in-langsmith

- [parameter] `project`: Environment variable=`LANGSMITH_CURSOR_PROJECT`, `LANGSMITH_PROJECT`; Default=`cursor`; Description=LangSmith project name. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#config-file

- [parameter] `attachments`: Environment variable=`LANGSMITH_CURSOR_ATTACHMENTS`; Default=`true`; Description=Set to `false` to skip enriching turns with image and file attachment bytes from Cursor's local database. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#config-file
- [parameter] `cursor_db_path`: Environment variable=`LANGSMITH_CURSOR_DB_PATH`; Default=platform default; Description=Override the Cursor `state.vscdb` path used for attachments. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#config-file
- [parameter] Always present: `ls_agent_type` (`"root"`, `"subagent"`, `"middleware"`, or `"compaction"`), `ls_agent_purpose` (`"coding"`), `ls_integration` (`"cursor"`), `ls_agent_runtime` (`"Cursor"`), `ls_trace_schema_version` (`"coding-agent-v1"`), `thread_id` (= Cursor's `conversation_id`). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#trace-metadata
- [parameter] Present where known: `ls_integration_version`, `ls_agent_runtime_version` (Cursor's `cursor_version`), `turn_id` (= Cursor's `generation_id`), `turn_number`, `repository_url`, `repository_provider`, `repository_name`, `git_branch`, `git_commit_sha`, `cwd`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#trace-metadata
- [parameter] Contextual: `local_username`, `user_email` (provisional). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#trace-metadata
- [parameter] Subagent runs only: `ls_subagent_id`, `ls_subagent_type`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#trace-metadata
- [parameter] Tool runs only: `ls_tool_name` (only emitted when the run name differs from the native tool name). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#trace-metadata
- [parameter] Model and tool runs only: `ls_provider`, `ls_model_name`, `ls_invocation_params`, `usage_metadata`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#trace-metadata
- [definition] Trace Cursor sessions — Trace [Cursor](https://cursor.com/) agent sessions in LangSmith using [Cursor hooks](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks). Each turn becomes one trace, grouped into a thread per Cursor conversation, which captures prompts, model responses, tool calls, token usage, and subagent activity. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#trace-cursor-sessions
- [definition] Prerequisites — Before setting up tracing, ensure you have: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#prerequisites
- [definition] Install and enable the plugin — Install the plugin directly from the GitHub repository in Cursor's settings: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#install-and-enable-the-plugin
- [definition] Alternative: install from a local clone — Install the hooks from a local clone of [`langsmith-cursor-plugins`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langsmith-cursor-plugins). This writes `~/.cursor/hooks.json` for all Cursor projects: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#alternative-install-from-a-local-clone
- [definition] Configure tracing — Tracing is disabled until both `enabled` (or `TRACE_TO_LANGSMITH=true`) and an API key are set. Configure credentials with [environment variables](#environment-variables), a [JSON config file](#config-file), or both. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#configure-tracing
- [definition] Environment variables — Every `LANGSMITH_CURSOR_*` variable also accepts the shorter `LANGSMITH_*` form. When both are set, `LANGSMITH_CURSOR_*` takes precedence. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#environment-variables
- [definition] Config file — Use `~/.cursor/langsmith.json` for global defaults or `./.cursor/langsmith.json` for project-level settings. Settings resolve in this order, with later sources overriding earlier ones: defaults, global config, project config, environment variables. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#config-file
- [definition] What gets traced — The plugin listens to Cursor hooks and assembles one trace per agent turn: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#what-gets-traced
- [definition] Trace metadata — Every run carries the shared `coding-agent-v1` metadata contract on `run.extra.metadata`, which lets traces from any coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) be identified and grouped with the same stable keys. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#trace-metadata
- [definition] View traces in LangSmith — Open the configured LangSmith project (default `cursor`) and complete a Cursor turn. The plugin uploads one trace per turn with this structure: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-cursor#view-traces-in-langsmith

- [definition] View traces in LangSmith — Open the configured LangSmith project and look for root runs named `opencode.session`. - [definition] How OTel tracing works — The following diagram shows the basic flow for OpenTelemetry tracing with LangSmith, including the fanout pattern where a single stream of spans is routed to multiple observability backends. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-opentelemetry#how-otel-tracing-works
- [definition] Trace a LangChain application — If you're using LangChain or LangGraph, use the built-in integration to trace your application: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-opentelemetry#trace-a-langchain-application
- [definition] Trace a non-LangChain application — For non-LangChain applications or custom instrumentation, you can trace your application in LangSmith with a standard OpenTelemetry client. - [definition] Send traces to an alternate provider — While LangSmith is the default destination for OpenTelemetry traces, you can also configure OpenTelemetry to send traces to other observability platforms. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-opentelemetry#send-traces-to-an-alternate-provider
- [definition] Use environment variables for global configuration — By default, the LangSmith OpenTelemetry exporter will send data to the LangSmith API OTEL endpoint, but this can be customized by setting standard OTEL environment variables: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-opentelemetry#use-environment-variables-for-global-configuration
- [definition] Add process-level resource attributes — You can attach custom metadata to every trace emitted by a process using the standard OpenTelemetry `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` environment variable. Unlike span-level attributes (set per-span in code), resource attributes are set once at the process level and automatically propagated to all spans. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-opentelemetry#add-process-level-resource-attributes
- [definition] Configure alternate OTLP endpoints — To send traces to a different provider, configure the OTLP exporter with your provider's endpoint: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-opentelemetry#configure-alternate-otlp-endpoints

- [definition] Trace using the LangSmith SDK — Use the LangSmith SDK's OpenTelemetry helper to configure export. The following example [traces a Google ADK agent](/langsmith/trace-with-google-adk): — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-opentelemetry#trace-using-the-langsmith-sdk
- [definition] Link OpenTelemetry spans to a LangSmith SDK trace — Native OTLP `parentSpanId` can't reference an existing LangSmith run: an OTLP span ID is 8 bytes, while LangSmith run IDs are full UUIDs. To attach an OpenTelemetry span to a run created elsewhere (for example, a LangChain-SDK run), set the `langsmith.*` attributes with the parent's full UUIDs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-opentelemetry#link-opentelemetry-spans-to-a-langsmith-sdk-trace
- [definition] Add an attachment to a trace — LangSmith supports [attaching files to traces](/langsmith/upload-files-with-traces). This is useful when building an agent with multimodal inputs or outputs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-opentelemetry#add-an-attachment-to-a-trace
- [definition] Use OpenTelemetry collector for fan-out — Use `LANGSMITH_OTEL_ENABLED=true` when you need OTEL fanout. Configure your application to emit OTEL spans once, then use an OpenTelemetry Collector to route them to LangSmith and any additional observability backends. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-opentelemetry#use-opentelemetry-collector-for-fan-out
- [definition] Distributed tracing with LangChain and OpenTelemetry — Distributed tracing is essential when your LLM application spans multiple services or processes. OpenTelemetry's context propagation capabilities ensure that traces remain connected across service boundaries. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-opentelemetry#distributed-tracing-with-langchain-and-opentelemetry

- [definition] Install — Install the integration along with the Pipecat service extras your pipeline uses: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-pipecat#install
- [definition] Set environment variables — The integration reads your LangSmith credentials from the environment and exports to LangSmith for you via OpenTelemetry: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-pipecat#set-environment-variables
- [definition] Set up tracing — Import `configure_pipecat` and call it once before building your pipeline. Enable tracing on the `PipelineTask`: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-pipecat#set-up-tracing
- [definition] Use a LangGraph or LangChain agent as the LLM — If your LLM stage is an in-process [LangGraph or LangChain](/oss/python/langgraph/overview) agent, its model and tool runs should nest inside Pipecat's `llm` span rather than forming a separate trace. To achieve this: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-pipecat#use-a-langgraph-or-langchain-agent-as-the-llm
- [definition] Use your own tracer provider — `configure_pipecat()` builds a `TracerProvider`, registers the LangSmith span processor, and wires it into Pipecat. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-pipecat#use-your-own-tracer-provider
- [definition] Group a conversation into a thread — To group a conversation's runs into a LangSmith [thread](/langsmith/threads) for thread-level views and token and cost aggregation, call `set_thread_id` once per conversation before its spans are emitted: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-pipecat#group-a-conversation-into-a-thread
- [definition] When using Pipecat with a realtime model — With a speech-to-speech (realtime) model there is no separate speech-to-text stage, so the user's transcript is never emitted as an OTel span. Instead it arrives through the user context aggregator's `on_user_turn_message_added` callback, which Pipecat fires once it has the finalized user text. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-pipecat#when-using-pipecat-with-a-realtime-model
- [definition] Record the conversation audio — Attach the conversation audio to the trace using Pipecat's [`AudioBufferProcessor`](https://docs.pipecat.ai/server/utilities/audio/audio-recording). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-pipecat#record-the-conversation-audio

- [parameter] `COPILOT_OTEL_ENDPOINT`: LangSmith OTLP endpoint. Takes precedence over `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-vscode-copilot#configure-tracing
- [parameter] `COPILOT_OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT`: Capture full prompts, responses, tool arguments, and tool results on spans. Off by default. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-vscode-copilot#configure-tracing
- [parameter] `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`: Authentication headers for the OTLP exporter. - [snippet] TypeScript: import { TRAJECTORY_ACCURACY_PROMPT_WITH_REFERENCE } from "agentevals"; — `import { TRAJECTORY_ACCURACY_PROMPT_WITH_REFERENCE } from "agentevals";` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#with-reference-trajectory

- [parameter] [`strict`](#strict-match): Description=Exact match of messages and tool calls in the same order; Use Case=Testing specific sequences (e.g., policy lookup before authorization) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#trajectory-match-evaluator
- [parameter] [`unordered`](#unordered-match): Description=Same tool calls allowed in any order; Use Case=Verifying information retrieval when order doesn't matter — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#trajectory-match-evaluator
- [parameter] [`subset`](#subset-and-superset-match): Description=Agent calls only tools from reference (no extras); Use Case=Ensuring agent doesn't exceed expected scope — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#trajectory-match-evaluator
- [parameter] [`superset`](#subset-and-superset-match): Description=Agent calls at least the reference tools (extras allowed); Use Case=Verifying minimum required actions are taken — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#trajectory-match-evaluator
- [definition] How to evaluate your agent with trajectory evaluations — Many agent behaviors only emerge when using a real LLM, such as which tool the agent decides to call, how it formats responses, or whether a prompt modification affects the entire execution trajectory. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#how-to-evaluate-your-agent-with-trajectory-evaluations
- [definition] Trajectory match evaluator — AgentEvals offers the `create_trajectory_match_evaluator` function in Python and `createTrajectoryMatchEvaluator` in TypeScript to match your agent's trajectory against a reference trajectory. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#trajectory-match-evaluator
- [definition] Strict match — The `strict` mode ensures trajectories contain identical messages in the same order with the same tool calls, though it allows for differences in message content. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#strict-match
- [definition] Unordered match — The `unordered` mode allows the same tool calls in any order, which is helpful when you want to verify that the correct set of tools are being invoked but don't care about the sequence. For example, an agent might need to check both weather and events for a city, but the order doesn't matter. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#unordered-match
- [definition] Subset and superset match — The `superset` and `subset` modes focus on which tools are called rather than the order of tool calls, allowing you to control how strictly the agent's tool calls must align with the reference. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#subset-and-superset-match
- [definition] LLM-as-judge evaluator — This section covers the trajectory-specific LLM-as-a-judge evaluator from the `agentevals` package. For general-purpose LLM-as-a-judge evaluators in LangSmith, refer to the [LLM-as-a-judge evaluator](/langsmith/llm-as-judge). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#llm-as-judge-evaluator
- [definition] With reference trajectory — If you have a reference trajectory, you can add an extra variable to your prompt and pass in the reference trajectory. Below, we use the prebuilt `TRAJECTORY_ACCURACY_PROMPT_WITH_REFERENCE` prompt and configure the `reference_outputs` variable: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#with-reference-trajectory
- [definition] Async support (Python) — All `agentevals` evaluators support Python asyncio. For evaluators that use factory functions, async versions are available by adding `async` after `create_` in the function name. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trajectory-evals#async-support-python

- [definition] Getting helpful information — To diagnose and resolve an issue, you will first need to retrieve some relevant information. The following sections explain how to do this for a Kubernetes or a Docker setup, and how to pull helpful browser information. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/troubleshooting#getting-helpful-information
- [definition] *DB::Exception: Cannot reserve 1.00 MiB, not enough space: While executing WaitForAsyncInsert. (NOT\_ENOUGH\_SPACE)* — This error occurs when ClickHouse runs out of disk space. You will need to increase the disk space available to ClickHouse. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/troubleshooting#dbexception-cannot-reserve-100-mib-not-enough-space-while-executing-waitforasyncinsert-not-enough-space
- [definition] *error: Dirty database version 'version'. fix and force version* — This error occurs when the ClickHouse database is in an inconsistent state with our migrations. - [definition] *413 - request entity too large* — This error occurs when the request size exceeds the maximum allowed size. You will need to increase the maximum request size in your Nginx configuration. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/troubleshooting#413-request-entity-too-large
- [definition] *Details: code: 497, message: default: Not enough privileges. to execute this query, it's necessary to have the grant CREATE ROW POLICY ON default.feedbacks\_rmt* — This error occurs when your user does not have the necessary permissions to create row policies in Clickhouse. - [definition] *ClickHouse fails to start up when running a cluster with AquaSec* — In some environments, AquaSec may prevent ClickHouse from starting up correctly. This may manifest as the ClickHouse pod not emitting any logs and failing to get marked as ready. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/troubleshooting#clickhouse-fails-to-start-up-when-running-a-cluster-with-aquasec

## Set up LangChain Tuned Evaluators
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators>

- [definition] Set up LangChain Tuned Evaluators — LangChain Tuned Evaluators are in **[beta](/langsmith/release-stages)**. Their interface and behavior may change before general availability. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators#set-up-langchain-tuned-evaluators
- [definition] Add an evaluator — Add a LangChain Tuned Evaluator to a compatible tracing project. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators#understand-how-langchain-tuned-evaluators-work
- [definition] Identify an eligible thread — LangSmith identifies a thread that meets the evaluator's requirements and the project's filters and sampling configuration. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators#understand-how-langchain-tuned-evaluators-work
- [definition] Evaluate the thread — The specialized LangChain-managed judge evaluates the eligible thread. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators#understand-how-langchain-tuned-evaluators-work
- [definition] Attach feedback — LangSmith attaches the result and its explanation to the thread as feedback. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators#understand-how-langchain-tuned-evaluators-work
- [definition] Enable LangChain Tuned Evaluators — Enabling LangChain Tuned Evaluators lets members attach them to tracing projects throughout the organization. Evaluation data is processed using LangChain-managed API keys. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators#enable-langchain-tuned-evaluators
- [definition] Add a LangChain Tuned Evaluator to a project — To add Perceived Error (Tuned) to a tracing project: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators#add-a-langchain-tuned-evaluator-to-a-project
- [definition] Disable LangChain Tuned Evaluators — To disable LangChain Tuned Evaluators for the organization: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators#disable-langchain-tuned-evaluators
- [definition] Review usage charges — Availability and pricing vary by LangChain Tuned Evaluator. LangSmith charges LCUs only for an evaluation run that attaches feedback. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators#review-usage-charges
- [definition] The project is empty — Add a thread to the tracing project, then try to save the evaluator again. The thread must contain supported message lists and at least one complete user-to-assistant exchange. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators#the-project-is-empty
- [definition] The project does not contain a valid message list — Check the inputs and outputs of the project's most recent threads. Their top-level `messages` fields must contain message lists in a [supported format](/langsmith/online-evaluations-multi-turn#prerequisites), and at least one user message must be followed by an assistant message. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators#the-project-does-not-contain-a-valid-message-list
- [definition] Enabling the feature does not take effect immediately — Organization settings can take a few seconds to propagate. If LangSmith reports that the managed-evaluator setting is still taking effect, wait a few seconds and try again. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/tuned-evaluators#enabling-the-feature-does-not-take-effect-immediately

- [parameter] Developer (no payment on file): Limit=5,000 traces; Window=1 month — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#plan-level-monthly-unique-traces-limit
- [definition] Data retention — This section covers how data retention works and how it's priced in LangSmith. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#data-retention
- [definition] How it works — LangSmith has two tiers of traces based on Data Retention with the following characteristics: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#how-it-works
- [definition] Data retention auto-upgrades — Auto upgrades can have an impact on your bill. Please read this section carefully to fully understand your estimated LangSmith tracing costs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#data-retention-auto-upgrades
- [definition] Rate limits — LangSmith has rate limits which are designed to ensure the stability of the service for all users. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#rate-limits
- [definition] Temporary throughput limit over a 1 minute period at our application load balancer — This 429 is the result of exceeding a fixed number of API calls over a 1 minute window on a per service key or PAT basis. The start of the window will vary slightly—it is not guaranteed to start at the start of a clock minute—and may change depending on application deployment events. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#temporary-throughput-limit-over-a-1-minute-period-at-our-application-load-balancer
- [definition] Plan-level hourly trace event limit — This 429 is the result of reaching your maximum hourly events ingested and is evaluated in a fixed window starting at the beginning of each clock hour in UTC and resets at the top of each new hour. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#plan-level-hourly-trace-event-limit
- [definition] Plan-level hourly trace data ingest limit — This 429 is the result of reaching the maximum amount of data ingested across your trace inputs, outputs, and metadata and is evaluated in a fixed window starting at the beginning of each clock hour in UTC and resets at the top of each new hour. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#plan-level-hourly-trace-data-ingest-limit
- [definition] Plan-level monthly unique traces limit — This 429 is the result of reaching your maximum monthly traces ingested and is evaluated in a fixed window starting at the beginning of each calendar month in UTC and resets at the beginning of each new month. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#plan-level-monthly-unique-traces-limit
- [definition] Self-configured monthly usage limits — This 429 is the result of reaching your usage limit as configured by your organization admin and is evaluated in a fixed window starting at the beginning of each calendar month in UTC and resets at the beginning of each new month. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#self-configured-monthly-usage-limits
- [definition] Maximum runs per trace — Each trace is limited to a maximum of 25,000 runs. Once the trace reaches this limit, LangSmith will reject any additional runs that you send for that trace. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#maximum-runs-per-trace
- [definition] Run query endpoint — The [`POST /runs/query`](/langsmith/smith-api/run/query-runs) endpoint has additional per-tenant rate limits based on query parameters. See [Query traces using the SDK](/langsmith/export-traces#rate-limits) for details. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#run-query-endpoint
- [definition] Workspace invite batch endpoint — Workspace invite batch requests are rate limited per workspace to reduce bulk invitation abuse. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#workspace-invite-batch-endpoint
- [definition] Handling 429s responses in your application — Since some 429 responses are temporary and may succeed on a successive call, if you are directly calling the LangSmith API in your application we recommend implementing retry logic with exponential backoff and jitter. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#handling-429s-responses-in-your-application
- [definition] Usage limits — LangSmith lets you configure usage limits on tracing. Note that these are *usage* limits, not *spend* limits, which mean they let you limit the quantity of occurrences of some event rather than the total amount you will spend. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#usage-limits
- [definition] Properties of usage limiting — Usage limiting is approximate, meaning that we do not guarantee the exactness of the limit. In rare cases, there may be a small period of time where additional traces are processed above the limit threshold before usage limiting begins to apply. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#properties-of-usage-limiting
- [definition] Side effects of extended data retention traces limit — The extended data retention traces limit has side effects. If the limit is already reached, LangSmith blocks actions that would create another extended-retention trace. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#side-effects-of-extended-data-retention-traces-limit
- [definition] Updating usage limits — Usage limits can be updated from the `Settings` page under `Usage and Billing`. Limit values are cached, so it may take a minute or two before the new limits apply. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing#updating-usage-limits
