- [parameter] `graph_id`: The graph (deployment) the thread belongs to. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#filter-by-metadata
- [parameter] `assistant_id`: The [assistant](/langsmith/assistants) used to create runs on the thread. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#filter-by-metadata
- [parameter] `langgraph_auth_user_id`: The authenticated user who owns the thread (set automatically when using [custom auth](/langsmith/custom-auth)). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#filter-by-metadata
- [parameter] `cron_id`: The [cron job](/langsmith/cron-jobs) that created runs on the thread. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#filter-by-metadata
- [definition] Use threads — This guide shows you how to create, view, and inspect _threads_. Threads work with [assistants](/langsmith/assistants) to enable [stateful](/oss/python/langgraph/persistence) execution of your [deployed graphs](/langsmith/deployment). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#use-threads
- [definition] Understand threads — A thread is a persistent conversation container that maintains state across multiple runs. Each time you execute a run on a thread, the graph processes the input with the thread's current state and updates that state with new information. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#understand-threads
- [definition] Create a thread — To run your graph with state persistence, you must first create a thread: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#create-a-thread
- [definition] Copy thread — Alternatively, if you already have a thread in your application whose state you wish to copy, you can use the `copy` method. This will create an independent thread whose history is identical to the original thread at the time of the operation: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#copy-thread
- [definition] Prepopulated state — You can create a thread with an arbitrary pre-defined state by providing a list of `supersteps` into the `create` method. The `supersteps` describe a sequence of state updates that establish the initial state of the thread. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#prepopulated-state
- [definition] Filter by thread status — Use the `status` field to filter threads based on their status. Supported values are `idle`, `busy`, `interrupted`, and `error`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#filter-by-thread-status
- [definition] Filter by metadata — The `search` method allows you to filter on metadata. This is useful for finding threads associated with specific graphs, users, or custom metadata you've added to threads. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#filter-by-metadata
- [definition] Sorting — The SDK also supports sorting threads by `thread_id`, `status`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` using the `sort_by` and `sort_order` parameters. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#sorting
- [definition] Get thread — To view a specific thread given its `thread_id`, use the [`get`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langgraph-sdk/_async/threads/ThreadsClient#member-get-0) method: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#get-thread
- [definition] Inspect thread state — To view the current state of a given thread, use the [`get_state`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langgraph-sdk/_async/threads/ThreadsClient/get_state) method. This returns the current values, next nodes to execute, and checkpoint information: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#inspect-thread-state
- [definition] Inspect full thread history — To view a thread's history, use the [`get_history`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langgraph-sdk/_async/threads/ThreadsClient/get_history) method. This returns a list of every state the thread experienced, allowing you to trace the full execution path: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-threads#inspect-full-thread-history

## Use tools in a prompt
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-tools>

- [definition] Use tools in a prompt — Tools allow language models to interact with external systems and perform actions beyond just generating text. In the Playground, you can use two types of tools: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-tools#use-tools-in-a-prompt
- [definition] Built-in tools — The Playground has native support for a variety of tools from OpenAI and Anthropic. If you want to use a tool that isn't explicitly listed in the Playground, you can still add it by manually specifying its `type` and any required arguments. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-tools#built-in-tools
- [definition] Add and use tools — The Playground lets you quickly [add tools](#add-a-tool) to any prompt with a single click. You can choose from built-in tools provided by model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic, or define your own [custom tools](#create-a-custom-tool) tailored to your specific needs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-tools#add-and-use-tools
- [definition] Add a tool — To add a tool to your prompt, click the **+ Tool** button at the bottom of the prompt editor. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-tools#add-a-tool
- [definition] Use a built-in tool — 1. In the tool section, select the built-in tool you want to use. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-tools#use-a-built-in-tool
- [definition] Create a custom tool — To create a custom tool, you'll need to provide: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-tools#create-a-custom-tool
- [definition] Manage tools with the registry — The Playground includes a [workspace](/langsmith/administration-overview#workspaces)-scoped **tool registry** that persists both custom and built-in tools across prompts and sessions. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-tools#manage-tools-with-the-registry
- [definition] Tool choice settings — Some models provide control over which tools are called. To configure this: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-tools#tool-choice-settings

- [parameter] `values`: Type=`JSON object`; Description=The state values from the latest checkpoint of the thread. Only present for stateful runs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#webhook-payload
- [parameter] `multitask_strategy`: Type=`string`; Description=The multitask strategy used for the run. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#webhook-payload
- [parameter] `error`: Type=`JSON object \| null`; Description=Present only if the run failed. Contains `error` (error type) and `message` (detail) fields. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#webhook-payload
- [parameter] `allowed_domains`: Hostname allowlist. Supports wildcards for subdomains (e.g., `*.mycompany.com`). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#restrict-webhook-destinations
- [parameter] `require_https`: Reject `http://` URLs when `true`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#restrict-webhook-destinations
- [parameter] `allowed_ports`: Explicit port allowlist. Defaults to 443 (https) and 80 (http). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#restrict-webhook-destinations
- [parameter] `disable_loopback`: Disallow relative URLs (internal loopback calls) when `true`. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#restrict-webhook-destinations
- [parameter] `max_url_length`: Maximum permitted URL length in characters. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#restrict-webhook-destinations
- [definition] Use webhooks — Webhooks enable event-driven communication from your LangSmith application to external services. For example, you may want to issue an update to a separate service once an API call to LangSmith has finished running. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#use-webhooks
- [definition] Supported endpoints — The following API endpoints accept a `webhook` parameter: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#supported-endpoints
- [definition] Set up your assistant and thread — Before making API calls, set up your assistant and thread. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#set-up-your-assistant-and-thread
- [definition] Use a webhook with a graph run — To use a webhook, specify the `webhook` parameter in your API request. When the run completes, LangSmith sends a `POST` request to the specified webhook URL. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#use-a-webhook-with-a-graph-run
- [definition] Webhook payload — LangSmith sends webhook notifications in the format of a [Run](/langsmith/runs). The request payload includes run input, configuration, and other metadata in the `kwargs` field. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#webhook-payload
- [definition] Secure webhooks — To ensure only authorized requests hit your webhook endpoint, consider adding a security token as a query parameter: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#secure-webhooks

- [definition] Disable webhooks — As of `langgraph-api>=0.2.78`, developers can disable webhooks in the `langgraph.json` file: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#disable-webhooks
- [definition] Test webhooks — You can test your webhook using online services like: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-webhooks#test-webhooks

- [parameter] **Custom separator**: SSO Groups Sync=Reuses org-level [`scim_group_name_separator`](#configure-custom-separator); SCIM=[`scim_group_name_separator`](#configure-custom-separator) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/user-management#when-to-use-sso-groups-sync-vs-scim
- [parameter] **Enable SSO Groups Sync**: Automatically assign workspace roles based on group memberships in the SSO token. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/user-management#configuration

- [parameter] **Require matching group to sign in**: Block login if the SSO token contains no groups matching the naming convention. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/user-management#configuration

## View traces
<https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces>

- [snippet] Customize the Messages view: @traceable(metadata={"ls_agent_type": "root"}) — `@traceable(metadata={"ls_agent_type": "root"})` — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#customize-the-messages-view
- [parameter] `"root"`: Messages from this run appear in the main Messages view. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#customize-the-messages-view
- [parameter] `"subagent"`: Messages from this run appear as a subagent action in the conversation thread. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#customize-the-messages-view
- [definition] View traces — From a tracing project, use the **Threads**, **Traces**, or **Runs** tabs to change what appears in the table. Click into any row to open the side panel. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#view-traces
- [definition] Start in the Messages view — Open a thread and switch to the Messages view to see the trajectory. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#view-traces
- [definition] Investigate — Scan the trajectory to identify unexpected behavior, for example, a bad tool result, an unexpected subagent handoff, a latency spike. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#view-traces
- [definition] Inspect the run — Click the relevant message or tool call to open the Details view at the exact run that produced it. Review its inputs, outputs, timing, errors, and metadata. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#view-traces
- [definition] Return to the trajectory — Toggle back to the Messages view to continue scanning the conversation. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#view-traces
- [definition] What the Messages view shows — Each turn in the trajectory renders as a single block containing the model's response, the tool calls it triggered, and the results those tools returned. You can scan the full trajectory and read the agent's behavior without opening a child run. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#what-the-messages-view-shows
- [definition] Customize the Messages view — You can control how runs appear in the Messages view using metadata keys on individual runs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#customize-the-messages-view
- [definition] Turns view — Use the Turns view to scan the structure of a thread one turn at a time, without the full conversation rendering of the Messages view. Each turn in the thread appears as a card showing the root run's inputs and outputs. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#turns-view
- [definition] Customize the Turns view — By default, LangSmith picks input and output fields to show on each turn card using heuristics. To override which fields appear, click the **Format** button at the top of the thread to open the format pane, select the specific input and output paths you want to display, and save. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#customize-the-turns-view
- [definition] Details view — The Details view is the debugging layer. When you click into a specific run, the surrounding thread context remains available so you can understand where that run fits in the broader conversation. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#details-view
- [definition] Customize the Details view — Setting `run_type="llm"` on a run causes the Details view to render token counts and latency for that run. For the full message format specification, refer to [Log an LLM trace](/langsmith/log-llm-trace). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-traces#customize-the-details-view

- [parameter] **LangSmith Deployment Nodes Executed**: Individual LangGraph node executions across deployed agents. Each step in a deployed agent's graph counts as one node execution. Tracked separately for Cloud-hosted and Self-hosted deployments. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-usage#billable-metrics

- [parameter] Invoices and payment management: Not available (billing is handled outside LangSmith) — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-usage#self-hosted-limitations
- [definition] View usage — LangSmith provides several views into your [organization's](/langsmith/administration-overview) usage, depending on your [plan](/langsmith/pricing-plans) and [hosting type](/langsmith/platform-setup). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-usage#view-usage
- [definition] Usage graph — The usage graph shows aggregate trace consumption for your [organization](/langsmith/administration-overview#organizations), broken down by [workspace](/langsmith/administration-overview#workspaces). It covers the current billing period and does not show spend—for spend, refer to the invoice. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-usage#usage-graph
- [definition] Contract usage — Enterprise customers with prepaid commitments can view how much of their contract has been consumed. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-usage#contract-usage
- [definition] Invoices — Invoices are available on **self-serve Cloud plans only**. Enterprise Cloud organizations have a separate usage view for tracking spend. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-usage#invoices
- [definition] Granular usage — Granular usage gives you trace counts broken down by a dimension you choose (workspace, project, user, or API key) over a time range you select. This is useful for internal chargebacks, identifying high-usage teams, or auditing trace activity. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-usage#granular-usage
- [definition] What "traces" means here — The granular usage view counts **traces**: root-level runs and all their child spans counted as a single unit. This is the same unit used for [billing](/langsmith/billing). — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-usage#what-traces-means-here
- [definition] When usage is recorded — Granular usage records traces by **insertion time** (when the trace was received and stored by LangSmith), not by when it ran in your application. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-usage#when-usage-is-recorded
- [definition] Self-hosted limitations — [Self-hosted](/langsmith/self-hosted) LangSmith have a different set of usage views available compared to [Cloud](/langsmith/cloud), due to differences in billing infrastructure. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-usage#self-hosted-limitations
- [definition] Granular usage on self-hosted — Granular usage is available on [Self-hosted](/langsmith/self-hosted) but requires explicit opt-in: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-usage#granular-usage-on-self-hosted
- [definition] Aggregate usage on Self-hosted — The usage graph is available on [Self-hosted](/langsmith/self-hosted) running Helm chart 0.9.5 or later. LangSmith automatically generates and syncs organization usage charts, available under **Settings** → **Usage and billing** → **Usage graph**: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/view-usage#aggregate-usage-on-self-hosted

- [definition] Setup — Set up the integrations as follows. Note that while you can add LangSmith evals alongside your other unit tests (as standard `*.test.ts` files) using your existing test config files, the below examples will also set up a separate test config file and command to run your evals. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/vitest-jest#setup
- [definition] Vitest — Install the required development dependencies if you have not already: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/vitest-jest#vitest
- [definition] Jest — Install the required development dependencies if you have not already: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/vitest-jest#jest

- [definition] Log outputs — Every time we run a test we're syncing it to a dataset example and tracing it as a run. - [definition] Trace intermediate calls — LangSmith will automatically trace any traceable intermediate calls that happen in the course of test case execution. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/vitest-jest#trace-intermediate-calls

- [definition] Configuring test suites — You can configure test suites with values like metadata or a custom client by passing an extra argument to `ls.describe()` for the full suite or by passing a `config` field into `ls.test()` for individual tests: — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/vitest-jest#configuring-test-suites
- [definition] Dry-run mode — If you want to run the tests without syncing the results to LangSmith, you can set omit your LangSmith tracing environment variables or set `LANGSMITH_TEST_TRACKING=false` in your environment. — https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/vitest-jest#dry-run-mode

<https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes>

- [snippet] Launch with YOLO: [startup] — `[startup]` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#enable-yolo
- [snippet] Auto decision flow: flowchart TD — `flowchart TD` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#how-auto-works
- [snippet] Select a classifier model: /auto model openai:gpt-5.6-luna — `/auto model openai:gpt-5.6-luna` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#select-a-classifier-model
- [snippet] Select a classifier model: dcode -y --auto-classifier-model openai:gpt-5.6-luna — `dcode -y --auto-classifier-model openai:gpt-5.6-luna` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#select-a-classifier-model
- [snippet] Select a classifier model: export DEEPAGENTS_CODE_AUTO_CLASSIFIER_MODEL="openai:gpt-5.6-luna" — `export DEEPAGENTS_CODE_AUTO_CLASSIFIER_MODEL="openai:gpt-5.6-luna"` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#select-a-classifier-model
- [snippet] title="~/.deepagents/config.toml": [models] — `[models]` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#select-a-classifier-model
- [parameter] **Manual** (default): Asks for approval before every gated action — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#choose-a-mode
- [parameter] **Auto**: Approves routine actions automatically; asks the model to review anything uncertain; falls back to you after repeated denials or failures — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#choose-a-mode
- [parameter] **YOLO**: Runs gated actions with no review at all — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#choose-a-mode
- [definition] Approval modes — By default, Deep Agents Code asks for your approval before running potentially consequential actions. These are called **gated actions** and include things like: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#approval-modes
- [definition] Enable Auto — Auto is eligible only in interactive, unsandboxed sessions. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#enable-auto
- [definition] Enable YOLO — YOLO runs gated actions without any review. Use it only when you accept that the agent can take any action without asking. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#enable-yolo
- [definition] How Auto works — Auto keeps the same gated-action rules as Manual but changes how those actions are reviewed. It uses two stages: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#how-auto-works
- [definition] Select a classifier model — By default, the Auto classifier uses the same model as the main agent. You can point it at a different (typically cheaper and faster) model to reduce cost and latency during Auto review. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#select-a-classifier-model
- [definition] Revalidate before side effects — The decision plan is bound to the thread, mode, batch, and exact gated calls. Missing or invalid state, a mode race, or a replay falls back to human review. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#revalidate-before-side-effects
- [definition] Where Auto and YOLO are available — Auto and YOLO are interactive-mode features. Auto is eligible only in an interactive, unsandboxed session; a remote `--sandbox` forces it to Manual. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#where-auto-and-yolo-are-available
- [definition] Remember the last mode across sessions — When no flag or configured mode applies, Deep Agents Code restores the last selected Manual or Auto mode. YOLO must be explicitly selected. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#remember-the-last-mode-across-sessions

- [parameter] `--rubric TEXT\|@PATH`: Acceptance criteria for rubric grading. Accepts literal text or `@path` to read a file. Requires `-n` or piped stdin — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--rubric-model MODEL`: Model the rubric grader uses. Defaults to the main agent model. Requires `-n` or piped stdin — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--rubric-max-iterations N`: Grader iterations per rubric attempt before stopping. Requires `-n` or piped stdin — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `-n`, `--non-interactive TEXT`: Run a single task non-interactively and exit. Shell is disabled unless `--shell-allow-list` is set — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--recursion-limit N`: Set the LangGraph graph step budget (maximum node invocations per turn). When unset, the LangGraph server default applies — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--max-turns N`: Cap agentic turns in non-interactive mode. Exits with code 124 when exceeded. Requires `-n` or piped stdin. See [Non-interactive mode and piping](#non-interactive-mode-and-piping) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options

- [parameter] `-q`, `--quiet`: Clean output for piping—only the agent's response goes to stdout. Requires `-n` or piped stdin — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--no-stream`: Buffer the full response and write to stdout at once instead of streaming. Requires `-n` or piped stdin — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--show-reasoning`: Show provider-visible reasoning in the interactive transcript or on stderr in non-interactive mode. Off by default — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--stdin`: Read input from stdin explicitly instead of auto-detection. Errors clearly when stdin is unavailable or is a TTY — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `-y`, `--auto-approve`: Enable classifier-backed [Auto](/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes) mode. Requires an interactive local session; toggle with `Shift+Tab` during an interactive session — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--auto-classifier-model MODEL`: Model used by the [Auto classifier](/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes#select-a-classifier-model) to review gated tool calls (`provider:model` format). Overrides `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_AUTO_CLASSIFIER_MODEL` and `[models].auto_classifier` in `config.toml`. Interactive TUI sessions only — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--yolo`: Run gated actions without review after the one-time local risk acknowledgement. Interactive mode only — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `-S`, `--shell-allow-list LIST`: Comma-separated shell commands to auto-approve, `'recommended'` for safe defaults, or `'all'` to allow any command. Applies to both `-n` and interactive modes — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--allow-fs-tools LIST`: Filesystem tools to expose. Defaults to `all`. See [Restrict filesystem tools](#restrict-filesystem-tools) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--json`: Emit machine-readable JSON from supported management subcommands, including `tools`, `agents`, `threads`, `skills`, and `update`. Output envelope: `{"schema_version": 1, "command": "...", "data": ...}` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--sandbox TYPE`: Remote sandbox for code execution: `none` (default), `langsmith`, `agentcore`, `daytona`, `modal`, `runloop`, `vercel`, and third-party providers. LangSmith is included; other built-ins require extras. Pass `--sandbox` with no value to use `[sandboxes].default` from config — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--sandbox-id ID`: Reuse an existing sandbox (skips creation and cleanup) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--sandbox-snapshot-name NAME`: Sandbox snapshot name to use or create (`langsmith`, `runloop`, and providers that advertise snapshot support) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--sandbox-setup PATH`: Path to setup script to run in sandbox after creation — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--mcp-config PATH`: Add an explicit MCP config as the highest-precedence source (merged with auto-discovered configs) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--no-mcp`: Disable all MCP tool loading — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--trust-project-mcp`: Trust project-level MCP servers without prompting for the current run. Explicit denies still apply. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `-e`, `--extension PATH`: Load a Python extension file or directory for this run. Repeat to add multiple paths. Requires `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL=1` and extension discovery enabled (`[extensions].enabled` / `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_EXTENSIONS`). See [Python extensions](/oss/deepagents/code/extensions) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--trust-project-extensions`: Trust project-level `.deepagents/extensions/` Python extensions for this run. Requires `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL=1`. See [Python extensions](/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#trust-project-extensions) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--interpreter`: Enable the JS interpreter (`js_eval`) middleware on the main agent when it has been disabled in config. `js_eval` is enabled by default. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--interpreter-tools VALUE`: PTC allowlist for `js_eval`: `safe`, `all`, or a comma-separated list of tool names. Default: `safe` (read-only `read_file`/`glob`/`grep` preset). See [JS interpreter](/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#js-interpreter) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--profile-override JSON`: Override model profile fields as a JSON string (e.g., `'{"max_input_tokens": 4096}'`). Merged on top of config file profile overrides — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--acp`: Run as an ACP server over stdio instead of launching the interactive UI — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--update`: Check for and install updates, then exit — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--auto-update`: Toggle automatic updates on or off, then exit — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--install NAME`: Install an optional extra (e.g., `quickjs`, `daytona`, `fireworks`), then exit. Add `--package` to treat `NAME` as a custom provider package installed via `uv --with` rather than an extra (see [arbitrary providers](/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#arbitrary-providers)), and `--yes` to skip confirmation prompts — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `--uninstall NAME`: Remove an installed optional extra and exit. Alias for `dcode uninstall NAME` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `-v`, `--version`: Display version — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `-h`, `--help`: Show help — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-line-options
- [parameter] `dcode help`: Show help — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode tools list [--json]`: List the tools available to the configured agent. Place top-level tool-shaping flags, such as `--allow-fs-tools`, `--no-mcp`, `--mcp-config`, and `--trust-project-mcp`, before `tools list` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode agents list`: List all agents (alias: `ls`) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode agents reset --agent NAME`: Clear agent memory and reset to default. Supports `--dry-run` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode agents reset --agent NAME --target SOURCE`: Copy memory from another agent — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode uninstall NAME`: Remove one installed optional extra while preserving the rest of the tool environment — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode update`: Check for and install Deep Agents Code updates — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode doctor`: Run diagnostics without launching a session. See [Run diagnostics](#run-diagnostics-dcode-doctor) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode skills list [--project]`: List all skills (alias: `ls`) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode skills create NAME [--project]`: Create a new skill with template `SKILL.md`. Idempotent—re-creating an existing skill prints an informational message instead of an error — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode skills info NAME [--project]`: Show detailed information about a skill — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode skills delete NAME [--project] [-f]`: Delete a skill and its contents. Supports `--dry-run` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode threads list [--agent NAME] [--limit N]`: List sessions (alias: `ls`). Default limit: 20. `-n` is a short flag for `--limit`. Additional flags: `--sort {created,updated}`, `--branch TEXT` (filter by git branch), `--cwd [PATH]` (filter by working directory; bare flag uses current directory), `-v`/`--verbose` (show all columns including branch, created time, and initial prompt)… — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode threads delete ID`: Delete a session. Supports `--dry-run` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode mcp login [NAME] [--mcp-config PATH]`: With `NAME`, run the OAuth login flow for a server marked `auth: "oauth"`. Omit `NAME` to list configured OAuth servers that need login. See [MCP tools](/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#oauth-login) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode mcp config`: Show MCP config discovery paths — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode config show`: Show every config option's effective value and the source it resolves from. See [Inspect configuration](#inspect-configuration-dcode-config) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode config list`: List all available config options with their type, default, and where each can be set (alias: `ls`) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode config get KEY`: Show the effective value and source for one option (e.g. `interpreter.memory_limit_mb`) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode config path`: Show config file locations and whether each exists — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode auth list`: List known providers and where each credential resolves from — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode auth status <provider>`: Show the credential source for one provider — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode auth set <provider>`: Store a provider credential from stdin or `--from-env` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode auth remove <provider>`: Remove a stored provider credential — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [parameter] `dcode auth path`: Show the credential store path — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#cli-commands
- [definition] Command reference — Deep Agents Code (`dcode`) accepts command-line flags at launch and exposes management subcommands for tools, agents, sessions, skills, credentials, and configuration. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#command-reference
- [definition] Choose a model — Launch with `--model` (`-M`) to pin a model for one session. Use the `provider:model` format (for example, `openai:gpt-5.5`) or pass a bare model name when the provider is unambiguous: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#choose-a-model
- [definition] Set or clear a default model — Persist a default model for all future launches: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#set-or-clear-a-default-model
- [definition] Choose a summarization model — Use a separate model for automatic context compaction, `/offload`, and `/compact` without changing the main agent model: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#choose-a-summarization-model
- [definition] Model parameters and profile overrides — Pass extra constructor kwargs to the model with `--model-params` as a JSON string. These apply for the current session only and override `config.toml` provider params: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#model-parameters-and-profile-overrides
- [definition] Install provider extras — Optional provider and sandbox packages ship as extras. Install from the shell without launching a session: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#install-provider-extras
- [definition] Remove an optional extra — Remove one installed extra while preserving the rest of the Deep Agents Code installation: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#remove-an-optional-extra
- [definition] Agents and sessions — Use `-a`/`--agent` to launch with a named agent that has its own memory, skills, and `AGENTS.md` under `~/.deepagents/<agent_name>/`. The flag overrides both `[agents].default` and `[agents].recent` in `config.toml`: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#agents-and-sessions
- [definition] Non-interactive mode and piping — Use `-n`/`--non-interactive` to run a single task without the interactive UI. Each non-interactive run starts a fresh thread; file-based state (memory, skills, configuration) persists across invocations: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#non-interactive-mode-and-piping
- [definition] Output, limits, and shell access — Use `-q`/`--quiet` to emit only the agent's response on stdout (for piping into other commands). Add `--no-stream` to buffer the full response before writing: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#output-limits-and-shell-access
- [definition] Skills at launch — The `--skill` flag invokes a skill immediately on launch in interactive or non-interactive mode: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#skills-at-launch
- [definition] Rubrics in scripts — Non-interactive runs cannot pause for interactive goal review. Pass acceptance criteria with `--rubric` when criteria are already known: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#rubrics-in-scripts
- [definition] Human-in-the-loop and shell access — Potentially destructive tool calls require approval by default. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#human-in-the-loop-and-shell-access
- [definition] Restrict filesystem tools — By default, Deep Agents Code exposes all filesystem tools. To expose only a subset, pass a comma-separated list: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#restrict-filesystem-tools
- [definition] Diagnose and audit a session — dcode exposes read-only slash commands for inspecting what a session loads and spends: `/tools` lists the active tool set, `/extensions` lists loaded Python extension registrations, `/context-doctor` audits the context injected before the conversation starts, and `/cost` reports the thread's… — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#diagnose-and-audit-a-session
- [definition] List loaded Python extensions — Run `/extensions` in a session to list each extension registration with its kind, name, scope, and source path. The report also shows load failures and whether graph-bound changes require `/restart`. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#list-loaded-python-extensions
- [definition] List available tools — Run `/tools` in a session to list the tools the current agent can call, grouped into built-in tools and tools from each MCP server: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#list-available-tools
- [definition] Audit injected context — Run `/context-doctor` in a session to audit what the session injects into every model request and its estimated token cost. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#audit-injected-context
- [definition] Track thread cost — Run `/cost` in a session to show the thread's estimated cost in USD: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#track-thread-cost
- [definition] Startup commands and initial prompts — Use `-m`/`--message` to auto-submit an initial prompt when an interactive session starts. Combine with `--startup-cmd` to run a shell command first: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#startup-commands-and-initial-prompts
- [definition] Remote sandboxes — Route code execution to a remote sandbox with `--sandbox`. Built-in providers include `langsmith`, `agentcore`, `daytona`, `modal`, `runloop`, and `vercel`. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#remote-sandboxes
- [definition] Manage credentials (`dcode auth`) — The `dcode auth` command group is the scriptable equivalent of the `/auth` credential manager. It reads and writes the same `auth.json` store without launching the TUI: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#manage-credentials-dcode-auth
- [definition] Inspect configuration (`dcode config`) — The `dcode config` command group reports effective configuration without starting a session. Use it to confirm that an environment variable or `config.toml` setting is picked up, or to share a redacted snapshot in a bug report: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#inspect-configuration-dcode-config
- [definition] Run diagnostics (`dcode doctor`) — Use `dcode doctor` when Deep Agents Code is not starting correctly, a provider or MCP server does not connect, tracing is misconfigured, or an install or update looks wrong. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/cli-reference#run-diagnostics-dcode-doctor

- [definition] Session cost warning — Deep Agents Code warns once per thread when its cumulative estimated cost exceeds $50 and suggests using `/offload` or `/clear`. You can configure the threshold in USD, or set it to `0` or a negative value to disable the warning: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#session-cost-warning
- [definition] Cold prompt-cache warning — Some LLM providers automatically cache the conversation prefix between turns, so a follow-up sent while the cache is warm re-processes only new tokens. That cache expires after a provider-specific idle window. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#cold-prompt-cache-warning
- [definition] Trust a gateway endpoint for cache policies — If requests reach the provider through a gateway or proxy instead of the official API, the cold-cache warning stays silent. Declaring an endpoint trusted asserts that it forwards cache settings untouched and honors the provider's documented retention: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#trust-a-gateway-endpoint-for-cache-policies
- [definition] Show provider-visible reasoning — Provider-visible reasoning is hidden by default. To show it in the interactive transcript and non-interactive output, set: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#show-provider-visible-reasoning
- [definition] Diff line numbers — Deep Agents Code shows file-relative line numbers in transcript and approval diffs by default. To hide them, set: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#diff-line-numbers
- [definition] Allowed models — Restrict `dcode` to an approved set of models with the `[models].allowed` list: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#allowed-models
- [definition] Redact LangSmith trace secrets — With LangSmith tracing enabled, Deep Agents Code redacts detected secrets from agent-trace inputs and outputs before upload. This is enabled by default. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#redact-langsmith-trace-secrets
- [definition] Provider configuration — Each provider is a TOML table under `[models.providers]`: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#provider-configuration
- [definition] Model constructor params — The [`params` field](#provider-configuration) forwards extra arguments to the model constructor. To give one model different values, add a model-keyed sub-table so you do not have to duplicate the whole provider config: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#model-constructor-params
- [definition] Retries — Deep Agents Code retries transient model errors at the model node. The default is five retries after the first request. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#retries
- [definition] Startup approval mode — Set the default [approval mode](/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes) for interactive sessions with the top-level `[startup].mode` key: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#startup-approval-mode
- [definition] Auto classifier timeout — When [Auto mode](/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes) is active, the classifier has a time budget to review each batch of gated actions. Batches not reviewed within the deadline are denied as `classifier_unavailable`; repeated misses fall back to the manual approval UI. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#auto-classifier-timeout
- [definition] Profile overrides (Advanced) — Override fields in the model's runtime profile to change how Deep Agents Code interprets model capabilities. See [`ModelProfile`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-core/language_models/model_profile/ModelProfile) for the full list of overridable fields. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#profile-overrides-advanced
- [definition] Adding models to the interactive switcher — Some providers (e.g. `langchain-ollama`) do not bundle model profile data (see [Provider reference](/oss/deepagents/code/providers#provider-reference) for full listing). — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#adding-models-to-the-interactive-switcher
- [definition] Custom base URL — Some provider packages accept a `base_url` to override the default endpoint. For example, `langchain-ollama` defaults to `http://localhost:11434` via the underlying `ollama` client. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#custom-base-url
- [definition] Compatible APIs — For providers that expose APIs that are wire-compatible with OpenAI or Anthropic, you can use the existing `langchain-openai` or `langchain-anthropic` packages by pointing `base_url` at the provider's endpoint: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#compatible-apis
- [definition] Arbitrary providers — Deep Agents Code works with any tool calling LLM available as a [LangChain `BaseChatModel`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain_core/language_models/#langchain_core.language_models.BaseChatModel). — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#arbitrary-providers
- [definition] Endpoints, keys, and gateways — An API key and the endpoint it is sent to have to match: the endpoint has to accept that key, or the request will likely fail. Deep Agents Code resolves the key and endpoint together, so overriding one updates the other to match. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#endpoints-keys-and-gateways
- [definition] How `base_url` resolves — Deep Agents Code resolves a provider's endpoint in this order (first match wins): — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#how-base-url-resolves
- [definition] Overrides keep the pair together — When you store a key with `/auth`, the endpoint you enter (or the provider's default, if left blank) is applied together with the key. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#overrides-keep-the-pair-together
- [definition] Managed gateways — On a machine provisioned with a model gateway (for example, the LangSmith gateway), the gateway typically exports a gateway key and the matching endpoint variable (`OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, or `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`) together. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#managed-gateways
- [definition] JS interpreter — The `[interpreter]` section tunes the built-in JavaScript interpreter (the `js_eval` tool), which runs agent-written code in a QuickJS sandbox. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#js-interpreter
- [definition] Python extensions — The `[extensions]` section controls [Python extension](/oss/deepagents/code/extensions) discovery and project trust. The experimental feature gate is required even when extension loading is enabled here. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#python-extensions
- [definition] Agent runtime limits — The LangGraph graph step budget is the maximum number of node invocations the `dcode` agent graph may execute in a single turn. Configure this recursion limit with the `[runtime]` section: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#agent-runtime-limits

- [definition] Configuration — Deep Agents Code stores user configuration in its profile directory, which defaults to `~/.deepagents/`, and in project-level dotfiles. Administrators can enforce settings from a fixed system path with [`managed_config.toml`](#managed-configuration). — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#configuration
- [definition] How settings resolve — Deep Agents Code uses tiered configuration. The precedence order depends on the setting type. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#how-settings-resolve
- [definition] Inspect configuration — The `dcode config` commands show the settings Deep Agents Code uses and where each value comes from, without starting a session. Use them to confirm that an administrator setting, environment variable, or `config.toml` setting is active. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#inspect-configuration
- [definition] Environment variables — In addition to shell exports, Deep Agents Code reads environment variables from dotenv files, so you can keep API keys out of your shell profile and avoid duplicating `.env` files across projects. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#environment-variables
- [definition] Loading order and precedence — At startup, Deep Agents Code reads the nearest project `.env`, found by searching the directory you launch from and walking up through its parents (the first `.env` found wins), then `~/.deepagents/.env` as a global fallback for all projects. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#loading-order-and-precedence
- [definition] `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_` prefix — All Deep Agents Code-specific environment variables use a `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_` prefix (e.g., `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_AUTO_UPDATE`, `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_DEBUG`). See the [environment variable reference](#environment-variable-reference) for the full list. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#deepagents-code-prefix
- [definition] Skill directory allowlist — By default, when Deep Agents Code loads skills it validates that a resolved skill file path stays inside one of the standard [skill directories](/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#skills). This prevents symlinks inside skill directories from reading arbitrary files outside those roots. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#skill-directory-allowlist
- [definition] Profile location (`DEEPAGENTS_HOME`) — `DEEPAGENTS_HOME` selects the directory Deep Agents Code uses as its user profile — everything normally stored under `~/.deepagents/` moves under the configured path. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#profile-location-deepagents-home
- [definition] Themes — Use `/theme` to open an interactive theme selector. Navigate the list to preview themes in real-time, press `Enter` to persist your choice to `config.toml`. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#themes
- [definition] Auto-update — Deep Agents Code automatically checks for and installs updates by default. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#auto-update
- [definition] Pricing catalog auto-update — Deep Agents Code refreshes its model pricing catalog from upstream hourly in the background so cost estimates stay current. To opt out: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#pricing-catalog-auto-update
- [definition] Custom pricing overrides — For models that the catalog does not cover, add rates to `~/.deepagents/prices.json`. The file uses the [genai-prices](https://github.com/pydantic/genai-prices) provider-array schema. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#custom-pricing-overrides
- [definition] Display options — These `[ui]` keys tune what the terminal UI shows. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#display-options
- [definition] Session usage stats — Deep Agents Code shows session usage statistics when a session ends (default on): — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#session-usage-stats
- [definition] Collapse large pastes — Large pastes into the chat input are collapsed into compact placeholders (default on). To keep the full pasted text visible: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#collapse-large-pastes
- [definition] Automatic memory — Deep Agents Code automatically saves learnings to memory. To keep loading memory while stopping automatic saves, change the [automatic memory setting](/oss/deepagents/code/memory-and-skills#automatic-memory): — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#automatic-memory
- [definition] Conversation history retention — Offloading a thread with `/offload` writes a markdown archive under `~/.deepagents/conversation_history/`. A startup sweep deletes archives older than 30 days. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#conversation-history-retention
- [definition] Compact on resume — Resuming a thread restores its full context, so the next turn pays for it. When a resumed thread's context exceeds a threshold, Deep Agents Code offers to compact it before your next message; declining is free and `/compact` (or `/offload`) remains available. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#compact-on-resume
- [definition] Uninstall — To remove the `dcode` and `deepagents-code` binaries and the isolated tool environment, run: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#uninstall
- [definition] Managed configuration — Managed configuration lets administrators control Deep Agents Code settings across a fleet. Deep Agents Code checks the administrator-owned `managed_config.toml` before user environment variables and config, so users cannot override settings defined there. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#managed-configuration
- [definition] Locate the managed config file — Deep Agents Code looks for `managed_config.toml` in a fixed location on each operating system: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#locate-the-managed-config-file
- [definition] Create a managed policy — Use the same TOML sections and keys as `~/.deepagents/config.toml`. Run `dcode config --verbose --json` to see the available settings, their accepted types, and whether they can be set in a config file. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#create-a-managed-policy
- [definition] Restrict model use — Set `[models].allowed` to exact, case-sensitive `provider:model` specifications, or use `provider:*` to allow all discoverable models from one provider. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#restrict-model-use
- [definition] Load policy remotely — You can store the policy on a central server while keeping its location in the local `managed_config.toml`: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#load-policy-remotely
- [definition] Validate a managed policy — Use the configuration and diagnostic commands after deploying or changing policy: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#validate-a-managed-policy
- [definition] Fix an invalid policy — Deep Agents Code stops rather than run without required administrator settings when it cannot read or parse the managed file, cannot download the complete remote policy, or cannot safely apply the policy. Commands that use configuration exit with code `78`. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#fix-an-invalid-policy
- [definition] Managed deployments — The [install script](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/main/libs/code/scripts/install.sh) supports running as root, targeting macOS MDM tools (Kandji, Jamf, etc.) that execute scripts in a minimal root environment. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#managed-deployments
- [definition] Pin the install with environment variables — The install script reads environment variables that let you pin a version, select extras, and choose a Python version fleet-wide. Set them on the same line as the piped install: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#pin-the-install-with-environment-variables
- [definition] Environment variable reference — All Deep Agents Code-specific environment variables use the `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_` prefix. See [`DEEPAGENTS_CODE_` prefix](#deepagents_code_-prefix) for how the prefix also works as an override for third-party credentials. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#environment-variable-reference
- [definition] Run diagnostics with `dcode doctor` — Use `dcode doctor` when Deep Agents Code is not starting correctly, a provider or MCP server does not connect, tracing is misconfigured, or an install or update looks wrong. It runs diagnostics without launching a session and summarizes the current runtime state. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#run-diagnostics-with-dcode-doctor
- [definition] Data locations — Deep Agents Code stores data in two directory hierarchies: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#data-locations
- [definition] Precedence rules — When the same item exists in multiple locations, **higher precedence wins completely** (no merging). — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#precedence-rules

- [parameter] `[env: VARNAME]`: The key comes from environment variable `VARNAME` (the resolved name, such as `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#use-auth-recommended
- [parameter] `[missing]`: No key is stored and the env var is unset; select the row to paste one — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#use-auth-recommended

- [parameter] `dcode auth set <provider>`: Store an API key, read from stdin by default — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#manage-credentials-from-the-shell-dcode-auth
- [parameter] `dcode auth remove <provider>` (aliases `rm`, `delete`): Delete a stored credential — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#manage-credentials-from-the-shell-dcode-auth
- [parameter] `dcode auth path`: Print the resolved path to the credential store (`auth.json`) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#manage-credentials-from-the-shell-dcode-auth
- [definition] Provider credentials — Deep Agents Code needs an API key for each model provider you use. The recommended way to add one is the [`/auth`](#use-%2Fauth-recommended) credential manager. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#provider-credentials
- [definition] Use `/auth` (recommended) — Open the credential manager from any session: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#use-auth-recommended
- [definition] Sign in with ChatGPT — Selecting the `openai_codex` provider in `/auth` starts a browser sign-in instead of prompting for an API key, letting you use OpenAI models with a ChatGPT subscription. To re-authenticate or sign out, select `openai_codex` again. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#sign-in-with-chatgpt
- [definition] Manage credentials from the shell (`dcode auth`) — The `dcode auth` command group is the scriptable equivalent of the `/auth` manager: it manages the same stored credentials without launching the TUI, which makes it usable for dotfile bootstrap, CI/CD, and setting a key on a remote box over SSH. The subcommands mirror the modal's verbs: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#manage-credentials-from-the-shell-dcode-auth
- [definition] Environment variables (CI and headless) — For non-interactive runs, CI/CD pipelines, or anywhere a TUI is not available, export the provider's env var in your shell: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#environment-variables-ci-and-headless
- [definition] Key resolution order — When a provider's key is set in more than one place, Deep Agents Code uses the first of these that is set: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#key-resolution-order
- [definition] Enable web search with Tavily — The built-in `web_search` tool uses [Tavily](https://tavily.com). Deep Agents Code shows a "Web search disabled" notification on startup until you provide a key. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#enable-web-search-with-tavily
- [definition] Get a key — Sign up at [tavily.com](https://tavily.com) and copy the key (it starts with `tvly-`). The free tier is sufficient for most Deep Agents Code usage. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#enable-web-search-with-tavily
- [definition] Add it to your environment — Add the key to `~/.deepagents/.env` so every session picks it up: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#enable-web-search-with-tavily
- [definition] Reload or restart — In an existing session, run `/reload` to re-read `.env` files. On the next launch, the "Web search disabled" notification goes away and the agent can call `web_search`. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/credentials#enable-web-search-with-tavily

- [definition] Python extensions — Python extensions customize the dcode agent server without modifying dcode itself. Use them to register model tools, LangChain middleware, virtual storage routes. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#python-extensions
- [definition] Create an extension — An extension entry file must expose an asynchronous `extension` setup function. dcode passes an `ExtensionAPI` registrar with read-only session context and methods for adding capabilities. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#create-an-extension
- [definition] Register capabilities — The extension API supports these methods: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#register-capabilities
- [definition] Register middleware — Register LangChain middleware to add model or tool behavior to the agent. dcode loads middleware when it builds the agent graph. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#register-middleware
- [definition] Register tools — Register a callable or `BaseTool` to make it available to the model. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#register-tools
- [definition] Route virtual storage — Backend route prefixes must be lowercase absolute paths with leading and trailing slashes, such as `/memories/` or `/company/knowledge/`. dcode rejects invalid paths and routes that overlap its internal artifact or conversation-history storage. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#route-virtual-storage
- [definition] Apply runtime changes — Tools registered after startup appear on the next model request. Middleware and backend routes change agent graph construction and require `/reload`. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#apply-runtime-changes
- [definition] Choose an extension source — dcode loads authorized extension sources in this order and ignores later duplicate entry paths: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#choose-an-extension-source
- [definition] Trust project extensions — Project extensions in `<project>/.deepagents/extensions/` execute only after project trust is granted. In interactive mode, dcode prompts you to allow the current files once, remember the canonical project path for future sessions and edits, or skip them. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#trust-project-extensions
- [definition] Configure extensions — Configure discovery in `~/.deepagents/config.toml`: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#configure-extensions
- [definition] Package an extension in a plugin — A versioned [plugin](/oss/deepagents/code/plugins) is the preferred way to distribute an extension. Declare one entry file or a list under the Deep Agents Code namespace in the plugin manifest: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#package-an-extension-in-a-plugin
- [definition] Handle failures — Each extension setup is transactional. If import or initialization fails, Deep Agents Code removes that extension's partial registrations, records the failure in the debug log and `/extensions`, and continues loading later extensions. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions#handle-failures

<https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/goals-and-rubrics>

- [snippet] Use a goal: /goal add OAuth refresh handling — `/goal add OAuth refresh handling` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/goals-and-rubrics#use-a-goal

- [snippet] Use a rubric: /rubric set tests pass; no unrelated files changed; help text is updated — `/rubric set tests pass; no unrelated files changed; help text is updated` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/goals-and-rubrics#use-a-rubric
- [snippet] Use rubrics in non-interactive mode: dcode -n "implement OAuth refresh handling" --rubric "tests pass; no unrelated files changed" — `dcode -n "implement OAuth refresh handling" --rubric "tests pass; no unrelated files changed"` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/goals-and-rubrics#use-a-rubric
- [snippet] Use rubrics in non-interactive mode: dcode -n "implement OAuth refresh handling" \ — `dcode -n "implement OAuth refresh handling" \` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/goals-and-rubrics#use-a-rubric
- [definition] Goals and rubrics — Goals and rubrics help Deep Agents Code check whether its work satisfies the criteria you care about. Use a goal for objective-driven work where the agent should help define acceptance criteria, and use a rubric when you already know the criteria. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/goals-and-rubrics#goals-and-rubrics
- [definition] Choose a goal or rubric — Use a **goal** when you have one measurable objective and want Deep Agents Code to draft acceptance criteria before it starts. A goal has a lifecycle: once accepted it stays active across turns until you pause it, the agent marks it completed or blocked, or you clear it. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/goals-and-rubrics#choose-a-goal-or-rubric
- [definition] Use a goal — Use `/goal` when you know the outcome you want, but want Deep Agents Code to propose the acceptance criteria before work begins. Goals are useful for open-ended work: the agent turns an objective into a concrete definition of done, then iterates until those criteria are satisfied. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/goals-and-rubrics#use-a-goal
- [definition] Amend, pause, and resume a goal — Steer an ongoing goal without cancelling the current task and replaying work: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/goals-and-rubrics#amend-pause-and-resume-a-goal
- [definition] Completion and grading — Each follow-up turn is graded against the goal's acceptance criteria until the work is done. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/goals-and-rubrics#completion-and-grading
- [definition] Use a rubric — Use `/rubric` when you already know the acceptance criteria and want them to act as a quality gate for the agent's work. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/goals-and-rubrics#use-a-rubric

- [parameter] `UserPromptSubmit.sessionTitle`: Parsed, not applied — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#unsupported-output-fields
- [parameter] `PreToolUse.updatedInput`: Mutation ignored; `allow` or `ask` uses the ordinary [PreToolUse](#control-tool-execution-with-pretooluse) decision — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#unsupported-output-fields
- [parameter] `PreToolUse.defer`: Uses the ordinary [PreToolUse](#control-tool-execution-with-pretooluse) decision; never treated as allow — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#unsupported-output-fields
- [parameter] `PostToolUse.updatedToolOutput`, `updatedMCPToolOutput`: Parsed, not applied — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#unsupported-output-fields
- [parameter] `PermissionRequest.updatedInput`: Mutation ignored; an `allow` uses the ordinary [PermissionRequest](#allow-or-deny-with-permissionrequest) decision — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#unsupported-output-fields
- [parameter] `PermissionRequest.updatedPermissions`: Parsed, not applied (no permission-rule store) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#unsupported-output-fields
- [parameter] `SubagentStop` block: [Context only](#inject-context); a completed subagent cannot be resumed — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#unsupported-output-fields
- [definition] Hooks — Hooks let external programs observe and control Deep Agents Code lifecycle events. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#hooks
- [definition] Setup — Create `~/.deepagents/hooks.json` for hooks that apply to every project, or `{project_root}/.deepagents/hooks.json` for project-scoped hooks (after you grant [workspace trust](#trust-project-hooks)). Handlers nest in three levels: event name, matcher group, then the handlers that run for that group. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#setup
- [definition] Trust project hooks — Project hooks come from the repository, so they load only after the workspace is trusted: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#trust-project-hooks
- [definition] Plugin hooks — An enabled plugin contributes the same configuration shape from `hooks/hooks.json`, a manifest `hooks` path, or an inline manifest object. Installing and enabling the plugin is the consent gate: workspace trust governs project hooks only, so it neither grants nor withholds a plugin's hooks. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#plugin-hooks
- [definition] Handler fields — Each entry in a matcher group's `hooks` array is a command handler: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#handler-fields
- [definition] Handler environment — A handler starts in the working directory reported as `cwd` in the payload and inherits the session environment with credential-looking variables removed: any name containing `KEY`, `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD`, or `APIKEY` is stripped before launch. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#handler-environment
- [definition] Matchers — A matcher filters whether a handler group runs for a given event. Each event matches against one field (see [Events](#events)): — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#matchers
- [definition] Events — Deep Agents Code emits the following events. Client-owned events run in the CLI process. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#events
- [definition] Input payload — Every handler receives a JSON object on stdin. All events share a common envelope, plus event-specific fields. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#input-payload
- [definition] Tool names — Hook scripts see stable public tool names and argument shapes, not internal Deep Agents Code tool names. Match on and read these names in `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, and `PermissionRequest`: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#tool-names
- [definition] Handler output — Command handlers communicate results through their exit code, stdout, and stderr. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#handler-output
- [definition] Universal output fields — Any handler may return these top-level fields: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#universal-output-fields
- [definition] Control tool execution with `PreToolUse` — Return a permission decision to allow, deny, or force a prompt before a tool runs: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#control-tool-execution-with-pretooluse
- [definition] Allow or deny with `PermissionRequest` — Return a decision to answer a permission prompt on the user's behalf: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#allow-or-deny-with-permissionrequest
- [definition] Continue a turn with `Stop` — Return a block decision to keep the agent working instead of ending the turn: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#continue-a-turn-with-stop
- [definition] Inject context — `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, and `SubagentStart` can add context for the model: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#inject-context
- [definition] Unsupported output fields — The following compatibility fields are recognized but not applied. Deep Agents Code emits a diagnostic and continues with the fallback in the Result column. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#unsupported-output-fields
- [definition] Troubleshoot hooks — Hook activity is visible in the session, not only in logs: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#troubleshoot-hooks
- [definition] Legacy configuration — Older list-shaped `hooks.json` files are deprecated but still supported. Deep Agents Code automatically migrates equivalent events; events without a safe mapping are skipped with a diagnostic. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#legacy-configuration
- [definition] Security — Hooks follow the same trust model as Git hooks or shell aliases: any process that can write to `hooks.json` can run arbitrary commands with your permissions. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks#security
