- [parameter] `--no-mcp`: Disable MCP entirely—no servers are loaded — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#flags
- [parameter] `ok`: Connected; tools are loaded and available to the agent — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#server-status
- [parameter] `unauthenticated`: OAuth login required or refresh failed — run `dcode mcp login <server>` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#server-status
- [parameter] `error`: Pre-flight, discovery, or transport setup failed; an error message is attached — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#server-status
- [parameter] `--trust-project-mcp`: Trust project-level servers without prompting for the current run. Servers denied by user policy remain disabled. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#flags
- [definition] MCP tools — [MCP (Model Context Protocol)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) lets you extend Deep Agents Code with tools from external servers—file systems, APIs, databases, and more—without modifying the agent itself. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#mcp-tools
- [definition] Quickstart — This quickstart adds the LangChain MCP servers to every Deep Agents Code session on your machine. We recommend adding `docs-langchain` for conceptual guides and how-tos, and `reference-langchain` for API reference. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#quickstart
- [definition] Create the config file — If it is not already present, create the `.mcp.json` file at the user level to make the server available to every project on the machine, or at the project level. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#quickstart
- [definition] Auto-discovery — Deep Agents Code automatically searches for `.mcp.json` files in standard locations. No flags are needed—just place a config file and it gets picked up. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#auto-discovery
- [definition] Discovery locations — Configs are checked in this order (lowest to highest precedence): — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#discovery-locations
- [definition] Claude Code compatibility — If you already have a `.mcp.json` at your project root for Claude Code, Deep Agents Code picks it up automatically—no extra setup needed. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#claude-code-compatibility
- [definition] Configuration format — Each key under `mcpServers` is a server name. The server's fields determine how Deep Agents Code connects to it. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#configuration-format
- [definition] stdio servers (default) — stdio servers are spawned as child processes. Deep Agents Code communicates with them over stdin/stdout. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#stdio-servers-default
- [definition] SSE and HTTP servers — For remote MCP servers, set `type` to `"sse"` or `"http"` and provide a `url`: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#sse-and-http-servers
- [definition] Environment variable interpolation — String values in `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, and `headers` support `${VAR}` references to parent-shell environment variables. Use `${VAR:-default}` to provide a value when the variable is unset or empty. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#environment-variable-interpolation
- [definition] Multiple servers — You can configure as many servers as you need. Tools from all servers are merged and available to the agent: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#multiple-servers
- [definition] Tool filtering — Each server may narrow the tools it exposes to the agent with one of two optional fields: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#tool-filtering
- [definition] Match rules — Each entry is a literal tool name or an [`fnmatch`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/fnmatch.html)-style glob (any entry containing `*`, `?`, or `[` is treated as a pattern). — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#match-rules
- [definition] Read-only tool annotations in Auto mode — MCP servers can attach standard `ToolAnnotations` when advertising a tool. Deep Agents Code lets a tool bypass classifier review in [Auto approval mode](/oss/deepagents/code/approval-modes) only when all of the following are true: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#read-only-tool-annotations-in-auto-mode
- [definition] OAuth login — For remote MCP servers that require OAuth (Slack, GitHub, Notion, Linear, and other hosted MCP endpoints), set `"auth": "oauth"` on the server entry and run the login subcommand once. Tokens are persisted to disk and refreshed automatically. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#oauth-login
- [definition] Run the login flow — List configured OAuth servers without stored credentials: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#run-the-login-flow
- [definition] Re-authentication — When refresh fails at runtime (the refresh token expired or was revoked), Deep Agents Code marks the server as `unauthenticated` instead of crashing the agent. The welcome banner shows the count of unauthenticated servers, and `/mcp` reports the reason per server. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#re-authentication
- [definition] Server status — Each configured server lands in one of three states after startup: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#server-status
- [definition] Project-level trust — Project-level configs can contain stdio servers that execute local commands and remote servers whose `headers` may interpolate `${VAR}` from your environment. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#project-level-trust
- [definition] Saved approvals — Saved approvals are stored in `~/.deepagents/config.toml`: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#saved-approvals
- [definition] Advanced allow and deny policy — Use `[mcp].disabled_project_servers` in `~/.deepagents/config.toml`, or `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_DISABLED_PROJECT_MCP_SERVERS` in your shell or global `~/.deepagents/.env`, to always reject project MCP servers by name. Denies win over saved approvals and over the `--trust-project-mcp` flag. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#advanced-allow-and-deny-policy
- [definition] System prompt awareness — Connected MCP servers and their tools are automatically listed in the agent's system prompt, grouped by server name and transport type. This helps the model reason about tool provenance and failure domains without requiring manual context. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools#system-prompt-awareness

- [definition] Add skills — Organize each skill as a directory containing `SKILL.md`: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/plugins#add-skills
- [definition] Add MCP servers — Place standard MCP server definitions in `.mcp.json` or declare them inline with `mcpServers` in the plugin manifest. MCP servers and hook commands support these path variables: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/plugins#add-mcp-servers
- [definition] Add hooks — Place a hook document at `hooks/hooks.json`, declare a relative `hooks` path, or define hooks inline in the plugin manifest. Hook commands receive the path variables above. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/plugins#add-hooks
- [definition] Add Python extensions — Python extensions require `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL=1`. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/plugins#add-python-extensions
- [definition] Create a marketplace — A marketplace is a JSON catalog with a name and a `plugins` array. Store it at one of these paths in the marketplace root: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/plugins#create-a-marketplace

- [definition] Inspect context-window usage — Run `/context` to open a color-coded report of the current model's context-window usage. - [parameter] `--sandbox TYPE`: Sandbox provider to use. Built-ins: `langsmith`, `agentcore`, `daytona`, `modal`, `runloop`, `vercel` (default: `none`). [Third-party](#third-party-providers) and [config-declared](#config-declared-providers) providers are also accepted. Pass `--sandbox` with no value to use `[sandboxes].default` from your config — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#sandbox-flags-and-examples
- [parameter] `--sandbox-id ID`: Reuse an existing sandbox by ID instead of creating a new one. Skips creation and cleanup. Only for providers that support reattaching by ID. Refer to your sandbox documentation for more — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#sandbox-flags-and-examples
- [parameter] `--sandbox-snapshot-name NAME`: Use or create a sandbox snapshot. Supported by `langsmith` and `runloop` (and any third-party provider that advertises snapshot support). Cannot be combined with `--sandbox-id` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#sandbox-flags-and-examples
- [parameter] `--sandbox-setup PATH`: Path to a setup script to run inside the sandbox upon creation — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#sandbox-flags-and-examples
- [parameter] LangSmith: `/root` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#sandbox-flags-and-examples
- [parameter] AgentCore: `/tmp` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#sandbox-flags-and-examples
- [parameter] Daytona: `/home/daytona` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#sandbox-flags-and-examples
- [parameter] Modal: `/workspace` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#sandbox-flags-and-examples
- [parameter] Runloop: `/home/user` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#sandbox-flags-and-examples
- [parameter] Vercel: `/vercel/sandbox` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#sandbox-flags-and-examples
- [parameter] E2B: `/home/user` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#sandbox-flags-and-examples
- [definition] Use remote sandboxes — Deep Agents Code uses the [sandbox as tool](/oss/python/deepagents/sandboxes#sandbox-as-tool-pattern) pattern: the `dcode` process (LLM loop, memory, tool dispatch) runs on your machine, but agent tool calls (`read_file`, `write_file`, `execute`, etc.) target the remote sandbox, not your local… — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#use-remote-sandboxes
- [definition] Install provider dependency — Each built-in provider ships as an optional extra. Install one from within a session with `/install`, or from the shell with `dcode --install`. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#use-remote-sandboxes
- [definition] Pluggable providers — The built-in providers are not the only options. Deep Agents Code discovers sandbox providers from three sources, so you can use providers shipped by other packages or declare your own without changing Deep Agents Code: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#pluggable-providers
- [definition] Third-party providers — A package can publish a sandbox provider under the `deepagents_code.sandbox_providers` [entry-point group](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/entry-points/). Once you install such a package, its provider is available to `--sandbox` automatically—no config needed: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#third-party-providers
- [definition] Config-declared providers — For an in-house or local provider you do not want to package, declare it under `[sandboxes.providers]` in `~/.deepagents/config.toml`. This parallels [arbitrary model providers](/oss/deepagents/code/config-file#arbitrary-providers) and uses the same `class_path` trust model. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#config-declared-providers
- [definition] Setup scripts — Use `--sandbox-setup` to run a shell script inside the sandbox after creation. This is useful for cloning repos, installing dependencies, and configuring environment variables. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/remote-sandboxes#setup-scripts

- [parameter] GitHub Actions: Example=[`openwiki-update.yml`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/openwiki/blob/main/examples/openwiki-update.yml); Destination=`.github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/automate-updates#add-a-workflow
- [parameter] GitLab CI: Example=[`openwiki-update.gitlab-ci.yml`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/openwiki/blob/main/examples/openwiki-update.gitlab-ci.yml); Destination=`.gitlab-ci.yml`, or include it from an existing pipeline — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/automate-updates#add-a-workflow
- [parameter] Bitbucket Pipelines: Example=[`openwiki-update.bitbucket-pipelines.yml`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/openwiki/blob/main/examples/openwiki-update.bitbucket-pipelines.yml); Destination=`bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, then schedule the `openwiki-update` custom pipeline — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/automate-updates#add-a-workflow
- [definition] Automate updates — OpenWiki can refresh repository documentation on a schedule and open a pull request or merge request when the wiki changes. Example workflows ship in the [OpenWiki repository](https://github.com/langchain-ai/openwiki/tree/main/examples). — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/automate-updates#automate-updates
- [definition] Run update in CI — For repository documentation in CI, use: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/automate-updates#run-update-in-ci
- [definition] Empty updates — OpenWiki automatically tracks wiki content in `openwiki/.last-update.json` and only rewrites that file when the wiki actually changed. If a scheduled `--update` run does not result in changes, the wiki files stay the same, and the CI does not open a pull request. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/automate-updates#empty-updates
- [definition] Telemetry in CI — Scheduled and CI runs send anonymous reliability telemetry under a shared CI identifier. To disable telemetry in CI, set: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/automate-updates#telemetry-in-ci

## Command reference
<https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference>

- [snippet] Core commands: openwiki — `# Interactive chat in code mode (current repository)` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#core-commands
- [snippet] Visualize: openwiki visualize — `openwiki visualize` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#visualize
- [snippet] Auth and connectors: openwiki auth — `# List supported auth providers and status` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#auth-and-connectors
- [snippet] Cron (macOS): openwiki cron list — `openwiki cron list` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#cron-macos
- [parameter] `--init`: Generate initial documentation. Defaults to code mode. In a TTY without `--print`, streams agent output and exits automatically on success. `--init` and `--update` cannot be combined. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#common-flags
- [parameter] `--update`: Update existing documentation. Defaults to code mode. In a TTY without `--print`, streams agent output and exits automatically on success. `--init` and `--update` cannot be combined. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#common-flags
- [parameter] `--mode <personal\|code>`: Choose personal brain or repository docs. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#common-flags
- [parameter] `-p`, `--print`: Run once, print the final assistant output, and exit. Provide a message or command. Interactive chat without `--print` stays open for follow-ups. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#common-flags
- [parameter] `--modelId` / `--model-id`: Choose a model ID for the run. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#common-flags
- [parameter] `--telemetry-file=<path>`: Also write the telemetry payload for the run to a local JSON file. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#common-flags
- [parameter] `-h`, `--help`: Print usage. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#common-flags
- [definition] Command reference — OpenWiki ships as a single `openwiki` binary for interactive chat and one-shot documentation runs. For installation and first use, see [Quickstart](/oss/openwiki/quickstart). — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#command-reference
- [definition] Visualize — You can visualize the generated wiki as an interactive node graph and live Markdown reader. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#visualize
- [definition] Cron (macOS) — Manage optional connector schedules for [personal mode](/oss/openwiki/personal-mode) sources. On macOS, OpenWiki can install schedules as user LaunchAgents that periodically refresh a source (for example Gmail or web search). — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#cron-macos
- [definition] Slash commands (interactive) — In interactive chat mode, you can use the following commands: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/cli-reference#slash-commands-interactive

## Code mode
<https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/code-mode>

- [snippet] Code mode: openwiki code --init — `openwiki code --init` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/code-mode#code-mode
- [snippet] Ignore paths: secrets/ — `secrets/` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/code-mode#ignore-paths
- [snippet] Diagrams: npm install mermaid jsdom — `npm install mermaid jsdom` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/code-mode#diagrams
- [snippet] Customize the wiki brief: openwiki "Update openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md to prioritize the public API and skip internal tooling" — `openwiki "Update openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md to prioritize the public API and skip internal tooling"` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/code-mode#customize-the-wiki-brief
- [definition] Code mode — Code mode builds a repository wiki in `openwiki/` with durable details such as architecture, integrations, and workflows. Coding agents use that wiki as context so they can work in the package more efficiently, with less rediscovery and fewer tokens. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/code-mode#code-mode
- [definition] What code mode produces — After a successful init or update, the repository typically includes: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/code-mode#what-code-mode-produces
- [definition] Markdown output — OpenWiki's durable output is Markdown (OKF), not a static HTML site. To explore the wiki in a browser, run [`openwiki visualize`](/oss/openwiki/visualize). — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/code-mode#markdown-output
- [definition] Open Knowledge Format — OpenWiki emits [Google Open Knowledge Format (OKF)](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/how-the-open-knowledge-format-can-improve-data-sharing) v0.1 bundles in both code and personal modes: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/code-mode#open-knowledge-format
- [definition] Ignore paths — Create a `.openwikiignore` file in the repository root to keep generated docs from reading or describing private, generated, or irrelevant paths. The syntax supports comments, blank lines, `*` and `**` globs, directory rules, and `!` negation: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/code-mode#ignore-paths
- [definition] Diagrams — OpenWiki embeds Mermaid diagrams where they clarify a concept better than prose. After each run, it validates Mermaid fences. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/code-mode#diagrams
- [definition] Customize the wiki brief — Edit `openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md` to steer scope, priorities, and preferred writing conventions for repository documentation (for example tone, terminology, and what to emphasize or skip). OpenWiki reads this file on init and update runs. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/code-mode#customize-the-wiki-brief

- [parameter] `x`: Credentials=OAuth user-context credentials; Behavior=Home timeline, user posts, mentions, bookmarks, and list posts via the X API — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#built-in-sources
- [parameter] `notion`: Credentials=Notion OAuth (hosted MCP); Behavior=Authenticate through Notion OAuth instead of pasting a Notion token — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#built-in-sources
- [parameter] `google`: Credentials=Gmail OAuth; Behavior=Fetches recent mail via the Gmail API after `openwiki auth gmail` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#built-in-sources
- [parameter] `web-search`: Credentials=`TAVILY_API_KEY`; Behavior=Uses Tavily through LangChain — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#built-in-sources
- [parameter] `hackernews`: Credentials=None; Behavior=Public Hacker News feed and search APIs — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#built-in-sources
- [parameter] `slack`: Credentials=Slack app client credentials + OAuth; Behavior=Requires HTTPS callback setup for OAuth; see [Slack OAuth](#slack-oauth) — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#built-in-sources
- [definition] Personal mode — Personal mode builds a local personal brain wiki in `~/.openwiki/wiki` from configured sources such as local repositories, Gmail, Notion, web search, Hacker News, Slack, and X/Twitter. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#personal-mode
- [definition] Connect your sources — In personal mode, OpenWiki ingests knowledge from the tools you already use and synthesizes it into your local wiki under `~/.openwiki/wiki/`. First-run onboarding can set up local git repositories, Notion, Gmail, X/Twitter, web search, Hacker News, and Slack. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#connect-your-sources
- [definition] Connect a source — For sources that need credentials, authenticate first, then ingest. Sources such as Hacker News need no auth; web search needs `TAVILY_API_KEY` in `~/.openwiki/.env`. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#connect-a-source
- [definition] Authenticate the provider — Run a local browser OAuth flow for providers that require it. OpenWiki saves returned tokens to `~/.openwiki/.env`, creates connector config when possible, and discovers MCP tools for MCP-backed providers: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#connect-a-source
- [definition] Ingest the source — Pull raw data into `~/.openwiki/connectors/` and synthesize updates into the personal wiki: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#connect-a-source
- [definition] Slack OAuth — Slack OAuth can require an HTTPS redirect URL: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#slack-oauth
- [definition] Manage schedules — On macOS, manage the connector schedules with: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/personal-mode#manage-schedules

## Quickstart
<https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart>

- [snippet] Install the CLI: npm install -g openwiki — `npm install -g openwiki` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#install-and-generate-repository-docs
- [snippet] Initialize in your repository: openwiki --init — `openwiki --init` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#install-and-generate-repository-docs
- [snippet] Review the generated wiki: openwiki visualize — `openwiki visualize` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#install-and-generate-repository-docs
- [snippet] Keep docs up to date: openwiki --update — `openwiki --update` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#install-and-generate-repository-docs
- [snippet] Personal wiki (optional): openwiki personal --init — `openwiki personal --init` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#personal-wiki-optional
- [snippet] Interactive and one-shot runs: openwiki "Please generate documentation for this repository" — `openwiki "Please generate documentation for this repository"` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#interactive-and-one-shot-runs
- [snippet] Interactive and one-shot runs: openwiki -p "Summarize what you can do" — `openwiki -p "Summarize what you can do"` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#interactive-and-one-shot-runs
- [snippet] Trace with LangSmith: LANGSMITH_API_KEY=your-key — `LANGSMITH_API_KEY=your-key` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#trace-with-langsmith
- [definition] Quickstart — OpenWiki is a CLI that writes and maintains a Markdown wiki for your codebase or personal knowledge. Coding agents use that wiki as durable context, so they spend less time and fewer tokens rediscovering architecture, integrations, and other repository details. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#quickstart
- [definition] Initialize in your repository — From the repository root, run the following command: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#install-and-generate-repository-docs
- [definition] Review the generated wiki — OpenWiki writes documentation to `openwiki/` in the repository, including a quickstart entrypoint and topic pages. It also maintains an `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` at the repository root, adding a block that instructs coding agents to consult the wiki for codebase context. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#install-and-generate-repository-docs
- [definition] Keep docs up to date — Refresh documentation after code changes: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#install-and-generate-repository-docs
- [definition] Personal wiki (optional) — To initialize a local personal brain instead of repository docs: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#personal-wiki-optional
- [definition] Interactive and one-shot runs — Bare `openwiki` opens an interactive session in code mode for the current repository. Pass a message to start with a request: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#interactive-and-one-shot-runs
- [definition] Trace with LangSmith — During onboarding, provide a LangSmith API key to trace OpenWiki runs to a LangSmith project named `openwiki`. You can also set these values in `~/.openwiki/.env` or the process environment: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart#trace-with-langsmith

## Visualize your wiki
<https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/visualize>

- [snippet] Open the visualizer: openwiki visualize — `openwiki visualize` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/visualize#open-the-visualizer
- [snippet] Options: openwiki visualize openwiki --port 4400 --no-open — `openwiki visualize openwiki --port 4400 --no-open` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/visualize#options
- [snippet] Options: openwiki visualize ~/.openwiki/wiki — `openwiki visualize ~/.openwiki/wiki` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/visualize#options
- [parameter] `[path]`: Wiki directory to serve. Defaults to `./openwiki` — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/visualize#options
- [parameter] `--port <port>`: Preferred port. Defaults to `4321`. Increments if the port is already in use — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/visualize#options
- [parameter] `--no-open`: Do not open the browser automatically — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/visualize#options
- [definition] Visualize your wiki — For exploring OpenWiki Markdown wikis, `openwiki visualize` serves a local interactive node graph beside a live Markdown reader in your browser. — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/visualize#visualize-your-wiki
- [definition] Open the visualizer — From a repository that already has an `openwiki/` directory: — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/visualize#open-the-visualizer
